knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A semilinear set is a finite union of base-plus-period monoids; finite counting measures its distinct points inside a specified finite window.
knowledge_statements.title: Semilinear-Set Counting

children.title: Presburger-Definable Counting
children.top_down_role: Counting sets presented through Presburger descriptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Presburger-Definable Counting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-fiber counting for parameterized Presburger formulas over the integers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varphi(p,x)\) be a Presburger formula, where \(p\in\mathbb Z^k\) is a parameter tuple and \(x\in\mathbb Z^d\) is counted. If every fiber \(S_p=\{x\in\mathbb Z^d:\varphi(p,x)\}\) is finite, its Presburger-definable counting function is \[g(p)=\#S_p=\#\{x\in\mathbb Z^d:\varphi(p,x)\}.\] If some fibers are infinite, the extended counting function may instead take values in \(\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}\); a finite-valued counting problem must explicitly restrict its parameter domain to fibers of finite cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Presburger counting function records the number of integer tuples satisfying a parameterized Presburger formula, with finite-valued problems restricted to parameters having finite fibers.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi\) uses integer addition, order, constants, Boolean operations, and first-order quantifiers.
Each counted fiber is finite on the stated parameter domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(p)=\#\{x\in\mathbb Z^d:\varphi(p,x)\}\in\mathbb N\).

notation.meaning: fiber defined by the formula at parameter p

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent, explicitly restricts finite-valued counting to finite fibers, and fits the Presburger-Definable Counting leaf. However, it has no citation or inspectable locator, and the local inventory contains no source supporting parameterized Presburger counting.

children.title: Representation Translation
children.top_down_role: Passage between logical descriptions and semilinear representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation Translation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effective equivalence between Presburger descriptions and semilinear representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A set \(S\subseteq\mathbb Z^d\) is Presburger-definable if and only if it is semilinear: there exist finitely many base vectors \(a_i\in\mathbb Z^d\) and period vectors \(b_{ij}\in\mathbb Z^d\) such that \[S=\bigcup_{i=1}^r\left\{a_i+\sum_{j=1}^{m_i}\lambda_jb_{ij}:\lambda_j\in\mathbb N\right\}.\] Both directions are effective. A semilinear representation yields a Presburger formula by existentially quantifying the coefficients; quantifier elimination and congruence decomposition yield a finite semilinear representation from a Presburger formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integer sets described by Presburger formulas are exactly finite unions of linear sets, and either representation can be effectively translated into the other.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb Z^d\).
Presburger arithmetic is interpreted over \((\mathbb Z,+,<,0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\text{ is Presburger-definable}\iff S\text{ is semilinear}\).

notation.meaning: base vector of a linear component

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation statement matches the leaf and states the standard effective correspondence between Presburger-definable and semilinear subsets of integer space. The equivalence and both effective translation claims are nontrivial and require an authoritative source with a specific theorem or section locator; none is supplied.

children.title: Quantifier-Complexity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Counting behavior across fixed or variable quantifier structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Quantifier-Complexity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Syntactic hierarchy by quantifier blocks in prenex Presburger formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Put a Presburger formula into prenex form with a quantifier-free matrix built from linear inequalities and congruences. The class \(\Sigma_k^{\mathrm{PA}}\) consists of formulas having at most \(k\) alternating nonempty quantifier blocks, beginning with an existential block; \(\Pi_k^{\mathrm{PA}}\) is defined analogously with a universal first block. Quantifier-free formulas form \(\Delta_0^{\mathrm{PA}}\). A counting family belongs to a regime when its defining fiber formula belongs to that class, with the number of variables, number of blocks, and coefficient encoding recorded separately because they affect algorithmic complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presburger counting regimes are classified by quantifier-block count and leading quantifier, while dimension and coefficient encoding remain separate complexity parameters.
assumptions_latex: Formulas are written in prenex form.
The quantifier-free matrix uses linear inequalities and congruences over \(\mathbb Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_0^{\mathrm{PA}},\Sigma_k^{\mathrm{PA}},\Pi_k^{\mathrm{PA}}\) specify distinct syntactic quantifier regimes.

notation.meaning: at most k alternating blocks beginning existentially
at most k alternating blocks beginning universally

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Quantifier-Complexity Regimes leaf and appropriately separates quantifier structure from dimension and encoding parameters. Because notation such as Sigma_k, Pi_k, block counting, and Delta_0 varies by convention, a source with a precise locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Lattice-Point Counting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted sums over lattice points of a bounded rational polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be a bounded rational polytope and let \(w:\mathbb Z^d\to R\) take values in a commutative ring \(R\). The weighted lattice-point count is \[W(P,w)=\sum_{m\in P\cap\mathbb Z^d}w(m).\] Its multivariate weighted generating polynomial is \[F_{P,w}(z)=\sum_{m\in P\cap\mathbb Z^d}w(m)z^m,\qquad z^m=\prod_{i=1}^dz_i^{m_i}.\] The unweighted count is recovered from \(w\equiv1\), equivalently as \(F_{P,1}(1,\ldots,1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted counting sums a prescribed weight over the lattice points of a bounded rational polytope; constant unit weight recovers ordinary counting.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a bounded rational polytope.
\(w:\mathbb Z^d\to R\), where \(R\) is a commutative ring.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W(P,w)=\sum_{m\in P\cap\mathbb Z^d}w(m)\) is a finite sum.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite weighted sum and generating polynomial are consistent for a bounded rational polytope, and definition is the correct content kind for this topic. No source or inspectable locator supports the definition or generating-function convention.

children.title: Polyhedral Valuation Localization Calculus
children.top_down_role: Valuation identities and cone-local representations underlying symbolic counting.

children.title: Indicator-Function Algebra
children.top_down_role: Algebraic manipulation of polyhedral indicator representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Indicator-Function Algebra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise algebraic identities for indicators of polyhedral sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For sets \(P,Q\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), their indicator functions satisfy \[\mathbf1_{P\cup Q}+\mathbf1_{P\cap Q}=\mathbf1_P+\mathbf1_Q.\] More generally, for finitely many sets \(P_1,\ldots,P_r\), \[\mathbf1_{\bigcup_{i=1}^rP_i}=\sum_{\varnothing\ne I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}}(-1)^{|I|+1}\mathbf1_{\bigcap_{i\in I}P_i}.\] These are pointwise identities. Consequently, formal signed polyhedral decompositions may be manipulated in the vector space generated by polyhedral indicators modulo pointwise equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Indicators obey union–intersection and inclusion–exclusion identities, allowing signed polyhedral decompositions to be treated algebraically.
assumptions_latex: \(P_1,\ldots,P_r\subseteq\mathbb R^d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed indicator identities hold at every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\).

notation.meaning: nonempty subset of the index set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pointwise union-intersection and finite inclusion-exclusion identities are correct and fit Indicator-Function Algebra as a property. The passage to signed polyhedral decompositions is also appropriate, but no supporting citation with a specific locator is present.

children.title: Polyhedral Valuations
children.top_down_role: Valuation-based treatment of polyhedral decompositions.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Valuations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive maps on polyhedra under union and intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P_d\) be a class of polyhedra in \(\mathbb R^d\), closed under intersection and under unions that remain polyhedral, and let \(A\) be an abelian group. A polyhedral valuation is a map \(V:\mathcal P_d\to A\) satisfying \(V(\varnothing)=0\) and \[V(P\cup Q)+V(P\cap Q)=V(P)+V(Q)\] whenever \(P,Q,P\cup Q\in\mathcal P_d\). Equivalently, \(V\) extends linearly to the group generated by polyhedral indicator functions modulo their pointwise relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral valuation is an additive invariant satisfying the union–intersection identity and vanishing on the empty set.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P_d\) has the stated closure properties.
\(A\) is an abelian group.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(P\cup Q)+V(P\cap Q)=V(P)+V(Q)\).

notation.meaning: chosen class of polyhedra in d-dimensional space

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record gives an appropriate definition of a polyhedral valuation and correctly identifies its indicator-group formulation. These conventions and the asserted equivalence require a cited source with an inspectable definition or theorem locator.

children.title: Valuation-Compatible Relations
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral relations preserved under relevant valuation maps.

knowledge_statements.title: Valuation-Compatible Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of pointwise indicator relations through a linear valuation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a polyhedral valuation \(V\) extends linearly to the group generated by indicators of polyhedra. For polyhedra \(P_1,\ldots,P_r\) and integers \(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r\), every pointwise relation \[\sum_{i=1}^r\alpha_i\mathbf1_{P_i}=0\] induces the valuation relation \[\sum_{i=1}^r\alpha_iV(P_i)=0.\] Thus two signed polyhedral decompositions having the same indicator function have the same value under \(V\); no disjointness assumption is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any linear relation among polyhedral indicators remains valid after applying a valuation, so equivalent signed decompositions have equal values.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) has a linear extension to the polyhedral indicator group.
\(\alpha_i\in\mathbb Z\) and \(P_i\) lie in the valuation domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i\alpha_i\mathbf1_{P_i}=0\implies\sum_i\alpha_iV(P_i)=0\).

notation.meaning: integer coefficient in an indicator relation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The implication is correct under the explicitly assumed linear extension and fits the Valuation-Compatible Relations leaf as a property. No source with a section, proposition, or page locator supports the indicator-group construction and transfer principle.

children.title: Lower-Dimensional Term Handling
children.top_down_role: Treatment of faces and lower-dimensional contributions in valuation identities.

knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Dimensional Term Handling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-dimensional pieces may vanish for volume but not for lattice enumeration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A lower-dimensional polyhedron may be discarded from a signed decomposition only when the chosen valuation annihilates it. In ambient dimension \(d\ge1\), the singleton \(P=\{0\}\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) satisfies \[\operatorname{vol}_d(P)=0,\qquad \#(P\cap\mathbb Z^d)=1,\qquad \sum_{m\in P\cap\mathbb Z^d}z^m=1.\] Hence equality modulo lower-dimensional indicator terms preserves full-dimensional volume but need not preserve lattice-point counts or lattice generating functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower-dimensional pieces can be ignored for volume, but even a singleton contributes to lattice counts and generating functions.
assumptions_latex: The ambient dimension satisfies \(d\ge1\).
The lattice is \(\mathbb Z^d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Vanishing under \(\operatorname{vol}_d\) does not imply vanishing under lattice enumeration.

notation.meaning: the singleton polyhedron containing the origin

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The singleton example correctly demonstrates that lower-dimensional terms vanish for ambient Lebesgue volume but not for lattice enumeration, and failure_boundary is the appropriate content kind. The valuation-specific warning lacks any cited source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Tangent Cones
children.top_down_role: Local cone representations attached to polyhedral points or faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Tangent Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-direction tangent cone along a face of a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be a polyhedron, let \(F\) be a nonempty face, and choose \(x\in\operatorname{relint}F\). The tangent cone of \(P\) along \(F\), expressed as a direction cone, is \[T_P(F)=\operatorname{cone}(P-x)=\{\lambda(y-x):\lambda\ge0,\ y\in P\}.\] It is independent of the chosen relative-interior point up to this direction representation, is a closed polyhedral cone, and contains the lineality space \(\operatorname{lin}(F-F)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tangent cone along a face consists of scaled feasible directions from any relative-interior point of that face.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a polyhedron.
\(F\) is a nonempty face and \(x\in\operatorname{relint}F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_P(F)=\operatorname{cone}(P-x)\) is a closed polyhedral cone.

notation.meaning: tangent direction cone of P along F

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The direction-cone definition, relative-interior convention, closedness, and face-direction lineality claim are coherent and fit the Tangent Cones leaf. A precise polyhedral-geometry source is required because tangent-cone conventions vary and none is cited.

children.title: Supporting Cones
children.top_down_role: Cone structures induced by supporting geometry at polyhedral faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Supporting Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal cone of objective vectors supporting a polyhedron at a face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be a polyhedron, let \(F\) be a nonempty face, and choose \(x\in\operatorname{relint}F\). The supporting cone, or normal cone, of \(P\) at \(F\) is \[N_P(F)=\{c\in\mathbb R^d:c^{\mathsf T}(y-x)\le0\text{ for every }y\in P\}.\] Equivalently, \(c\in N_P(F)\) exactly when every point of \(F\) maximizes \(c^{\mathsf T}y\) over \(P\). The vectors exposing exactly \(F\) lie in \(\operatorname{relint}N_P(F)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The supporting cone contains objective vectors whose maximum over the polyhedron is attained throughout the specified face.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a polyhedron.
\(F\) is a nonempty face and \(x\in\operatorname{relint}F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_P(F)=\{c:c^{\mathsf T}(y-x)\le0\ \forall y\in P\}\).

notation.meaning: supporting or normal cone at F

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: With the stated maximization sign convention, the normal-cone formula and face-exposure characterization are coherent and definition is the appropriate content kind. The term supporting cone and the relative-interior exposure assertion require a source with a specific locator.

children.title: Cone Correspondence at Faces
children.top_down_role: Relations between tangent and supporting constructions across face dimensions.

knowledge_statements.title: Cone Correspondence at Faces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polar duality and inclusion reversal for tangent and supporting cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) and a nonempty face \(F\), define the negative polar by \(K^\circ=\{c:c^{\mathsf T}u\le0\text{ for all }u\in K\}\). Then the tangent and supporting cones satisfy \[N_P(F)=T_P(F)^\circ,\qquad T_P(F)=N_P(F)^\circ.\] Moreover, if \(F\subseteq G\) are nonempty faces, then \[T_P(F)\subseteq T_P(G),\qquad N_P(G)\subseteq N_P(F).\] Thus passage from faces to normal cones reverses face inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tangent and supporting cones are negative polars, and larger faces have larger tangent cones but smaller normal cones.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a polyhedron.
\(F\) and \(G\) are nonempty faces of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_P(F)=T_P(F)^\circ\) and \(F\subseteq G\implies N_P(G)\subseteq N_P(F)\).

notation.meaning: supporting or normal cone at F

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The negative-polar convention is explicit, and the polarity and inclusion-reversal statements are consistent with the preceding tangent and normal cone definitions. Duality is the correct content kind, but the nontrivial correspondence has no cited theorem or section locator.

children.title: Nonpointed Cone Boundary
children.top_down_role: Representation issues arising from lines or nonpointed local geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonpointed Cone Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why cones containing lines require valuation rather than convergent-series interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be a rational polyhedral cone with nonzero lineality. Then some \(0\ne u\in\mathbb Z^d\) satisfies \(u,-u\in C\). Consequently, the bilateral subseries indexed by \(\{ku:k\in\mathbb Z\}\) prevents \(\sum_{m\in C\cap\mathbb Z^d}z^m\) from having a nonempty domain of absolute convergence: convergence would require both \(|z^u|<1\) and \(|z^u|>1\). In the standard rational generating-function valuation, cones containing lines are therefore assigned value \(0\), rather than interpreted by their divergent lattice series.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rational cone containing a line has no absolutely convergent lattice series; generating-function valuation conventionally assigns it zero.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a rational polyhedral cone.
\(C\) has nonzero lineality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{m\in C\cap\mathbb Z^d}z^m\) has no domain of absolute convergence, and its rational-function valuation is \(0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The absolute-convergence obstruction from an integral lineality direction is coherent, and failure_boundary correctly describes the role of the record. The assignment of zero to cones containing lines is a valuation convention that requires an authoritative generating-function source with a precise locator.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subset\mathbb R^d\) is a rational polytope.
For each vertex \(v\), \(C_v=v+\operatorname{cone}(P-v)\) is its tangent cone.
Generating functions are interpreted as rational functions after valuation extension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_P(\mathbf z)=\sum_{v\in\operatorname{vert}(P)}f_{C_v}(\mathbf z)\).

notation.meaning: Lattice-point generating function of a rational polyhedron or cone
Tangent cone of P at v

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rational-function form of Brion's theorem for lattice-point generating functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subset\mathbb R^d\) be a rational polytope and, for every \(v\in\operatorname{vert}(P)\), let \(C_v=v+\operatorname{cone}(P-v)\). The lattice-point enumerator \(f_Q(\mathbf z)=\sum_{m\in Q\cap\mathbb Z^d}\mathbf z^m\), initially defined where the series converges, extends by polyhedral valuation to a rational function whenever the recession cone is pointed; polyhedra containing lines have value zero. In the field \(\mathbb Q(z_1,\ldots,z_d)\), Brion localization gives \[f_P(\mathbf z)=\sum_{v\in\operatorname{vert}(P)}f_{C_v}(\mathbf z).\] Thus the global lattice-point generating function is assembled solely from vertex tangent-cone contributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Brion localization expresses a rational polytope's lattice-point generating function as the sum of the rational generating functions of its vertex tangent cones.
knowledge_statements.title: Brion Theorem Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Brion localization statement fits the leaf and is mathematically plausible, but no cited source supports the precise rational-function valuation, pointed-recession, or line-cone conventions.

children.title: Cone Polarization
children.top_down_role: Polarized cone representations used in symbolic decomposition.

assumptions_latex: \(C=v+\operatorname{cone}(u_1,\ldots,u_d)\) is a simplicial pointed cone.
\(\xi\in(\mathbb R^d)^*\) satisfies \(\langle\xi,u_i\rangle\ne0\) for every ray generator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C^\xi=v+\sum_i\mathbb R_{\ge0}u_i^\xi\) with sign \((-1)^{|I^-|}\), where negatively paired rays are reversed.

notation.meaning: Indices of rays negatively paired with the covector

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic-covector polarization of a simplicial cone; facet openness conventions are recorded separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=v+\operatorname{cone}(u_1,\ldots,u_d)\) be a simplicial pointed cone and choose \(\xi\in(\mathbb R^d)^*\) with \(\langle\xi,u_i\rangle\ne0\) for all \(i\). Define \(I^-=\{i:\langle\xi,u_i\rangle<0\}\) and \[u_i^\xi=\begin{cases}u_i,&i\notin I^-,\\-u_i,&i\in I^-.
\end{cases}\] The polarized cone is \(C^\xi=v+\sum_{i=1}^d\mathbb R_{\ge0}u_i^\xi\), equipped with orientation sign \(\varepsilon(C,\xi)=(-1)^{|I^-|}\). For indicator-function identities, facets corresponding to reversed rays must be made relatively open so that boundary lattice points are neither omitted nor multiply counted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generic covector polarizes a simplicial cone by reversing negatively paired rays and attaching the sign determined by the number of reversals.
knowledge_statements.title: Cone Polarization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits Cone Polarization, but the orientation and relatively open facet convention is convention-sensitive and has no inspectable source.

children.title: Local Cone Contributions
children.top_down_role: Vertex-level or face-level contributions to global counting representations.

assumptions_latex: \(v\in\mathbb Z^d\) and \(C_v=v+\operatorname{cone}(u_1,\ldots,u_k)\) is a pointed rational simplicial cone.
The primitive integral rays \(u_i\) are linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_{C_v}(\mathbf z)=\dfrac{\sum_{a\in\Pi\cap\mathbb Z^d}\mathbf z^{v+a}}{\prod_{i=1}^k(1-\mathbf z^{u_i})}\).

notation.meaning: Half-open fundamental parallelepiped of the ray lattice

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit local rational contribution for a pointed simplicial tangent cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v\in\mathbb Z^d\) and let \(C_v=v+\operatorname{cone}(u_1,\ldots,u_k)\), where the \(u_i\in\mathbb Z^d\) are primitive and linearly independent. For the half-open fundamental parallelepiped \(\Pi=\{\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i u_i:0\le\lambda_i<1\}\), every lattice point of \(C_v\) has a unique decomposition into a point of \(v+(\Pi\cap\mathbb Z^d)\) plus a nonnegative integral combination of the \(u_i\). Consequently, wherever the series converges and hence as a rational function, \[f_{C_v}(\mathbf z)=\frac{\sum_{a\in\Pi\cap\mathbb Z^d}\mathbf z^{v+a}}{\prod_{i=1}^k(1-\mathbf z^{u_i})}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simplicial tangent cone contributes a rational function whose numerator enumerates a fundamental parallelepiped and whose denominator records its primitive rays.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Cone Contributions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The simplicial-cone representation is precise and fits the leaf, but the candidate supplies no source for the unique decomposition and rational generating-function formula.

children.title: Polarization–Localization Interface
children.top_down_role: Interaction between polarized cones and localized contributions.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subset\mathbb R^d\) is a simple rational polytope.
\(\xi\) is nonzero on every edge direction of \(P\).
Half-open facets follow the reversed-ray convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_P(\mathbf z)=\sum_v(-1)^{|I_v^-|}f_{C_v^\xi}(\mathbf z)\).

notation.meaning: Polarized tangent cone at vertex v
Set of reversed edge directions at v

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polarized localization for simple rational polytopes under a generic covector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subset\mathbb R^d\) be a simple rational polytope. At each vertex \(v\), polarize the simplicial tangent cone by a covector \(\xi\) that is nonzero on every incident edge direction, reverse the rays indexed by \(I_v^-\), and impose the corresponding half-open facet convention. Applying the lattice-point generating-function valuation to the polarized indicator identity yields \[f_P(\mathbf z)=\sum_{v\in\operatorname{vert}(P)}(-1)^{|I_v^-|}f_{C_v^\xi}(\mathbf z).\] Although the individual polarized rational functions and their convergence chambers depend on \(\xi\), their signed sum is independent of \(\xi\) and equals the polytope generating function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polarized tangent-cone functions, signed by ray reversals, localize the polytope generating function; dependence on the generic covector cancels globally.
knowledge_statements.title: Polarization–Localization Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the interface leaf, but the signed half-open cone identity and covector-independence claim require a source specifying the same polarization convention.

children.title: Degeneracy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Behavior under non-simple, nonpointed, or otherwise degenerate cone geometry.

assumptions_latex: A proposed polarizing covector \(\xi\) may vanish on an edge direction.
A vertex cone may be nonsimplicial or may contain a line.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Direct simplicial polarization is undefined or incomplete unless generic perturbation, triangulation, or line-cone valuation rules are imposed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure modes of naive polarized-cone formulas and their required regularizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The direct polarization rule fails to determine a signed half-open cone when \(\langle\xi,u\rangle=0\) for some ray \(u\), because that ray has no prescribed orientation and boundary ownership is ambiguous. If \(C_v\) is nonsimplicial, a ray-by-ray product formula is likewise unavailable without a signed simplicial decomposition. If a cone contains a line, its lattice-point series has no nonempty ordinary domain of absolute convergence and is assigned zero only after valuation extension. Thus localization requires, respectively, a generic perturbation of \(\xi\), a compatible triangulation or subdivision, and an explicit line-cone valuation convention; omitting these choices makes local terms undefined even when the global identity has a regularized meaning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Non-generic covectors, nonsimplicial cones, and cones containing lines invalidate naive polarization unless perturbation, subdivision, and valuation conventions are supplied.
knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits Degeneracy Regimes, but the perturbation, subdivision, and line-cone valuation prescriptions are convention-dependent and uncited.

children.title: Short Rational Generating Functions
children.top_down_role: Compact symbolic representations and the operations supported on them.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Short Rational Generating Functions for Lattice Point Problems
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Journal of the American Mathematical Society 16, 2003
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Short Rational Generating Functions for Lattice Point Problems

children.title: Cone Generating Functions
children.top_down_role: Generating-function representations for lattice points in rational cones.

assumptions_latex: \(C=v+\operatorname{cone}(u_1,\ldots,u_k)\subset\mathbb R^d\) is rational and pointed.
\(v\in\mathbb Z^d\) and each \(u_i\in\mathbb Z^d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_C(\mathbf z)=\sum_{m\in C\cap\mathbb Z^d}\mathbf z^m\) is a rational function, with the displayed product form when the cone is unimodular simplicial.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rational-function representation for pointed rational cones, including the unimodular case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rational pointed cone \(C=v+\operatorname{cone}(u_1,\ldots,u_k)\) with integral apex and integral ray generators, define \(f_C(\mathbf z)=\sum_{m\in C\cap\mathbb Z^d}\mathbf z^m\) on any nonempty domain where this Laurent series converges. It extends uniquely to a rational function. If \(C\) is simplicial and unimodular, so its primitive rays extend to a lattice basis in their span, then \[f_C(\mathbf z)=\frac{\mathbf z^v}{\prod_{i=1}^k(1-\mathbf z^{u_i})}.\] For a general pointed rational cone, subdivision into simplicial cones and fundamental-parallelepiped numerators produces a finite signed sum of such rational terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lattice points of a pointed rational cone have a rational generating function; a unimodular simplicial cone has a single monomial-over-binomial-product form.
knowledge_statements.title: Cone Generating Functions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits Cone Generating Functions and distinguishes the unimodular case, but no source supports the rationality and signed-subdivision claims.

children.title: Polytope Generating Functions
children.top_down_role: Generating-function representations for lattice points in bounded polytopes.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subset\mathbb R^d\) is a rational polytope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_P(\mathbf z)=\sum_{m\in P\cap\mathbb Z^d}\mathbf z^m\) is a Laurent polynomial and \(f_P(\mathbf 1)=|P\cap\mathbb Z^d|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multivariate lattice-point enumerator of a bounded rational polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rational polytope \(P\subset\mathbb R^d\), its multivariate lattice-point generating function is \[f_P(\mathbf z)=\sum_{m\in P\cap\mathbb Z^d}\mathbf z^m,\qquad \mathbf z^m=\prod_{i=1}^dz_i^{m_i}.\] Since \(P\) is bounded, \(P\cap\mathbb Z^d\) is finite, so \(f_P\) is a Laurent polynomial and is defined for every \(\mathbf z\in(\mathbb C^*)^d\). Its support is exactly \(P\cap\mathbb Z^d\), every coefficient is one, and evaluation at \(\mathbf z=\mathbf 1\) gives \(f_P(\mathbf 1)=|P\cap\mathbb Z^d|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polytope generating function is the finite Laurent polynomial whose monomials encode exactly the polytope's lattice points.
knowledge_statements.title: Polytope Generating Functions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is standard, precise, and appropriate for the leaf, but the record contains no citation or standard-field rationale permitted by the evidence contract.

children.title: Cone-to-Polytope Assembly
children.top_down_role: Assembly of polytope representations from local cone contributions.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subset\mathbb R^d\) is a rational polytope.
\(C_v=v+\operatorname{cone}(P-v)\) denotes the tangent cone at each vertex.
Cone series are interpreted through their rational-function continuations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_P=\sum_v f_{C_v}\), with each cone term replaceable by a finite simplicial rational decomposition.

notation.meaning: Generating function of a polyhedron Q
Signed simplicial pieces of a tangent cone

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact assembly procedure from vertex cones to a polytope generating function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a rational polytope \(P\subset\mathbb R^d\). Enumerate its vertices \(v\), construct each tangent cone \(C_v=v+\operatorname{cone}(P-v)\), and decompose every nonsimplicial \(C_v\) into signed rational simplicial cones \(C_{v,j}\). Compute each \(f_{C_{v,j}}\) from its fundamental parallelepiped and ray denominators, then form \[F(\mathbf z)=\sum_{v\in\operatorname{vert}(P)}\sum_j\sigma_{v,j}f_{C_{v,j}}(\mathbf z),\qquad \sigma_{v,j}\in\{-1,1\}.\] Simplify in \(\mathbb Q(z_1,\ldots,z_d)\) and output \(F\). Brion localization guarantees \(F=f_P\); apparent poles at \(\mathbf z=\mathbf 1\) cancel globally before lattice-point counting by specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerate vertex cones, decompose them into signed simplicial pieces, compute their rational functions, and sum; Brion localization identifies the result with the polytope function.
knowledge_statements.title: Cone-to-Polytope Assembly

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Cone-to-Polytope Assembly, but Brion correctness, signed cone decomposition, and cancellation before specialization are unsupported by an inspectable source.

children.title: Unbounded Support Regimes
children.top_down_role: Representation behavior when cone support or polyhedral support is unbounded.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\subset\mathbb R^d\) is a rational polyhedron with recession cone \(K=\operatorname{rec}(Q)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ordinary convergence requires a pointed \(K\) and \(|\mathbf z^u|<1\) along every nonzero recession direction; lineality destroys such a domain.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Analytic and valuation boundaries for generating functions with unbounded lattice support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subset\mathbb R^d\) be rational and unbounded, with \(K=\operatorname{rec}(Q)\). If \(K\) is pointed, the formal series \(f_Q(\mathbf z)=\sum_{m\in Q\cap\mathbb Z^d}\mathbf z^m\) may converge absolutely only in chambers satisfying decay along every nonzero integral recession direction, equivalently \(|\mathbf z^u|<1\) for all \(u\in K\cap\mathbb Z^d\setminus\{0\}\). Its rational continuation can nevertheless be manipulated outside those chambers. If \(K\) contains a line generated by nonzero \(u\), convergence would require both \(|\mathbf z^u|<1\) and \(|\mathbf z^{-u}|<1\), which is impossible. Hence line-containing polyhedra require a formal valuation convention, commonly value zero, rather than an ordinary convergent series.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointed recession permits convergence in decay chambers; lineality makes ordinary convergence impossible and forces a formal valuation interpretation.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Support Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the claimed equivalence describing absolute-convergence chambers and the zero valuation for line-containing polyhedra need authoritative support.

children.title: Multigraded Generating Functions
children.top_down_role: Generating functions carrying multiple grading coordinates.

assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb Z^d\) and every fiber of \(A:S\to\mathbb Z^r\) used below is finite.
\(A\in\mathbb Z^{r\times d}\) is an integral grading map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_{S,A}(\mathbf t)=\sum_{m\in S}\mathbf t^{Am}=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb Z^r}|\{m\in S:Am=\alpha\}|\mathbf t^\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pushforward of a lattice-set enumerator through an integral multigrading.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb Z^d\) and let \(A\in\mathbb Z^{r\times d}\) define an integral multigrading \(m\mapsto Am\). Assuming each relevant fiber \(\{m\in S:Am=\alpha\}\) is finite, the multigraded generating function is \[H_{S,A}(\mathbf t)=\sum_{m\in S}\mathbf t^{Am}=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb Z^r}|\{m\in S:Am=\alpha\}|\mathbf t^\alpha.\] It is the monomial pushforward of the fine generating function \(f_S(\mathbf z)=\sum_{m\in S}\mathbf z^m\) under the substitution \(z_i=\prod_{j=1}^rt_j^{A_{ji}}\), whenever the substitution is valid formally or analytically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multigraded generating function groups lattice points by an integral vector-valued degree and records each fiber cardinality as a coefficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Multigraded Generating Functions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits Multigraded Generating Functions, but no source supports the fiber-finiteness formulation or the stated formal/analytic substitution condition.

children.title: Weighted Generating Functions
children.top_down_role: Generating functions whose lattice-point contributions carry weights.

assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb Z^d\).
\(w:S\to R\) takes values in a commutative coefficient ring \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_{S,w}(\mathbf z)=\sum_{m\in S}w(m)\mathbf z^m\), with coefficients equal to the prescribed lattice-point weights.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient-weighted lattice-point enumerator over a commutative ring.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb Z^d\), let \(R\) be a commutative ring, and let \(w:S\to R\). The weighted lattice-point generating function is \[F_{S,w}(\mathbf z)=\sum_{m\in S}w(m)\mathbf z^m.\] It is interpreted as a Laurent polynomial when \(S\) is finite, as a formal series when its support is admissible, or through rational continuation when such a representation exists. Its defining coefficient identity is \([\mathbf z^m]F_{S,w}=w(m)\) for \(m\in S\) and zero otherwise. The unweighted enumerator is recovered by taking \(w\equiv1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted generating function replaces each lattice-point coefficient one by a prescribed value in a commutative coefficient ring.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Generating Functions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits Weighted Generating Functions, but it is uncited and the phrase 'support is admissible' does not specify the formal-series setting.

children.title: Grading–Weight Interaction
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between multigraded representations and weight encodings.

knowledge_statements.title: Grading–Weight Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial degree weights obtained from Euler operators on a multigraded series.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb Z^{r\times d}\) grade \(S\subseteq\mathbb Z^d\), and write \(H_{S,A}(\mathbf t)=\sum_{m\in S}\mathbf t^{Am}\). For \(j=1,\ldots,r\), define the Euler operator \(\Theta_j=t_j\frac{\partial}{\partial t_j}\). Since \(\Theta_j\mathbf t^{Am}=(Am)_j\mathbf t^{Am}\), every polynomial \(p\in R[y_1,\ldots,y_r]\) satisfies \[p(\Theta_1,\ldots,\Theta_r)H_{S,A}(\mathbf t)=\sum_{m\in S}p(Am)\mathbf t^{Am}.\] Thus polynomial weights depending only on the multidegree are implemented by differential operators after grading; points in the same grading fiber necessarily receive the same weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Euler differentiation in grading variables converts a multigraded enumerator into a weighted enumerator for any polynomial function of the multidegree.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb Z^d\) has generating function \(f_S(\mathbf z)\).
\(A\in\mathbb Z^{r\times d}\) defines the multidegree \(Am\).
\(p\in R[y_1,\ldots,y_r]\) is a polynomial weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{m\in S}p(Am)\mathbf t^{Am}=p(\Theta_1,\ldots,\Theta_r)H_{S,A}(\mathbf t)\), where \(\Theta_j=t_j\partial/\partial t_j\).

notation.meaning: Euler operator in grading variable j

children.title: Encoding Complexity
children.top_down_role: Representation-size effects caused by grading dimension and weight descriptions.

assumptions_latex: The exponents and denominator directions are integer vectors, and all rational coefficients are written in lowest terms.
Each denominator direction is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The encoding length is the total binary length of all coefficients, exponent vectors, denominator directions, signs, and structural delimiters in the displayed representation.

notation.meaning: Binary encoding length of an integer or rational datum.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary length of an explicitly presented short rational generating function.

source_refs.locator: 1.3.1 Problems, Instances, Encoding Size p. 17

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an explicitly presented short rational function \(F(\mathbf{x})=\sum_{i=1}^{N}c_i\mathbf{x}^{\mathbf{a}_i}/\prod_{j=1}^{k_i}(1-\mathbf{x}^{\mathbf{b}_{ij}})\), define its encoding complexity by \[L(F)=\ell(N)+\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left(\ell(c_i)+\ell(\mathbf{a}_i)+\ell(k_i)+\sum_{j=1}^{k_i}\ell(\mathbf{b}_{ij})\right),\] up to a fixed self-delimiting coding convention. Vector lengths are sums of signed binary coordinate lengths. Thus polynomial-time bounds for manipulating \(F\) are measured in \(L(F)\), not in the generally much larger cardinality of the encoded lattice set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encoding complexity is the total binary length of the explicit rational-function data, including coefficients, exponents, denominator directions, and representation structure.
knowledge_statements.title: Encoding Complexity

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3.1 Problems, Instances, Encoding Size p. 17

children.title: Boolean Set Operations
children.top_down_role: Union, intersection, and difference at the represented-set level.

assumptions_latex: The sets \(S,T\subseteq U\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Union, intersection, difference, and relative complement are represented by the displayed arithmetic-Hadamard identities.

notation.meaning: Indicator generating function of a finite lattice set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite lattice sets with complement taken relative to a fixed finite universe.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_S\), \(f_T\), and \(f_U\) be the indicator generating functions of finite sets \(S,T\subseteq U\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d\). Because their coefficients lie in \(\{0,1\}\), the Boolean operations satisfy \[f_{S\cap T}=f_S*f_T,\qquad f_{S\cup T}=f_S+f_T-f_S*f_T,\] \[f_{S\setminus T}=f_S-f_S*f_T,\qquad f_{U\setminus S}=f_U-f_S.\] Every right-hand side again has coefficients in \(\{0,1\}\) and is exactly the indicator series of the stated set operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Indicator generating functions translate intersection to Hadamard product and express union, difference, and relative complement by arithmetic identities.
knowledge_statements.title: Boolean Set Operations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-set Boolean identities are mathematically precise and the representation kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable citation supports them.

children.title: Hadamard Products
children.top_down_role: Coefficientwise products used to combine generating-function supports.

assumptions_latex: The two Laurent series are indexed over \(\mathbb{Z}^d\), and coefficientwise products are defined in the coefficient ring.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coefficient of \(\mathbf{x}^{\mathbf{u}}\) in \(f*g\) is exactly \(a_{\mathbf{u}}b_{\mathbf{u}}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficientwise product of multivariate Laurent series.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For Laurent series \(f(\mathbf{x})=\sum_{\mathbf{u}\in\mathbb{Z}^d}a_{\mathbf{u}}\mathbf{x}^{\mathbf{u}}\) and \(g(\mathbf{x})=\sum_{\mathbf{u}\in\mathbb{Z}^d}b_{\mathbf{u}}\mathbf{x}^{\mathbf{u}}\), their Hadamard product is defined by \[ (f*g)(\mathbf{x})=\sum_{\mathbf{u}\in\mathbb{Z}^d}a_{\mathbf{u}}b_{\mathbf{u}}\mathbf{x}^{\mathbf{u}}. \] Unlike ordinary multiplication, no convolution of exponent vectors occurs. In particular, if \(f=f_S\) and \(g=f_T\) are indicator series, then \(f*g=f_{S\cap T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Hadamard product multiplies equal-index coefficients. For indicator series, it produces the generating function of the set intersection.
knowledge_statements.title: Hadamard Products

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coefficientwise definition and indicator-series consequence are correct and fit the leaf, but the record has no source or locator.

children.title: Set-Algebra Translation
children.top_down_role: Translation of set operations into generating-function operations.

assumptions_latex: All sets under consideration are finite subsets of a common finite universe \(U\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The indicator-series map translates Boolean set expressions into expressions formed from addition, subtraction, and Hadamard product.

notation.meaning: Indicator generating function of a set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive translation of finite Boolean set expressions into generating-function expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\Phi(S)=\sum_{\mathbf{u}\in S}\mathbf{x}^{\mathbf{u}}\) for \(S\subseteq U\). A Boolean expression in atomic sets can be translated recursively by replacing intersection with Hadamard product, union with \(p+q-p*q\), relative complement with \(\Phi(U)-p\), and difference with \(p-p*q\). Induction on the expression tree gives a series whose coefficient at every \(\mathbf{u}\in U\) equals the truth value of membership in the represented set. Hence the resulting series is \(\Phi(E)\) for the set expression \(E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Boolean expression on finite lattice sets can be recursively converted into an arithmetic-Hadamard expression whose coefficients are its membership truth values.
knowledge_statements.title: Set-Algebra Translation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recursive translation is correct for finite subsets of a common finite universe, and principle is an appropriate kind, but no supporting citation is supplied.

children.title: Representation-Size Growth
children.top_down_role: Expansion risks under repeated Boolean or coefficientwise operations.

assumptions_latex: The ambient dimension and the maximum number of binomials in each denominator term are fixed constants.
Input supports lie in a common bounded rational polytope, and each input is given by a short rational generating function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For a fixed Boolean expression, the output short rational representation has encoding length polynomial in the combined input length.

notation.meaning: Combined binary encoding length of all input representations.
Encoding length of the computed output representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-dimension size control for a fixed Boolean expression on bounded lattice sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix the ambient dimension, a bound on denominator length per rational term, and a Boolean expression with a fixed number of leaves. Given short rational generating functions of total encoding length \(L\) for the leaf sets, the expression can be evaluated using addition, subtraction, and Hadamard products so that \[L_{\mathrm{out}}\leq p(L)\] for a polynomial \(p\) depending only on the fixed dimension, denominator bound, and expression. If these parameters are allowed to grow with the input, this polynomial representation-size guarantee is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In fixed dimension and for a fixed Boolean expression, output representation size is polynomial in input size; the claim does not cover growing dimension or expression depth.
knowledge_statements.title: Representation-Size Growth

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This nontrivial polynomial representation-size claim requires an exact fixed-dimension theorem and computational-model locator. The supplied inventory contains no source establishing it.

children.title: Coordinate Projection
children.top_down_role: Elimination of coordinates from represented lattice-point sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued coordinate projection, which discards multiplicity from coincident images.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d\) be a positive integer and let \(I=\{i_1<\cdots<i_k\}\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\). The coordinate projection \(\pi_I:\mathbb{Z}^d\to\mathbb{Z}^k\) is defined by \(\pi_I(\mathbf{u})=(u_{i_1},\ldots,u_{i_k})\). For a finite set \(S\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d\), its projected set is \[\pi_I(S)=\{\pi_I(\mathbf{u}):\mathbf{u}\in S\},\] and its indicator generating function is \(f_{\pi_I(S)}(\mathbf{z})=\sum_{\mathbf{v}\in\pi_I(S)}\mathbf{z}^{\mathbf{v}}\). Distinct points of \(S\) having the same image contribute only one projected monomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate projection keeps the coordinates indexed by I in increasing order and treats coincident projected images as one set element.
assumptions_latex: \(d\) is a positive integer.
\(S\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d\) is finite.
\(I=\{i_1<\cdots<i_k\}\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coordinate projection is \(\pi_I(S)=\{(u_{i_1},\ldots,u_{i_k}):\mathbf{u}\in S\}\), with duplicate images retained only once.

notation.meaning: Coordinate projection onto the coordinates indexed by \(I\), listed in increasing order.
Indicator generating function of the projected set.

children.title: Monomial Substitution
children.top_down_role: Variable transformations induced by exponent mappings.

assumptions_latex: The set \(S\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d\) is finite.
The matrix \(A\in\mathbb{Z}^{k\times d}\) defines an integer linear map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Monomial substitution transforms \(f_S\) into \(\sum_{\mathbf{u}\in S}\mathbf{z}^{A\mathbf{u}}\), whose coefficients count fibers of \(A\) on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-support monomial substitution induced by an integer linear map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the columns of \(A\in\mathbb{Z}^{k\times d}\) be \(\mathbf{a}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{a}_d\). Applying the monomial substitution \(x_j\mapsto\mathbf{z}^{\mathbf{a}_j}\) to \(f_S(\mathbf{x})=\sum_{\mathbf{u}\in S}\mathbf{x}^{\mathbf{u}}\) gives \[f_S(\mathbf{z}^{\mathbf{a}_1},\ldots,\mathbf{z}^{\mathbf{a}_d})=\sum_{\mathbf{u}\in S}\mathbf{z}^{A\mathbf{u}}=\sum_{\mathbf{v}\in\mathbb{Z}^k}|S\cap A^{-1}(\mathbf{v})|\mathbf{z}^{\mathbf{v}}.\] Thus substitution records projected images with fiber multiplicity rather than automatically producing a set-indicator series.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substitution induced by an integer matrix sends each exponent to its linear image, with coefficients equal to image-fiber cardinalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Monomial Substitution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The substitution identity and fiber-multiplicity interpretation are correct for finite support and fit the representation leaf, but no citation or locator is provided.

children.title: Projection–Substitution Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Conditions linking geometric projection to monomial transformations.

assumptions_latex: The set \(S\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d\) is finite.
The integer linear map \(A:\mathbb{Z}^d\to\mathbb{Z}^k\) is injective on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under injectivity, \(f_{A(S)}(\mathbf{z})=f_S(\mathbf{z}^{\mathbf{a}_1},\ldots,\mathbf{z}^{\mathbf{a}_d})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correspondence in the collision-free finite-support regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{Z}^{k\times d}\) have columns \(\mathbf{a}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{a}_d\), and suppose \(A\) is injective on the finite set \(S\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d\). Then every fiber \(S\cap A^{-1}(\mathbf{v})\) has size at most one, so monomial substitution yields \[f_S(\mathbf{z}^{\mathbf{a}_1},\ldots,\mathbf{z}^{\mathbf{a}_d})=\sum_{\mathbf{v}\in A(S)}\mathbf{z}^{\mathbf{v}}=f_{A(S)}(\mathbf{z}).\] Therefore projection and substitution coincide exactly when no two points of \(S\) collide under the map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the exponent map is injective on the set, monomial substitution equals the indicator generating function of the projected image.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection–Substitution Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The collision-free correspondence is mathematically correct for the stated finite-set setting, but it lacks supporting evidence with a specific locator.

children.title: Collision Regimes
children.top_down_role: Multiplicity and cancellation issues caused by noninjective exponent mappings.

assumptions_latex: The set \(S\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d\) is finite.
The integer linear map \(A\) is not injective on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A collision produces coefficients greater than one, so raw substitution is not the indicator generating function of \(A(S)\).

notation.meaning: Multiplicity of the image fiber at \(\mathbf{v}\).
Support operation replacing every nonzero coefficient by one.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of raw substitution when projected lattice points collide.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If distinct \(\mathbf{u},\mathbf{u}'\in S\) satisfy \(A\mathbf{u}=A\mathbf{u}'=\mathbf{v}\), then the coefficient of \(\mathbf{z}^{\mathbf{v}}\) after substitution is \(m_{\mathbf{v}}\geq2\), whereas its coefficient in \(f_{A(S)}\) is one. For example, with \(S=\{(0,0),(1,0)\}\) and \(A(u_1,u_2)=u_2\), substitution gives \(2\), while \(f_{A(S)}(z)=1\). Thus raw substitution fails in the collision regime; recovering the projected-set series requires coefficient support reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When multiple original points share an image, substitution records multiplicity and no longer equals the projected-set indicator series.
knowledge_statements.title: Collision Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure phenomenon and example correctly distinguish multiplicity-generating substitution from projected-set indicators, but the record supplies no citation.

children.title: Variable Specialization
children.top_down_role: Evaluation or restriction of selected generating-function variables.

assumptions_latex: The Laurent polynomial \(f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})\) has finite support.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Specializing \(\mathbf{y}=\mathbf{1}\) sums coefficients over all exponents in the specialized variables.

notation.meaning: A finitely supported multivariate Laurent polynomial.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-support specialization, avoiding convergence and rational-presentation singularity issues.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finitely supported Laurent polynomial \(f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})=\sum_{\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}}c_{\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}}\mathbf{x}^{\mathbf{u}}\mathbf{y}^{\mathbf{v}}\), specialization of the \(\mathbf{y}\)-variables at one is \[f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{1})=\sum_{\mathbf{u}}\left(\sum_{\mathbf{v}}c_{\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}}\right)\mathbf{x}^{\mathbf{u}}.\] Hence specialization aggregates coefficients along fibers of the coordinate-forgetting map. If \(f\) is presented rationally, direct termwise substitution into that presentation is valid only when the substituted denominators are nonzero or their singularities have first been removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Setting selected variables to one sums coefficients across their exponents; a rational presentation may require cancellation before evaluation.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable Specialization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-support specialization formula is correct, but the additional rational-presentation singularity boundary is nontrivial and has no supporting source.

children.title: Coefficient Extraction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of selected coefficient data from compact representations.

assumptions_latex: The formal Laurent series has well-defined coefficients in the chosen coefficient ring.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The operator \([\mathbf{x}^{\mathbf{a}}]\) returns exactly the coefficient indexed by \(\mathbf{a}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient extraction for formal multivariate Laurent series.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a formal Laurent series \(f(\mathbf{x})=\sum_{\mathbf{u}\in\mathbb{Z}^d}c_{\mathbf{u}}\mathbf{x}^{\mathbf{u}}\) and an exponent \(\mathbf{a}\in\mathbb{Z}^d\), define \[[\mathbf{x}^{\mathbf{a}}]f(\mathbf{x})=c_{\mathbf{a}}.\] Equivalently, coefficient extraction is constant-term extraction after a monomial shift: \[[\mathbf{x}^{\mathbf{a}}]f(\mathbf{x})=\operatorname{CT}_{\mathbf{x}}\bigl(\mathbf{x}^{-\mathbf{a}}f(\mathbf{x})\bigr).\] If \(f=f_S\) is an indicator generating function, this coefficient equals one precisely when \(\mathbf{a}\in S\), and equals zero otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficient extraction selects one exponent's coefficient and equals constant-term extraction after shifting by the inverse monomial.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Extraction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The extraction definition, constant-term identity, and indicator interpretation are correct and fit the definition leaf, but no evidence is cited.

children.title: Specialization–Extraction Interface
children.top_down_role: Interaction between variable restrictions and coefficient queries.

assumptions_latex: The Laurent polynomial \(f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})\) has finite support.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Extraction produces individual fiber series, while specialization at \(\mathbf{y}=\mathbf{1}\) sums all such fiber series.

notation.meaning: Finite support of exponents in the \(\mathbf{y}\)-variables.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-support decomposition into extracted fibers and their specialized aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})\) be a finitely supported Laurent polynomial, and let \(B\) be its finite set of \(\mathbf{y}\)-exponents. Define \(g_{\mathbf{b}}(\mathbf{x})=[\mathbf{y}^{\mathbf{b}}]f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})\). Then \[f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})=\sum_{\mathbf{b}\in B}g_{\mathbf{b}}(\mathbf{x})\mathbf{y}^{\mathbf{b}},\qquad f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{1})=\sum_{\mathbf{b}\in B}g_{\mathbf{b}}(\mathbf{x}).\] Thus extraction isolates a single fiber, whereas specialization aggregates all fibers. Moreover, for any finite \(C\subseteq B\), the selected aggregate is \(\sum_{\mathbf{b}\in C}[\mathbf{y}^{\mathbf{b}}]f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficient extraction isolates one exponent fiber, while specialization at one sums the extracted fiber series over all specialized exponents.
knowledge_statements.title: Specialization–Extraction Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-support decomposition accurately relates extraction and specialization, and property is an appropriate kind, but the record has no source or locator.

children.title: Singular Evaluation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Cases where specialization reaches poles or requires cancellation handling.

assumptions_latex: The displayed short rational functions represent the same Laurent polynomial or rational function before specialization.
The specialization homomorphism may map one or more denominator monomials to \(1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A singular termwise substitution is not a valid evaluation rule; the aggregate expression must first be combined or regularized, and the desired value exists only when the aggregate singularity is removable.
review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports singular specialization of short rational generating functions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between algebraically valid specialization and undefined termwise evaluation at denominator zeros.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(\mathbf{x})=\sum_i \varepsilon_i\mathbf{x}^{\mathbf{a}_i}/\prod_j(1-\mathbf{x}^{\mathbf{b}_{ij}})\) represent an aggregate rational function, and let \(\phi\) be a monomial specialization with \(M\mathbf{b}_{ij}=\mathbf{0}\) for some denominator vector. Then the corresponding summand has denominator \(1-\mathbf{y}^{\mathbf{0}}=0\), so applying \(\phi\) term by term is undefined. Even when cancellations make \(\phi(F)\) regular, its value must be obtained from the combined rational function or from a common perturbation followed by Laurent-series cancellation. If the aggregate principal part does not vanish, no finite specialized value exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When specialization sends a denominator monomial to one, individual terms become undefined. A value is legitimate only after aggregate pole cancellation or a common regularization.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular Evaluation Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role and mathematical formulation are plausible, but no cited source with an inspectable locator supports the regularization and aggregate-pole claims.

children.title: Barvinok Algorithm Family
children.top_down_role: Fixed-dimension cone decompositions and short-generating-function construction.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: A Polynomial Time Algorithm for Counting Integral Points in Polyhedra When the Dimension Is Fixed
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Mathematics of Operations Research 19(4), 1994
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: A Polynomial Time Algorithm for Counting Integral Points in Polyhedra When the Dimension Is Fixed

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Effective Lattice Point Counting in Rational Convex Polytopes
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Barvinok implementations and LattE
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Effective Lattice Point Counting in Rational Convex Polytopes

assumptions_latex: \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is a bounded rational polytope.
Generating functions are interpreted as rational-function valuations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lattice-point generating function of \(P\) equals the sum of the generating functions of its vertex tangent cones.

notation.meaning: The lattice-point generating function of a rational polyhedron.
The feasible tangent cone of the polytope at a vertex.

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports Brion-type vertex-cone localization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Brion localization for bounded rational polytopes, interpreted through rational generating-function valuations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every vertex \(v\in\operatorname{vert}(P)\), define the tangent cone \(C_v=v+\operatorname{cone}(P-v)\). Under the rational-function continuation of lattice-point generating functions, Brion localization gives \[f_P(\mathbf{x})=\sum_{v\in\operatorname{vert}(P)}f_{C_v}(\mathbf{x}).\] Contributions associated with nonvertex faces cancel in the valuation, and cones containing lines have zero image. Thus lattice-point counting or coefficient extraction for \(P\) may be reduced to computing and assembling rational generating functions for its vertex cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded rational polytope's lattice-point generating function is the sum of the rational generating functions of its vertex tangent cones.
knowledge_statements.title: Vertex-Cone Localization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation accurately resembles Brion localization and fits the leaf, but no source or locator is supplied for the valuation identity and treatment of line-containing cones.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplicial-Cone Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Half-open triangulation form, which avoids inclusion-exclusion corrections on common faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exists a rational triangulation \(C=C_1\cup\cdots\cup C_s\) in which every \(C_k\) is generated by linearly independent rays and intersections are common faces. After choosing compatible open or closed status for boundary facets, the resulting half-open cones satisfy \[C\cap\mathbb{Z}^d=\biguplus_{k=1}^{s}\bigl(C_k^{\circ}\cap\mathbb{Z}^d\bigr),\qquad f_C(\mathbf{x})=\sum_{k=1}^{s}f_{C_k^{\circ}}(\mathbf{x}).\] Equivalently, closed simplicial cones may be used with inclusion-exclusion terms supported on proper faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Triangulate a pointed rational cone into simplicial cones; a compatible half-open convention makes their lattice points disjoint and their generating functions additive.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is a pointed rational polyhedral cone.
A consistent half-open convention is fixed for shared faces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generating function of \(C\) is the sum of the generating functions of finitely many half-open simplicial cones forming a triangulation of \(C\).

notation.meaning: Half-open simplicial cones in a triangulation.

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports simplicial reduction for cone generating functions.

assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a full-dimensional simplicial rational cone in fixed dimension \(d\).
Its primitive integer ray generators are given in binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A signed decomposition into unimodular cones yields short rational summands whose denominators use lattice-basis ray generators.

notation.meaning: The lattice index of the ray-generator matrix.
Signed unimodular cones produced by the recursion.

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports Barvinok signed unimodular decomposition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-dimensional signed decomposition of a simplicial cone, modulo line-containing or lower-dimensional corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\Delta(C)=1\), output \(C\). Otherwise choose a nonzero integer vector giving a short integral combination of the rays, form the signed child cones obtained by replacing one ray at a time, and recurse on children having smaller determinant. In the cone valuation modulo cones containing lines, the output satisfies \[[C]=\sum_k\varepsilon_k[U_k],\qquad \varepsilon_k\in\{-1,1\},\qquad \Delta(U_k)=1.\] For a translated unimodular cone \(v+U_k\), enumerate its fundamental parallelepiped representative \(a_k\) and output \(\varepsilon_k\mathbf{x}^{a_k}/\prod_{j=1}^{d}(1-\mathbf{x}^{u_{kj}})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recursively replace a simplicial cone by signed lower-index cones until every cone is unimodular, then emit one short rational term per cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Unimodular-Cone Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the signed recursion, determinant reduction, valuation qualifications, and translated-cone numerator require an authoritative source with a specific locator.

children.title: Primal Decomposition Variants
children.top_down_role: Signed decomposition performed directly in primal cone space.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Decomposition Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct decompositions performed on rays and faces of the original cone rather than its polar.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A primal decomposition variant constructs rational cones \(C_k\) directly from rays or faces of \(C\) and signs \(\varepsilon_k\in\{-1,1\}\) such that \[[C]=\sum_k\varepsilon_k[C_k]\] in the chosen cone valuation. Ordinary triangulation uses positive coefficients together with half-open boundary assignments; signed ray-replacement variants allow overlapping cones and compensate by signs and lower-dimensional terms. Applying the lattice-point generating-function valuation gives \(f_C(\mathbf{x})=\sum_k\varepsilon_k f_{C_k}(\mathbf{x})\), provided every boundary convention or correction term is retained consistently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal variants decompose the original cone directly by its rays, using half-open subdivisions or signed identities whose generating functions add to the original.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is a pointed rational cone.
Cone identities are taken in a polyhedral valuation modulo cones containing lines.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Direct subdivisions or signed ray-replacement identities in the primal space produce an additive representation of \([C]\) by simpler primal cones.

notation.meaning: The indicator-function valuation class of a cone.

review_flags: The exact intended family of primal variants is not specified by the node path.
No supplied source locator supports the stated valuation formulation.

children.title: Polar Decomposition Variants
children.top_down_role: Decomposition organized through polar or dual cone representations.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is full-dimensional and pointed.
Polarity is taken with respect to the standard inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Decomposing the polar cone and polarizing the pieces back yields a signed valuation identity for the primal cone.

notation.meaning: The polar cone under the nonpositive convention.
Signed cones in a decomposition of the polar.

review_flags: The exact intended family of polar variants is not specified by the node path.
No supplied source locator supports the stated polar-decomposition procedure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decompose in the dual space, then return to primal cones by polarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: First form \(C^{\circ}\), construct a valuation identity \([C^{\circ}]=\sum_k\varepsilon_k[D_k]\), and discard terms whose later valuation is zero. Polarizing the surviving cones back, with the incidence-reversing signs and face corrections required by the selected cone algebra, produces \[[C]=\sum_k\widetilde{\varepsilon}_k[D_k^{\circ}].\] The lattice-point generating-function valuation may then be applied to the primal cones \(D_k^{\circ}\). This procedure is useful when the facet description of \(C\) makes the ray description of \(C^{\circ}\) easier to decompose.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polar variant decomposes the dual cone, converts the pieces back by polarity, and tracks the signs and face corrections required for equality.
knowledge_statements.title: Polar Decomposition Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the variants leaf, but polarity does not transparently transport an arbitrary signed indicator identity in the stated form. The required signs, face corrections, and zero terms are left unspecified, so a source is needed to determine a reliable formulation.

children.title: Primal–Polar Duality
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between primal decomposition data and polar representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Polar Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric polarity underlying interchangeable primal-ray and polar-facet decomposition strategies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Polarity satisfies \((C^{\circ})^{\circ}=C\) and \(C_1\subseteq C_2\) if and only if \(C_2^{\circ}\subseteq C_1^{\circ}\). For every face \(F\) of \(C\), the set \(F^{\diamond}=C^{\circ}\cap F^{\perp}\) is a face of \(C^{\circ}\), and \[\dim F+\dim F^{\diamond}=d.\] This correspondence reverses face inclusion, so extreme rays of one cone correspond to facets of the other. Consequently, a cone may be decomposed using either its primal rays or the rays of its polar, provided polarity-induced signs and boundary terms are handled in the applicable valuation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polarity is an inclusion-reversing involution exchanging rays and facets, thereby linking decompositions based on primal generators with decompositions based on dual inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is a closed, full-dimensional, pointed polyhedral cone.
The polar uses the nonpositive inner-product convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Polarity is an inclusion-reversing involution that exchanges rays with facets and converts primal cone descriptions into dual descriptions.

notation.meaning: The dual face corresponding to a face of the primal cone.

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports the full primal-polar face correspondence.

children.title: Dimension-Sensitive Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Comparative behavior under primal dimension, dual dimension, and cone structure.

assumptions_latex: The ambient dimension \(d\) is fixed.
The rational cone or polytope is encoded by binary rational inequalities or generators of total length \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Short generating-function construction is polynomial in \(L\) for fixed \(d\), while its degree and output constants may grow rapidly with \(d\).
review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports the fixed-dimensional Barvinok complexity bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-dimension tractability boundary for signed cone decomposition and short generating-function output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each fixed \(d\), vertex localization, simplicial reduction, signed unimodular decomposition, and rational-function assembly can be performed in \(L^{O_d(1)}\) bit operations, producing \(L^{O_d(1)}\) short rational terms. The exponent and hidden constants depend on \(d\). If \(d\) is part of the input, this statement supplies no polynomial bound: triangulation size, decomposition branching, and the number of necessary rational terms can grow exponentially with dimension. Thus choosing primal or polar variants may improve instance-dependent cone sizes without removing the fixed-dimension hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Barvinok-style construction is polynomial in binary input length when dimension is fixed; dependence on dimension can be exponential and variant choice affects practical size.
knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Sensitive Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the leaf, but the bit-complexity and output-size bounds, as well as the asserted dimension dependence, need an authoritative Barvinok reference with a theorem or section locator.

children.title: Rational-Function Assembly
children.top_down_role: Combination of local rational terms into compact global representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Rational-Function Assembly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assembly of signed cone contributions into one short rational generating-function representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each signed cone record, form \[R_i(\mathbf{x})=\varepsilon_i\frac{\mathbf{x}^{\mathbf{a}_i}}{\prod_{j=1}^{k_i}(1-\mathbf{x}^{\mathbf{b}_{ij}})}.\] Initialize \(F(\mathbf{x})=0\), add every \(R_i\), and retain the result as a signed list rather than expanding its numerator or power series. Terms with identical denominator data may be combined by exact monomial arithmetic. The output \(F(\mathbf{x})=\sum_iR_i(\mathbf{x})\) represents the target lattice-point generating function in the rational-function valuation, although individual summands may have poles at points where the aggregate function is regular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convert each signed cone to a rational term and retain their exact sum as a compact list, without expanding the represented power series.
assumptions_latex: A finite signed collection of translated unimodular or simplicial cones has been produced.
All cone terms use a common monomial variable vector \(\mathbf{x}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Summing the cone terms constructs a short rational function representing the localized lattice-point generating function.
review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports short rational-function assembly.

children.title: Exact Rational Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Exact evaluation of assembled rational-function representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Rational Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact regularized evaluation at the all-ones point using a generic one-parameter perturbation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Substitute \(x_r=e^{t\lambda_r}\) simultaneously into every summand of \(F\). Expand each exponential numerator and each factor \((1-e^{t\langle\lambda,\mathbf{b}\rangle})^{-1}\) as a Laurent series, retaining enough terms to determine degree zero after multiplication. Sum the truncated Laurent series exactly over \(\mathbb{Q}\); regularity implies cancellation of every negative-power coefficient. Output \[F(\mathbf{1})=\operatorname{CT}_t F(e^{t\lambda_1},\ldots,e^{t\lambda_d}).\] When \(F\) represents a finite set's generating polynomial, this value is its lattice-point count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate a regular short rational function exactly by a common exponential perturbation, cancellation of Laurent poles, and extraction of the constant term.
assumptions_latex: \(F(\mathbf{x})\) is an assembled short rational function whose aggregate is regular at the requested point.
A rational vector \(\lambda\) is chosen so no denominator direction is orthogonal to it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact value at \(\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{1}\) is the constant term of the aggregate Laurent expansion under \(x_r=e^{t\lambda_r}\).

notation.meaning: Constant-term extraction in the Laurent variable.

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports exact Laurent-series evaluation of short generating functions.

children.title: Assembly–Evaluation Interface
children.top_down_role: Representation choices affecting exact evaluation and simplification.

knowledge_statements.title: Assembly–Evaluation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility rule connecting signed rational assembly with exact specialization and evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F(\mathbf{x})=\sum_iR_i(\mathbf{x})\) and every denominator of every \(R_i\) is nonzero at the evaluation point, then linearity gives \[E(F)=\sum_iE(R_i).\] If some summands have poles there, the right-hand side is not defined termwise even when \(F\) is regular. In that regime, apply one common perturbation to all summands, assemble their Laurent expansions, verify cancellation of the aggregate principal part, and only then take the finite coefficient or limit. Hence a short representation and its represented function have different admissible termwise evaluation domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assembly and evaluation commute where every term is regular. At term poles, use one common regularization and evaluate only after aggregate cancellation.
assumptions_latex: The assembled short rational function represents an aggregate function \(F\).
All evaluation and specialization operations are performed over exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Evaluation commutes with assembly away from term poles; at singular points it is valid only after common regularization and aggregate cancellation.
