review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports the assembly-evaluation commutation boundary.

children.title: Pole-Cancellation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Evaluation settings where individual terms are singular but aggregate values remain regular.

knowledge_statements.title: Pole-Cancellation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Laurent-coefficient criterion for removable aggregate singularities under a common generic perturbation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write each perturbed summand as \(R_i(t)=\sum_{k=-m_i}^{\infty}c_{ik}t^k\) and let \(m=\max_i m_i\). The aggregate \(F(t)=\sum_iR_i(t)\) is regular at \(t=0\) if and only if \[\sum_i c_{ik}=0\qquad\text{for every }k=-m,\ldots,-1.\] Under this condition its exact value is \(F(0)=\sum_i c_{i0}\). If any negative coefficient sum is nonzero, the selected specialization retains a pole and finite evaluation fails. A generic perturbation is required to avoid accidentally hiding denominator directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An aggregate pole is removable exactly when all negative Laurent coefficients cancel across the signed terms; the value is then the summed constant coefficient.
assumptions_latex: A common generic perturbation converts every rational summand into a Laurent series in \(t\).
Only finitely many negative powers occur in each summand.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregate has a removable pole precisely when the sum of every negative Laurent coefficient is zero.

notation.meaning: Laurent coefficients of the individual perturbed summands.

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports this pole-cancellation criterion in the generating-function setting.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Decomposition Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Signed primal-space decomposition of pointed rational cones into unimodular cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a pointed rational simplicial cone \(C=\operatorname{cone}(b_1,\ldots,b_d)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) with integral generators, initialize the list with \((1,C)\). Whenever a listed cone has lattice determinant exceeding \(1\), choose a nonzero lattice vector in its fundamental parallelepiped and replace the cone, under the lattice-point valuation, by signed cones obtained by substituting that vector for one generator. Apply consistent half-open boundary conventions and repeat until every full-dimensional cone is unimodular. The output \((\varepsilon_j,C_j)_{j=1}^N\) satisfies \[f(C\cap\mathbb{Z}^d;z)=\sum_{j=1}^N\varepsilon_j f(C_j\cap\mathbb{Z}^d;z),\qquad \varepsilon_j\in\{-1,1\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recursively replace a non-unimodular primal cone by signed cones of smaller determinant, using half-open boundaries, until their rational generating functions form an exact unimodular decomposition.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is pointed, full-dimensional, rational, and simplicial.
The decomposition uses a lattice-point valuation with consistent half-open facets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(C\cap\mathbb{Z}^d;z)=\sum_j\varepsilon_j f(C_j\cap\mathbb{Z}^d;z)\) with unimodular \(C_j\).

notation.meaning: The multivariate generating function summing the monomials indexed by the lattice set S.
The sign attached to the j-th decomposed cone.

review_flags: A Barvinok-algorithm source is required for the precise primal signed-decomposition variant and its boundary convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind fits the leaf, but no source supports the precise determinant-reducing vector choice, signed valuation identity, termination, or half-open boundary treatment. Those details are essential to the mathematical validity of this primal Barvinok variant.

knowledge_statements.title: Irrational Decomposition Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary-free cone decomposition using lattice-preserving irrational perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the rational cones occurring in a finite Barvinok decomposition, choose perturbations of their apices that preserve each cone's lattice points and place no lattice point on any proper facet hyperplane. Recursively perform signed simplicial decompositions on the perturbed cones, retaining only full-dimensional terms; facet contributions vanish under the lattice-point valuation because the perturbed facets contain no lattice points. Stop when all retained cones are unimodular. If \(C_j'\) are the resulting perturbed cones, then the algorithm returns signs \(\varepsilon_j\) satisfying \[f(C\cap\mathbb{Z}^d;z)=\sum_j\varepsilon_j f(C_j'\cap\mathbb{Z}^d;z).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perturb cone boundaries without changing their lattice points, then decompose while discarding lower-dimensional boundary terms because no lattice point lies on a perturbed facet.
assumptions_latex: Only finitely many cones and facet hyperplanes must be treated.
Each perturbation preserves the lattice points of its associated cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The signed full-dimensional unimodular terms give the same lattice-point generating function as the original cone.

notation.meaning: An irrationally perturbed cone produced during decomposition.
The multivariate lattice-point generating function of S.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind fits the leaf. A specialized source is required to establish the simultaneous lattice-preserving irrational perturbations, the absence of lattice points on all relevant facets, and the validity of discarding lower-dimensional terms.

children.title: Homogenized Variants
children.top_down_role: Barvinok variants using homogenized cone representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Homogenized Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogenization represents a bounded rational polytope as a pointed cone one dimension higher.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be a bounded rational polytope and define its homogenized cone by \[\widehat P=\{(tx,t)\in\mathbb{R}^{d+1}:t\geq0,\ x\in P\}.\] Then \(\widehat P\) is a pointed rational polyhedral cone and its height-one lattice slice satisfies \[\widehat P\cap(\mathbb{Z}^d\times\{1\})=\{(x,1):x\in P\cap\mathbb{Z}^d\}.\] Consequently, if \(F_{\widehat P}(z,u)=\sum_{(a,m)\in\widehat P\cap\mathbb{Z}^{d+1}}z^a u^m\), then \[f(P\cap\mathbb{Z}^d;z)=[u^1]F_{\widehat P}(z,u).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lattice points of a bounded rational polytope are exactly the height-one lattice points of its homogenized cone, so coefficient extraction recovers their generating function.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a bounded rational polytope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(P\cap\mathbb{Z}^d;z)=[u^1]F_{\widehat P}(z,u)\).

notation.meaning: Coefficient extraction at degree one in u.

However, the record supplies neither a citation nor an explicit standard-field rationale, so it lacks the required evidence.

children.title: Dual-Space Variants
children.top_down_role: Barvinok variants operating through dual or polar geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Space Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barvinok decomposition performed after passing from a cone to its polar.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a full-dimensional pointed rational cone \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\), compute its polar \(C^\circ=\{y:\langle y,x\rangle\leq0\text{ for every }x\in C\}\). Triangulate and recursively decompose \(C^\circ\), under the polyhedral valuation, into signed unimodular cones \((\varepsilon_j,D_j)\). Polarize the resulting cones back to primal space and impose a consistent half-open convention on shared faces. The returned cones satisfy the valuation identity \[[C]=\sum_j\varepsilon_j[D_j^\circ],\] and applying the lattice-point generating-function valuation yields a signed short rational representation for \(f(C\cap\mathbb{Z}^d;z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polarize the input cone, perform signed unimodular decomposition in dual space, and polarize the pieces back to obtain the primal generating function.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is full-dimensional, pointed, and rational.
Polarity and boundary conventions are applied within the same polyhedral valuation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The polarized-back signed cones represent \([C]\) and hence its lattice-point generating function.

notation.meaning: The nonpositive polar cone of C.
The indicator of C regarded as a polyhedral valuation element.

children.title: Homogenization–Duality Interface
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between homogenized representations and dual-space decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Homogenization–Duality Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polar description of the homogenized cone through the support function of the polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be a nonempty bounded rational polytope, let \(\widehat P=\{(tx,t):t\geq0,\ x\in P\}\), and let \(h_P(y)=\max_{x\in P}\langle y,x\rangle\). With the nonpositive-polar convention, \[\widehat P^\circ=\{(y,s)\in\mathbb{R}^{d+1}:\langle y,x\rangle+s\leq0\text{ for every }x\in P\}=\{(y,s):s\leq-h_P(y)\}.\] Thus homogenization converts all affine inequalities defining \(P\) into homogeneous cone inequalities, while polarity represents the dual cone as the hypograph of the negative support function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polar of a polytope's homogenized cone is exactly the hypograph of the negative support function, linking affine homogenization with cone duality.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is nonempty, bounded, and rational.
The polar uses the inequality \(\langle v,w\rangle\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat P^\circ=\{(y,s):s\leq-h_P(y)\}\).

notation.meaning: The nonpositive polar of the homogenized cone.

children.title: Dimension Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Comparative dependence on ambient, homogenized, and dual dimensions.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of homogenization and polarity on fixed-dimensional Barvinok complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For input dimension \(d\), homogenization replaces a polytope in \(\mathbb{R}^d\) by a cone in \(\mathbb{R}^{d+1}\), whereas polarity preserves the ambient cone dimension. Hence a Barvinok subroutine whose bit complexity is \(L^{O(1)}\) for each fixed ambient dimension remains polynomial after either transformation when \(d\) is fixed. The polynomial degree and hidden constants may, however, change from their values at dimension \(d\) to those at dimension \(d+1\). Therefore homogenization preserves fixed-dimensional polynomiality but does not preserve dimension-dependent parameter bounds or constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenization adds one dimension and duality adds none; fixed-dimensional polynomiality survives, but dimension-dependent exponents and constants may worsen.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) denotes the binary encoding length of the rational input.
The generating-function subroutine is polynomial-time for every fixed ambient dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transformed computation is polynomial in \(L\) for fixed \(d\), with parameters governed by dimension \(d+1\) after homogenization.

children.title: Exact Cardinality Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery of exact lattice-point counts from compact generating functions.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Cardinality Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact evaluation of a finite-set short generating function at the all-ones point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d\) be finite and let a short rational expression represent \(f_S(z)=\sum_{a\in S}z^a\). Choose an integer vector \(\lambda\) generic for every denominator direction, substitute \(z_i=\exp(\lambda_i t)\), expand each rational summand as a Laurent series at \(t=0\), and sum their constant terms after cancellation. Although individual summands may have poles, their sum represents the Laurent polynomial \(f_S\) and is regular at \(t=0\). Output \[|S|=f_S(1,\ldots,1)=\lim_{t\to0}f_S(\exp(\lambda_1t),\ldots,\exp(\lambda_dt)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substitute a generic exponential curve into the short rational function and cancel Laurent poles; the resulting constant term is the exact set cardinality.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite.
The supplied short rational expression equals \(f_S\) as a rational function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regularized all-ones evaluation equals the integer \(|S|\).

notation.meaning: The generating polynomial of the finite lattice set S.
A generic integer direction used for regularized evaluation.

review_flags: A source is needed for the regularized specialization algorithm and its exact-arithmetic complexity.

children.title: Weighted Sum Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery of aggregate values under encoded lattice-point weights.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Sum Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial lattice-point weights recovered by Euler differential operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d\) be finite, let \(f_S(z)=\sum_{a\in S}z^a\), and let \(p\in\mathbb{Q}[x_1,\ldots,x_d]\). Define the Euler operators \(E_i=z_i\frac{\partial}{\partial z_i}\). Since \(E_i z^a=a_i z^a\), the weighted sum has the exact representation \[\sum_{a\in S}p(a)=\left. p(E_1,\ldots,E_d)f_S(z)\right|_{z=(1,\ldots,1)}.\] For a short rational representation, differentiation is performed symbolically and the final specialization is evaluated by a common generic Laurent expansion so that removable poles cancel across summands.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply the polynomial weight as Euler differential operators to the generating function, then regularize at one to recover the exact weighted sum.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite.
\(p\) is a rational-coefficient polynomial.
The rational expression represents \(f_S\) exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{a\in S}p(a)=\left.p(E_1,\ldots,E_d)f_S(z)\right|_{z=(1,\ldots,1)}\).

children.title: Weight-Encoding Regimes
children.top_down_role: Output behavior across polynomial, monomial, or externally encoded weights.

knowledge_statements.title: Weight-Encoding Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Succinctness condition for polynomial-time weighted recovery from short generating functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A weight family \(w:S\to\mathbb{Q}\) is compatible with short-generating-function recovery when it is supplied by a polynomial-size expression that induces polynomially many permitted substitutions, Hadamard products, or differential operators on \(f_S\), and when all intermediate exponent and coefficient bit lengths remain polynomially bounded. Sparse polynomial weights of fixed degree satisfy this condition through Euler operators. An explicitly tabulated arbitrary weight requires input proportional to \(|S|\), while a black-box weight without compatible algebraic encoding does not by itself yield a short rational representation of \(\sum_{a\in S}w(a)z^a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted recovery is succinct only when the weight has a compact algebraic encoding compatible with generating-function operations and polynomially bounded intermediate bit lengths.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and represented by a short generating function.
Arithmetic is exact and measured in the binary bit model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fixed-degree sparse polynomial weights are compatible; arbitrary tables or unsupported black-box weights need not be.

notation.meaning: The encoded weight function on S.
The short generating function representing S.

children.title: Output-Complexity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Dependence of recovery cost on output length and weight representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Output-Complexity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential separation between expanded support and compact generating-function or cardinality output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S_n=\{0,1\}^n\), an inequality description has size polynomial in \(n\), and \[f_{S_n}(z)=\prod_{i=1}^n(1+z_i)\] has a representation of size \(O(n)\). Its expanded monomial list nevertheless contains \(2^n\) terms, so no algorithm can emit that list in time polynomial in \(n\). In contrast, the exact cardinality \(|S_n|=2^n\) has only \(n+1\) binary digits. Thus polynomial-time short generating-function construction or cardinality recovery does not imply polynomial-time enumeration or expanded-polynomial output.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Boolean cube has a linear-size factored generating function and a short binary count, but its expanded support has exponentially many monomials.
assumptions_latex: Output time includes the time required to write the requested representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compact representation and exact counting can be polynomial-output tasks even when explicit enumeration necessarily has exponential output.

notation.meaning: The n-dimensional Boolean cube viewed as a lattice set.

review_flags: The example is self-contained, but an authoritative output-sensitive complexity source is not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary content kind is correct, and the Boolean-cube example consistently demonstrates the output-size separation. Nevertheless, no citation or explicit standard-field rationale is supplied for the output-complexity conclusion required by the evidence contract.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimization from Generating Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear optimization over a finite lattice set using threshold filtering and emptiness tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite set \(S\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d\) through its short generating function, an integral objective \(c\in\mathbb{Z}^d\), and valid integer bounds \(L\leq c^\top a\leq U\) for every \(a\in S\). Repeatedly form the generating function of \(S\cap\{a:c^\top a\geq\tau\}\) and test whether it is zero, using binary search on \(\tau\in[L,U]\). The largest feasible threshold is \(v^*=\max_{a\in S}c^\top a\). To recover an optimizer, intersect with \(c^\top a=v^*\) and successively fix coordinates using analogous nonemptiness queries until one lattice point remains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary-search objective thresholds using generating-function intersection and emptiness, then fix coordinates to recover a maximizing lattice point.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and nonempty.
Threshold intersection and zero testing are available in the chosen short-generating-function model.
\(L\) and \(U\) are valid encoded objective bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns \(v^*=\max_{a\in S}c^\top a\) and some \(a^*\in S\) attaining it.
review_flags: A source is required for closure under threshold intersection, zero testing, and the associated fixed-dimensional complexity.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind fits the leaf. Conditional on threshold intersection and zero testing, binary search recovers the value, but the availability and complexity of those operations, as well as coordinate-fixing bounds, require a source and a specified fixed-dimensional short-generating-function model.

children.title: Projection Queries

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Queries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean projection of a finite lattice set represented by a short generating function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^{d+k}\) be finite and let \(\pi(x,y)=x\) project onto the first \(d\) coordinates. Given a short rational generating function for \(S\), apply a generating-function projection procedure that merges all points with the same projected coordinate and Booleanizes their coefficients. The output represents the set, rather than the multiset, \[T=\pi(S)=\{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d:\text{there exists }y\in\mathbb{Z}^k\text{ with }(x,y)\in S\},\qquad f_T(z)=\sum_{x\in T}z^x.\] For fixed \(d+k\), the procedure is polynomial-time in the input and short-representation lengths.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project a finite lattice set, merge duplicate images, and output a short generating function whose coefficients indicate existence rather than fiber multiplicity.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite.
The total dimension \(d+k\) is fixed.
The input is an exact short rational generating function for \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a short representation of \(f_{\pi(S)}(z)=\sum_{x\in\pi(S)}z^x\), with every nonzero coefficient equal to \(1\).

notation.meaning: Coordinate projection onto the first d coordinates.
The projected lattice set with duplicate images removed.

children.title: Set Union Interfaces

knowledge_statements.title: Set Union Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indicator generating-function interface for unions of finite projected lattice-point sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite sets \(A,B\subseteq\mathbb Z^d\), define \(f_S(\mathbf z)=\sum_{u\in S}\mathbf z^u\). Since these series have coefficients in \(\{0,1\}\), their union satisfies \[f_{A\cup B}(\mathbf z)=f_A(\mathbf z)+f_B(\mathbf z)-f_{A\cap B}(\mathbf z)=f_A+f_B-(f_A*f_B),\] where \(*\) is the coefficientwise Hadamard product. For sets \(A_1,\ldots,A_m\), the corresponding interface is the inclusion-exclusion identity over nonempty index subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A union’s indicator generating function is obtained by inclusion-exclusion; for two sets, subtract their Hadamard-product intersection from the sum.
assumptions_latex: \(A,B\subseteq\mathbb Z^d\) are finite.
\(f_A\) and \(f_B\) encode set indicators, not multiplicities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_{A\cup B}=f_A+f_B-f_A*f_B\).

children.title: Set Intersection Interfaces

knowledge_statements.title: Set Intersection Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hadamard-product interface for intersections of finite lattice-point sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A,B\subseteq\mathbb Z^d\) be finite and let \(f_A(\mathbf z)=\sum_u a_u\mathbf z^u\) and \(f_B(\mathbf z)=\sum_u b_u\mathbf z^u\), where \(a_u,b_u\in\{0,1\}\) are membership indicators. The coefficientwise product satisfies \[f_A*f_B=\sum_{u\in\mathbb Z^d}a_ub_u\mathbf z^u=f_{A\cap B}(\mathbf z).\] Thus intersection is represented exactly by the Hadamard product of the two indicator generating functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Hadamard product multiplies membership coefficients, so it exactly represents the intersection of two finite lattice sets.
assumptions_latex: \(A,B\subseteq\mathbb Z^d\) are finite.
All generating-function coefficients are membership indicators in \(\{0,1\}\).

children.title: Set Difference Interfaces

knowledge_statements.title: Set Difference Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indicator generating-function interface for relative complements of finite lattice sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite \(A,B\subseteq\mathbb Z^d\), the difference \(A\setminus B\) has indicator \(1_A(u)(1-1_B(u))\). Consequently, if \(f_S(\mathbf z)=\sum_{u\in S}\mathbf z^u\), then \[f_{A\setminus B}(\mathbf z)=f_A(\mathbf z)-f_{A\cap B}(\mathbf z)=f_A-(f_A*f_B).\] Every resulting coefficient is again either zero or one, because the Hadamard term removes precisely the monomials supported by both sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Set difference is represented by subtracting the Hadamard-product intersection from the first set’s indicator generating function.
assumptions_latex: \(A,B\subseteq\mathbb Z^d\) are finite.
\(f_A\) and \(f_B\) have Boolean coefficients.

children.title: Projection–Set Interaction

knowledge_statements.title: Projection–Set Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set identities and multiplicity caveat for linear projections of lattice-point generating functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi:\mathbb Z^d\to\mathbb Z^k\) be linear and let \(A,B\subseteq\mathbb Z^d\) be finite. Then \(\pi(A\cup B)=\pi(A)\cup\pi(B)\), while only \(\pi(A\cap B)\subseteq\pi(A)\cap\pi(B)\) and \(\pi(A\setminus B)\supseteq\pi(A)\setminus\pi(B)\) hold generally. Moreover, monomial substitution induced by \(\pi\) sends \(f_A\) to \(\sum_y |A\cap\pi^{-1}(y)|\mathbf z^y\); it yields the indicator series of \(\pi(A)\) only when fibers are Booleanized or \(\pi|_A\) is injective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection preserves unions, but not generally intersections or differences; direct generating-function substitution counts fiber multiplicities unless projection is injective.

\(A,B\subseteq\mathbb Z^d\) are finite.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-Dimension Short Rational Generating Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial-time computation of a short rational representation for lattice-point generating functions of rational polyhedra in fixed dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{For fixed }d\text{ and a polyhedron }P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\text{ given by rational inequalities, there is a polynomial-time algorithm computing }g(P;\mathbf z)=\sum_{i\in I}\epsilon_i\frac{\mathbf z^{\mathbf a_i}}{\prod_{j=1}^d(1-\mathbf z^{\mathbf b_{ij}})},\quad \epsilon_i\in\{\pm1\},\quad \mathbf a_i,\mathbf b_{ij}\in\mathbb Z^d.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In fixed dimension, the lattice-point generating function of a rational polyhedron can be computed in polynomial time as a signed short rational function with d binomial denominator factors in each summand.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Dimension Counting Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barvinok’s polynomial-time lattice-point counting regime for fixed ambient dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(d\in\mathbb N\). Given a bounded rational polytope \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:Ax\le b\}\), with rational data encoded in binary, a Barvinok algorithm computes a short rational generating function for \(P\cap\mathbb Z^d\), and hence \(|P\cap\mathbb Z^d|\), in time polynomial in the binary input length. The polynomial’s degree and constants may depend on the fixed dimension \(d\); the assertion is not a uniform polynomial-time bound when \(d\) belongs to the input.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In every fixed dimension, Barvinok’s method counts lattice points in a bounded rational polytope in polynomial time in the binary input length.

\(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a bounded rational polytope.

The precise complexity theorem and short-generating-function output guarantee require an authoritative theorem or section locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Dimension Hardness Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the fixed-dimension polynomial-time guarantee when dimension is input-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When \(d\) is part of the input, exact lattice-point counting is \(\#\mathrm P\)-hard, even for bounded polytopes. Indeed, for integers \(a_1,\ldots,a_d,b\), the lattice points of \[P=\{x\in[0,1]^d:\textstyle\sum_{i=1}^d a_i x_i=b\}\] are exactly the incidence vectors of subsets whose weights sum to \(b\). Thus a polynomial-time exact counter for variable-dimensional rational polytopes would yield a polynomial-time algorithm for the associated counting subset-sum problem; absent \(\mathrm{FP}=\#\mathrm P\), no such general algorithm exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allowing dimension to vary makes exact polytope lattice-point counting #P-hard through the counting subset-sum encoding.
assumptions_latex: The dimension \(d\) is encoded as part of the instance.
Polytope coefficients are integers encoded in binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact computation of \(|P\cap\mathbb Z^d|\) is \(\#\mathrm P\)-hard in variable dimension.

notation.meaning: Counting complexity class associated with nondeterministic polynomial-time witnesses.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: parsimonious encoding of counting subset-sum by 0–1 lattice points

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The variable-dimension boundary is appropriately classified as a failure_boundary, but the #P-hardness claim depends on the complexity status and reduction properties of counting subset sum. Those claims require a specific authoritative source locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation-Length Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-sensitive size bound for Barvinok short rational generating-function outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each fixed \(d\), the Barvinok decomposition of a rational polytope \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) can be encoded as a signed sum of rational terms \(\epsilon_i\mathbf z^{a_i}/\prod_{j=1}^d(1-\mathbf z^{b_{ij}})\) whose total binary length is polynomial in the input length of \(P\). This bound is dimension-dependent: when \(d\) varies, the number of cones, rational summands, and denominator directions need not remain polynomially bounded by a dimension-independent polynomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Short generating functions have polynomial encoding length in fixed dimension, but that guarantee is not uniform when dimension grows.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a rational polytope given in binary.
The ambient dimension \(d\) is fixed for the polynomial-size guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The short rational representation has polynomial total encoding length for fixed \(d\), with no stated uniform bound over variable \(d\).

notation.meaning: Sign of a rational generating-function summand.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: output-sensitive formulation of fixed-dimensional Barvinok theory

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-dimensional polynomial encoding-length claim and the asserted loss of a dimension-independent polynomial bound are source-sensitive complexity statements. No theorem or section locator is supplied to establish the exact representation model and size guarantee.

children.title: Lattice-Polytope Dilations
children.top_down_role: Dilations of polytopes whose vertices lie in the ambient lattice.

knowledge_statements.title: Lattice-Polytope Dilations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ehrhart theorem for full-dimensional lattice polytopes and nonnegative integral dilations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be a full-dimensional lattice polytope and define \(L_P(n)=|nP\cap\mathbb Z^d|\) for \(n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\). There exists a polynomial \(E_P(t)\in\mathbb Q[t]\) of degree \(d\) such that \(L_P(n)=E_P(n)\) for every \(n\ge0\). Its leading coefficient is the Euclidean volume \(\operatorname{vol}_d(P)\), and its constant coefficient is \(E_P(0)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integral dilations of a full-dimensional lattice polytope have lattice-point counts given by a degree-d polynomial with leading coefficient equal to volume.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is full-dimensional.
Every vertex of \(P\) lies in \(\mathbb Z^d\).
\(n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_P(n)=E_P(n)\), where \(\deg E_P=d\), \([t^d]E_P=\operatorname{vol}_d(P)\), and \(E_P(0)=1\).

notation.meaning: Dilation of P by the nonnegative integer n.
Number of lattice points in nP.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical Ehrhart theorem for lattice polytopes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated full-dimensional lattice-polytope version of Ehrhart's theorem is mathematically standard, correctly classified as a theorem, and consistent across plain text and LaTeX. It nevertheless has no authoritative theorem, section, or page citation.

children.title: Rational-Polytope Dilations
children.top_down_role: Dilations of polytopes with rational vertex coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Rational-Polytope Dilations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ehrhart quasipolynomial theorem for full-dimensional rational polytopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be a full-dimensional rational polytope, and let \(q\) be the least positive integer for which \(qP\) is a lattice polytope. Then \(L_P(n)=|nP\cap\mathbb Z^d|\) is a quasipolynomial of degree \(d\): there exist polynomials \(E_0,\ldots,E_{q-1}\in\mathbb Q[t]\) such that \(L_P(n)=E_r(n)\) whenever \(n\equiv r\pmod q\). The leading coefficient of every constituent is \(\operatorname{vol}_d(P)\); the minimal quasiperiod divides \(q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Counts in integer dilations of a rational polytope form a degree-d quasipolynomial whose period divides the polytope denominator.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is full-dimensional and rational.
\(q\) is the least positive integer such that \(qP\) has integral vertices.
\(n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_P(n)\) is a degree-\(d\) quasipolynomial with period dividing \(q\).

notation.meaning: Denominator of the rational polytope P.
Polynomial constituent for residue class r modulo q.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical rational Ehrhart quasipolynomial theorem

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rational Ehrhart quasipolynomial statement, denominator bound, and leading-coefficient claim fit the leaf and are appropriately classified as a theorem. An authoritative theorem or page locator is absent.

children.title: Integrality–Periodicity Interface
children.top_down_role: Influence of vertex integrality on counting periodicity.

knowledge_statements.title: Integrality–Periodicity Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relationship between vertex integrality, denominator, and Ehrhart quasiperiod.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a full-dimensional rational polytope \(P\), let \(q\) be its denominator and let \(p_P\) be the minimal period of its Ehrhart quasipolynomial. Then \(p_P\mid q\). In particular, if \(P\) is a lattice polytope, then \(q=1\) and \(p_P=1\), so the quasipolynomial is an ordinary polynomial. The converse implication is not generally valid: a rational nonlattice polytope may have \(p_P=1\), a phenomenon called quasiperiod collapse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integrality forces Ehrhart period one, while a rational polytope’s minimal period divides its denominator and may collapse below it.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a full-dimensional rational polytope.
\(q\) and \(p_P\) denote its denominator and minimal Ehrhart period.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_P\mid q\), and \(q=1\Rightarrow p_P=1\), but \(p_P=1\nRightarrow q=1\).

notation.meaning: Least positive dilation making P a lattice polytope.
Minimal period of the Ehrhart quasipolynomial.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: denominator bounds Ehrhart period and period collapse is known

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The period-divisibility and lattice-integrality implications are standard, while the nonconverse invokes the nontrivial phenomenon of quasiperiod collapse. A specific authoritative locator is required, especially for that existence claim.

children.title: Denominator Regimes
children.top_down_role: Dependence of dilation behavior on rational denominators.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a rational polytope.
Dilations are indexed by \(n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_P\) has a residue-class polynomial representation modulo \(q(P)\).

notation.meaning: Least positive integer clearing all vertex denominators of P.
Ehrhart constituent on residue class r.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: rational Ehrhart counts decompose by denominator residue classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residue-class representation of Ehrhart counting controlled by the polytope denominator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rational polytope \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), define its denominator by \(q(P)=\min\{q\in\mathbb Z_{>0}:qP\text{ has integral vertices}\}\). Its dilation count admits the residue-class representation \[L_P(n)=E_r(n)\quad\text{when }n\equiv r\pmod{q(P)},\qquad r=0,\ldots,q(P)-1,\] for polynomial constituents \(E_r\). Thus denominator one gives a single polynomial regime, a fixed denominator gives at most \(q(P)\) constituents, and unbounded denominators permit an unbounded number of residue classes, although the minimal period can be smaller.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polytope denominator indexes polynomial residue-class formulas for dilation counts, while the actual Ehrhart period may be a proper divisor.

children.title: Ehrhart Polynomials
children.top_down_role: Polynomial counting representations associated with lattice polytopes.

knowledge_statements.title: Ehrhart Polynomials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial representation of lattice-point counts for integral dilations of a lattice polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a full-dimensional lattice polytope, its counting function has the unique representation \[L_P(n)=c_d n^d+c_{d-1}n^{d-1}+\cdots+c_1n+c_0\qquad(n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}),\] with \(c_i\in\mathbb Q\), \(c_d=\operatorname{vol}_d(P)\), and \(c_0=1\). Uniqueness follows from agreement at all nonnegative integers, and this polynomial is called the Ehrhart polynomial of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lattice polytope’s dilation counts have a unique rational-coefficient polynomial representation with volume as leading coefficient and constant term one.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a full-dimensional lattice polytope.
\(n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_P(n)=\sum_{i=0}^d c_i n^i\), with \(c_d=\operatorname{vol}_d(P)\) and \(c_0=1\).

notation.meaning: Number of lattice points in the nth dilation of P.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The polynomial representation, uniqueness, leading coefficient, and constant coefficient are mathematically standard and representation is the correct role for this leaf. No authoritative Ehrhart theorem or page locator is supplied.

children.title: Ehrhart Quasipolynomials
children.top_down_role: Periodic-coefficient counting representations associated with rational polytopes.

knowledge_statements.title: Ehrhart Quasipolynomials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ehrhart counting for full-dimensional rational polytopes under nonnegative integral dilation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) be a full-dimensional rational polytope and let \(q\ge 1\) satisfy \(qP\) lattice. Then there exist polynomials \(f_0,\ldots,f_{q-1}\in\mathbb{Q}[t]\), each of degree at most \(d\), such that for every \(n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\), \[L_P(n):=\lvert nP\cap\mathbb{Z}^d\rvert=f_r(n)\quad\text{when }n\equiv r\pmod q.\] Thus \(L_P\) is a quasipolynomial whose period divides \(q\), and every constituent has leading coefficient \(\operatorname{vol}(P)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lattice-point count of every nonnegative integral dilation of a rational polytope is a degree-d quasipolynomial, with period dividing any denominator of the polytope.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is a full-dimensional rational polytope.
\(qP\) has integral vertices for some integer \(q\ge 1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_P(n)=f_{n\bmod q}(n)\), with \(\deg f_r\le d\) and common leading coefficient \(\operatorname{vol}(P)\).

notation.meaning: number of integer lattice points in the dilation nP
a positive denominator clearing all vertex denominators of P

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The full-dimensional rational Ehrhart statement is mathematically standard and fits the theorem role, but no authoritative source or inspectable theorem locator is supplied.

children.title: Polynomial–Quasipolynomial Transition
children.top_down_role: Change in counting representation as vertex integrality is relaxed.

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial–Quasipolynomial Transition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transition caused by vertex denominators, allowing possible period collapse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) be a rational polytope and let \(q\) be the least positive integer for which \(qP\) is a lattice polytope. Ehrhart counting gives a quasipolynomial \(L_P\) with period dividing \(q\). If \(q=1\), then all residue constituents coincide and \(L_P\in\mathbb{Q}[n]\) is a polynomial. For \(q>1\), distinct constituents may occur, although the minimal quasiperiod can be a proper divisor of \(q\), including \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integral vertices force polynomial counting; rational vertices generally produce residue-dependent polynomials, but the actual period may be smaller than the vertex denominator.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is a rational polytope.
\(q\) is the least positive integer such that \(qP\) has integral vertices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q=1\Rightarrow L_P\) is polynomial, while in general the minimal quasiperiod of \(L_P\) divides \(q\).

notation.meaning: the Ehrhart counting function of P

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The transition from polynomial to quasipolynomial counting and the possibility of period collapse fit this property container, but the claims require an authoritative locator.

children.title: Period Structure
children.top_down_role: Periods, constituent behavior, and denominator-sensitive variation.

knowledge_statements.title: Period Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Divisibility and coefficient-period structure of rational Ehrhart quasipolynomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) be a rational polytope of dimension \(d\), with denominator \(q\), and write \(L_P(n)=\sum_{j=0}^{d}c_j(n)n^j\), where each \(c_j\) is periodic. Every coefficient period divides \(q\); hence the minimal quasiperiod of \(L_P\) divides \(q\). The top coefficient is constant, namely \(c_d(n)=\operatorname{vol}_{\operatorname{aff}(P)}(P)\), using lattice-normalized relative volume when \(P\) is not full-dimensional. Equality between the minimal quasiperiod and \(q\) is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficient functions have periods dividing the polytope denominator; the leading coefficient is constant, and period collapse can make the true period smaller.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a rational polytope of dimension \(d\).
\(q\) is the denominator of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{per}(c_j)\mid q\) for all \(j\), and \(c_d\) is the constant relative volume of \(P\).

notation.meaning: periodic coefficient function of degree j
minimal positive period of the coefficient function

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coefficient-period claim needs a source, and the asserted constant leading coefficient is not valid as written for every lower-dimensional rational polytope: dilation residue classes can have different lattice support. A source-backed correction must either impose suitable full-dimensional/lattice-affine hypotheses or state the lower-dimensional behavior precisely.

children.title: Ehrhart Series
children.top_down_role: Generating-series encoding of lattice-point counts across dilations.

knowledge_statements.title: Ehrhart Series
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordinary generating function of lattice-point counts under integral dilation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rational polytope \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^d\), its Ehrhart series is the formal power series \[\operatorname{Ehr}_P(z):=\sum_{n\ge 0}L_P(n)z^n,\qquad L_P(n):=\lvert nP\cap\mathbb{Z}^d\rvert.\] If \(P\) is a \(d\)-dimensional lattice polytope, then \(\operatorname{Ehr}_P(z)\) is rational and has the form \(h_P^*(z)/(1-z)^{d+1}\), where \(h_P^*(z)\) is a polynomial of degree at most \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Ehrhart series packages all dilation counts into one generating function and, for lattice polytopes, has denominator (1-z) raised to dimension plus one.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is a rational polytope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Ehr}_P(z)=\sum_{n\ge0}\lvert nP\cap\mathbb{Z}^d\rvert z^n\); for lattice \(P\), it equals \(h_P^*(z)/(1-z)^{d+1}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generating-function definition and lattice-polytope rational form are standard and fit the container, but neither has a cited source with a specific locator.

children.title: h-Star Polynomials
children.top_down_role: Numerator data associated with Ehrhart-series representations.

knowledge_statements.title: h-Star Polynomials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerator polynomial for the Ehrhart series of a lattice polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) be a \(d\)-dimensional lattice polytope. Its \(h^*\)-polynomial is the unique polynomial \[h_P^*(z):=(1-z)^{d+1}\sum_{n\ge0}\lvert nP\cap\mathbb{Z}^d\rvert z^n=\sum_{i=0}^{d}h_i^*z^i.\] Its coefficients are integers satisfying \(h_i^*\ge0\), \(h_0^*=1\), and \(\sum_{i=0}^{d}h_i^*=d!\operatorname{vol}(P)\), where volume is measured in the ambient lattice normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The h-star polynomial is the Ehrhart-series numerator of a lattice polytope; its coefficients are nonnegative integers and sum to normalized volume.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is a full-dimensional lattice polytope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_P^*(z)=(1-z)^{d+1}\operatorname{Ehr}_P(z)\), with \(h_i^*\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\), \(h_0^*=1\), and \(h_P^*(1)=d!\operatorname{vol}(P)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and stated integrality, nonnegativity, constant-term, and normalized-volume properties are standard for full-dimensional lattice polytopes, but they require an authoritative section or theorem locator.

children.title: Numerator–Series Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Relationship between h-star coefficients and the full dilation-counting series.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerator–Series Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent binomial-basis and rational-series representations for lattice Ehrhart counting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a \(d\)-dimensional lattice polytope \(P\), the identities \[\sum_{n\ge0}L_P(n)z^n=\frac{\sum_{i=0}^{d}h_i^*z^i}{(1-z)^{d+1}}\quad\text{and}\quad L_P(n)=\sum_{i=0}^{d}h_i^*\binom{n+d-i}{d}\] are equivalent, with the convention \(\binom{m}{d}=0\) for integers \(m<d\). Consequently, the numerator coefficients uniquely determine every dilation count, and the counting polynomial uniquely determines the numerator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expanding the rational Ehrhart series converts h-star coefficients into a binomial-basis formula for every lattice-point count, and either representation determines the other.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a \(d\)-dimensional lattice polytope.
\(n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Ehr}_P(z)=h_P^*(z)/(1-z)^{d+1}\) if and only if \(L_P(n)=\sum_i h_i^*\binom{n+d-i}{d}\).

notation.meaning: coefficient of z^i in the h-star polynomial
Ehrhart count of P at n

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The series and binomial-basis formulas are mutually consistent and the representation kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the correspondence.

children.title: Positivity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Geometric and representation regimes affecting coefficient positivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Positivity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the lattice-denominator numerator form for rational nonlattice polytopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Nonnegativity of the coefficients of \((1-z)^{d+1}\operatorname{Ehr}_P(z)\) is tied to the lattice-polytope setting. For the rational interval \(P=[0,1/2]\subset\mathbb{R}\), \(L_P(n)=\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1\) and \[\operatorname{Ehr}_P(z)=\frac{1}{(1-z)(1-z^2)}.\] Hence \((1-z)^2\operatorname{Ehr}_P(z)=1/(1+z)\), which is not a polynomial and has formal expansion \(1-z+z^2-z^3+\cdots\). Thus the usual lattice \(h^*\)-polynomial and its coefficientwise positivity cannot be asserted with denominator \((1-z)^{d+1}\) after dropping integrality of the vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonlattice rational interval, the lattice-style numerator is not polynomial and its expansion alternates, so ordinary h-star positivity does not extend unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(P=[0,1/2]\subset\mathbb{R}\).
Dilations are indexed by \(n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((1-z)^2\operatorname{Ehr}_P(z)=1/(1+z)\notin\mathbb{Z}[z]\), so lattice-style polynomial positivity fails.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The interval calculation correctly exhibits failure of the ordinary lattice-style numerator after dropping vertex integrality and fits a failure-boundary leaf, but the nontrivial boundary claim has no cited source or locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Ehrhart Reciprocity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rational-polytope reciprocity using quasipolynomial evaluation at negative integers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) be a rational polytope of dimension \(d\), let \(P^\circ\) denote its relative interior, and let \(L_P(n)=\lvert nP\cap\mathbb{Z}^d\rvert\) for \(n\ge0\). Extend the Ehrhart quasipolynomial to all integers by evaluating its residue-class constituents. Then for every positive integer \(n\), \[L_P(-n)=(-1)^d\lvert nP^\circ\cap\mathbb{Z}^d\rvert.\] Equivalently, the interior counting quasipolynomial satisfies \(L_{P^\circ}(n)=(-1)^dL_P(-n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluating a rational polytope’s Ehrhart quasipolynomial at negative integers gives, up to a dimension sign, the lattice-point count in the relative interior.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is a rational polytope of dimension \(d\).
\(n\) is a positive integer.

notation.meaning: number of lattice points in n times the relative interior of P

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rational Ehrhart reciprocity statement is appropriately classified as a theorem and is internally consistent, but it lacks an authoritative theorem locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise Quasipolynomial Counting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric lattice-point counts on a finite polyhedral chamber complex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}\) be fixed and suppose \(P_b:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^n:Ax=b\}\) is bounded for every parameter \(b\) under consideration. On the parameter cone \(\operatorname{cone}(A)\), there exists a finite rational polyhedral chamber complex such that, on the lattice points of each relatively open chamber \(C\), the function \[b\longmapsto\lvert P_b\cap\mathbb{Z}^n\rvert\] agrees with a quasipolynomial in the coordinates of \(b\). Values on chamber boundaries may require lower-dimensional pieces and different quasipolynomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed integer matrix with bounded fibers, the number of nonnegative integer solutions is quasipolynomial on each cell of a finite polyhedral chamber complex.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}\) is fixed.
Every considered fiber \(P_b\) is bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b\mapsto\lvert P_b\cap\mathbb{Z}^n\rvert\) is quasipolynomial on lattice points in each chamber.

notation.meaning: nonnegative real fiber defined by Ax=b
cone generated by the columns of A

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Piecewise quasipolynomiality fits the container, but the precise required hypotheses, parameter domain, chamber complex, and treatment of boundary strata depend on the theorem variant and cannot be validated without a source.

knowledge_statements.title: Vector Partition Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counting nonnegative integral representations by columns of a fixed integer matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer matrix \(A=[a_1\ \cdots\ a_n]\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}\), the associated vector partition function is \[\varphi_A(b):=\left\lvert\left\{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}^n:Ax=b\right\}\right\rvert,\qquad b\in\mathbb{Z}^m.\] It is finite whenever the recession cone \(\{x\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^n:Ax=0\}\) is \(\{0\}\). Its support is contained in \(\operatorname{cone}(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\cap\mathbb{Z}^m\), and it is zero outside the affine semigroup generated by the columns of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector partition function counts nonnegative integer combinations of fixed column vectors that equal a parameter vector; pointed fibers ensure the count is finite.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}\) is fixed.
\(b\in\mathbb{Z}^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varphi_A(b)=\lvert\{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}^n:Ax=b\}\rvert\), finite if \(\{x\ge0:Ax=0\}=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: vector partition function associated with A

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The vector partition function is correctly presented as a definition, and the recession-cone finiteness condition is plausible, but the definition and accompanying support claims lack a specific source locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Chamber Decompositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral subdivision governing formulas for parametric vector-partition counts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[a_1\ \cdots\ a_n]\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}\) have rank \(m\), and assume \(\operatorname{cone}(A)\) is pointed. The chamber complex of \(A\) is the common refinement of the simplicial cones \(\operatorname{cone}(a_i:i\in\sigma)\) over all column bases \(\sigma\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with \(|\sigma|=m\) and \(\det(A_\sigma)\ne0\). Its relatively open maximal cells are chambers. Within each chamber, the set of feasible bases for \(Ax=b,\ x\ge0\) is constant, providing the polyhedral domains on which \(\varphi_A(b)\) has a single quasipolynomial formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The chamber complex refines cones spanned by column bases; inside each chamber the feasible-basis pattern is fixed and one vector-partition quasipolynomial applies.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}\) has rank \(m\).
\(\operatorname{cone}(A)\) is pointed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The common refinement partitions \(\operatorname{cone}(A)\) into chambers with constant feasible-basis data.

notation.meaning: submatrix formed by columns indexed by sigma
vector partition function associated with A

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed chamber-complex definition is variant-sensitive, especially the meaning of common refinement and the claim that one quasipolynomial applies on each chamber. An authoritative definition and theorem locator are required.

children.title: Enumeration Output-Complexity Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Explicit enumeration models and their distinction from compact counting representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Integer-Point Enumeration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lexicographic enumeration from an explicitly bounded rational polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input integer data \(A\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times d}\), \(b\in\mathbb{Z}^m\), and finite integer bounds \(\ell,u\in\mathbb{Z}^d\) with \(\ell\le u\), defining \(S:=\{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d:Ax\le b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}\). Initialize \(x:=\ell\). Inspect every vector in the finite box \([\ell,u]\cap\mathbb{Z}^d\) in lexicographic order; output \(x\) exactly when \(Ax\le b\), then advance to the lexicographic successor. Stop after inspecting \(u\). The output contains every point of \(S\) exactly once and no infeasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scan a finite integer box lexicographically, test each point against the inequalities, and output precisely the feasible integer points once each.
assumptions_latex: \(A,b,\ell,u\) are integral and \(\ell\le u\).
The displayed bounds contain every feasible integer point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm terminates and outputs exactly \(S=\{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d:Ax\le b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}\) without duplication.

notation.meaning: bounded set of feasible integer points

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-box scan is a valid terminating enumeration algorithm and makes no unsupported complexity claim, but the candidate supplies no source or algorithm locator.

children.title: Output-Sensitive Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Enumeration complexity measured against total output size.

assumptions_latex: The instance encoding has length \(n\).
Every solution has a finite encoding, and the enumerator outputs each solution exactly once before halting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The enumeration algorithm is output-sensitive precisely when its total running time is bounded by \(p(n+L)\) for some polynomial \(p\).

notation.meaning: total bit length of all emitted solutions
a fixed polynomial independent of the instance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses total encoded output length, rather than merely the number of solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an instance of encoding length \(n\), let \(L\) be the total bit length of the complete, duplicate-free output. An enumeration algorithm is output-sensitive, or output-polynomial, if there exists a polynomial \(p\) such that it halts after at most \(p(n+L)\) computation steps on every instance, including instances with empty output. The polynomial is uniform over all instances in the enumeration problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An enumerator is output-sensitive when its total running time is polynomial in the combined input length and encoded length of all solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Output-Sensitive Enumeration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Output-Sensitive Enumeration leaf, introduces the relevant size parameters, and keeps all TeX commands inside math delimiters. However, no citation or inspectable locator supports the chosen output-polynomial convention, so the candidate requires an authoritative enumeration-complexity source.

children.title: Polynomial-Delay Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Enumeration complexity measured between successive outputs.

assumptions_latex: The instance encoding has length \(n\).
Solutions are emitted without duplication, and termination after the last solution is detectable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The enumerator has polynomial delay when every preprocessing, inter-output, and postprocessing interval is bounded by \(p(n)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes delays before the first output and after the last output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An enumeration algorithm has polynomial delay if some polynomial \(p\) bounds, by \(p(n)\), each of the following intervals: initialization to the first output, two consecutive outputs, and the last output to termination. When no solution exists, initialization to termination is also bounded by \(p(n)\). The bound depends only on input length \(n\), not on the number \(K\) of solutions already produced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial delay bounds the wait before, between, and after outputs by a polynomial depending only on input length.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial-Delay Enumeration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the Polynomial-Delay Enumeration leaf, including initial, inter-output, empty-output, and terminal intervals. No source is cited for this convention, particularly the inclusion of post-output termination delay, so authoritative support with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Delay–Total-Time Comparison
children.top_down_role: Relationship between per-output delay guarantees and aggregate running time.

assumptions_latex: An enumerator has delay at most \(p(n)\) and emits exactly \(K\) solutions.
Writing any one solution takes at most \(q(n)\) steps for a polynomial \(q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Its total running time is at most \((K+1)p(n)+Kq(n)\), hence polynomial in \(n+L\); the reverse implication need not hold.

notation.meaning: input length and number of solutions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares uniform polynomial delay with total output-polynomial time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an enumerator produces \(K\) solutions with delay at most \(p(n)\), including initial and terminal delay, and writing each solution costs at most \(q(n)\), then its total time is at most \((K+1)p(n)+Kq(n)\). Since \(K\leq L+1\) for nonempty finite encodings, this is polynomial in \(n+L\). Output-polynomial total time alone does not bound each individual delay by a polynomial in \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial delay implies output-polynomial total time, but an output-polynomial total bound does not necessarily control each wait between solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Delay–Total-Time Comparison

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The comparison is appropriately a property and expresses the standard implication from polynomial delay to output-polynomial total time. Its use of a bound relating the solution count to total encoded output length depends on a nonempty or self-delimiting output-encoding convention that is not fully established by the assumptions, and neither the implication nor the strict converse is cited. A source fixing these conventions is required.

children.title: Output-Size Regimes
children.top_down_role: Behavior when represented sets have small, large, or exponentially large output.

assumptions_latex: The input length is \(n\), the solution count is \(K(n)\), and every emitted solution uses at least one symbol.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Explicit enumeration requires \(\Omega(K(n))\) output operations; it can be input-polynomial only when \(K(n)\) is polynomially bounded.

notation.meaning: number of solutions for an input of length n

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates polynomial-output and superpolynomial-output instance families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a sequential output model, emitting \(K(n)\) distinct solutions of total encoding length \(L(n)\) requires \(\Omega(L(n))\) time and therefore \(\Omega(K(n))\) time. If \(K(n)\leq n^c\) and each solution has polynomial length, output-polynomial enumeration may also be input-polynomial. If \(K(n)\) is superpolynomial, no explicit complete enumerator can have total running time polynomial solely in \(n\), irrespective of its internal counting method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomially many short outputs permit input-polynomial enumeration; superpolynomially many outputs impose a matching output-time lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Output-Size Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits Output-Size Regimes, and the sequential-output lower bound is mathematically plausible under the stated positive-length encoding model. No source with a specific locator supports the output-size lower bound or the claimed regime comparison, so the record remains source-dependent.

assumptions_latex: Output is written to a one-way stream and need not remain in working memory.
The instance encoding has length \(n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The enumerator is polynomial-space when its working storage is at most \(p(n)\), independently of the number or total length of previously emitted solutions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts mutable workspace but excludes read-only input and write-only output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A streaming enumeration algorithm is polynomial-space if a polynomial \(p\) satisfies \(S(n)\leq p(n)\) on every instance of length \(n\), where \(S(n)\) counts mutable working storage but excludes the read-only input and the write-only output stream. The bound must not depend on the number or total encoding length of solutions already emitted; retaining all prior outputs therefore generally violates this requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial-space enumeration uses workspace polynomial in input length, excluding read-only input and write-only output, regardless of accumulated output size.
knowledge_statements.title: Space-Sensitive Enumeration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits Space-Sensitive Enumeration and explicitly distinguishes workspace from read-only input and write-only output. That exclusion is a computational-model convention, and the claim about retaining prior outputs also depends on representation and access assumptions. No authoritative source or locator is supplied.

assumptions_latex: The finite lattice set is \(F\subset\mathbb{Z}^d\).
A representation of \(f(\mathbf z)=\sum_{\mathbf a\in F}\mathbf z^{\mathbf a}\) supports exact regularized specialization at \(\mathbf z=\mathbf 1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cardinality is \(|F|=f(\mathbf 1)\), interpreted through regularized evaluation when the representation has singular summands.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Addresses exact cardinality extraction from a compact generating-function representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite set \(F\subset\mathbb Z^d\), its generating polynomial \(f(\mathbf z)=\sum_{\,\mathbf a\in F}\mathbf z^{\mathbf a}\) satisfies \(f(\mathbf 1)=|F|\). Thus an exact compact representation that permits addition and regularized specialization can determine \(|F|\) without emitting the elements of \(F\). This avoids the \(\Omega(|F|)\) explicit-output cost, although representation construction and specialization may still be computationally expensive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite lattice set can be counted by evaluating its generating polynomial at all ones, without listing its points, provided singular terms are regularized.
knowledge_statements.title: Counting Without Explicit Enumeration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits Counting Without Explicit Enumeration and correctly distinguishes the generating polynomial identity from evaluation of a compact rational presentation. The asserted availability and correctness of exact regularized specialization, and the resulting avoidance of explicit enumeration, need a generating-function source with a specific locator.

children.title: Generating-Function Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Representation, projection, specialization, and explicit-output boundaries.

children.title: Singular Specializations
children.top_down_role: Variable substitutions that place rational terms at singular points.

assumptions_latex: A rational representation contains a denominator factor \(1-\mathbf z^{\mathbf b}\) with \(\mathbf b\neq\mathbf 0\).
The specialization satisfies \(\mathbf z^{\mathbf b}=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termwise substitution is undefined even when cancellation makes the represented total function finite at the specialization.

notation.meaning: nonzero exponent vector in a denominator

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies failure of direct substitution into short rational generating functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R(\mathbf z)=\sum_j r_j(\mathbf z)\), where some summand has denominator divisible by \(1-\mathbf z^{\mathbf b}\). At a point \(\boldsymbol\zeta\) satisfying \(\boldsymbol\zeta^{\mathbf b}=1\), direct evaluation of that summand is undefined. This does not imply that \(R\) is singular: for example, \((1-z^N)/(1-z)=1+z+\cdots+z^{N-1}\) has a removable singularity at \(z=1\) and value \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rational summand may be undefined at a specialization although cancellations make the represented generating function finite there.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular Specializations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits Singular Specializations, and the removable-singularity example correctly shows why termwise substitution can fail. No source or inspectable locator is supplied for this generating-function specialization failure boundary.

children.title: Pole Cancellation
children.top_down_role: Cancellation of singularities across collections of rational terms.

assumptions_latex: Each \(r_j(t)\) is meromorphic near \(t=0\) with a finite principal part.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sum \(R(t)=\sum_j r_j(t)\) is holomorphic at \(0\) exactly when \(\sum_j c_{j,k}=0\) for every \(k<0\).

notation.meaning: Laurent coefficient of degree k in summand j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States pole cancellation through vanishing Laurent principal parts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write the Laurent expansions \(r_j(t)=\sum_{k=-m_j}^{\infty}c_{j,k}t^k\) near \(t=0\). Their sum \(R(t)=\sum_j r_j(t)\) has a removable singularity at \(0\) if and only if \(\sum_j c_{j,k}=0\) for every negative integer \(k\). Under this condition, the regular value is the combined constant coefficient \(R(0)=\sum_j c_{j,0}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Poles cancel exactly when every negative-degree coefficient in the combined Laurent expansion vanishes; the regular value is the combined constant coefficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Pole Cancellation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Laurent-principal-part criterion fits Pole Cancellation and is correct for a finite sum of meromorphic summands. The record does not explicitly state that the index set of summands is finite or otherwise justify coefficientwise summation, and it supplies no authoritative source. A source fixing the intended finite rational-sum setting is required before the mathematical scope can be accepted.

children.title: Regularized Evaluation Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Symbolic interfaces for extracting finite aggregate values near singular specializations.

assumptions_latex: The rational expression represents a function regular at the target point \(\boldsymbol\zeta\).
A direction \(\boldsymbol\lambda\) is chosen so substituted denominator factors are not identically zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After summing Laurent expansions, return the coefficient of \(t^0\), which equals the regular value at \(\boldsymbol\zeta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses a generic one-parameter perturbation and constant-term extraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a rational sum \(R(\mathbf z)=\sum_j r_j(\mathbf z)\), a regular target \(\boldsymbol\zeta\), and a generic direction \(\boldsymbol\lambda\). Substitute \(z_i=\zeta_i e^{\lambda_i t}\). Expand every resulting summand as a Laurent series through degree \(0\), add the truncated series, and verify that all coefficients of \(t^k\) for \(k<0\) vanish. Stop with failure if they do not; otherwise output the coefficient of \(t^0\), equal to \(R(\boldsymbol\zeta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perturb the singular point generically, combine Laurent expansions, verify cancellation of negative powers, and return the constant term.
knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Evaluation Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Regularized Evaluation Interfaces, but the stated substitution requires additional domain conditions, such as nonzero target coordinates when multiplicative exponential perturbation is used, and a finite pole-order bound sufficient to compute every needed Laurent coefficient through degree zero. The meaning of a generic direction is also not formalized. An authoritative source is needed to determine the correct hypotheses and algorithmic interface.

children.title: Cancellation Failure Modes
children.top_down_role: Representation, precision, or simplification conditions that obstruct reliable cancellation.

assumptions_latex: The rational presentation is evaluated term by term at a common pole without symbolic combination or regularization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Individual undefined values cannot be combined to recover the finite value of the represented function.

notation.meaning: positive integer controlling the finite polynomial

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete removable-singularity example showing why separate substitution fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(N\geq1\), take \(r_1(z)=1/(1-z)\) and \(r_2(z)=-z^N/(1-z)\). Neither \(r_1(1)\) nor \(r_2(1)\) exists, so termwise substitution produces no valid arithmetic result. Nevertheless, \(R(z)=r_1(z)+r_2(z)=(1-z^N)/(1-z)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}z^k\), and hence the regular value is \(R(1)=N\). Cancellation must occur before evaluation or through an equivalent regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two individually singular rational terms can sum to a finite polynomial, so evaluating them separately at the pole loses the correct value.
knowledge_statements.title: Cancellation Failure Modes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample role is appropriate for Cancellation Failure Modes, and the displayed pair of singular summands correctly combines into a polynomial with value N at one. No citation with a specific locator supports its use as the intended generating-function cancellation failure example.

assumptions_latex: The integer \(M\geq2\) is encoded in binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A quasipolynomial may have exact period \(M\), so listing all residue-class constituents can require \(\Omega(M)\) output despite an \(O(\log M)\)-bit parameter.

notation.meaning: ordinary generating function of the sequence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows exponential explicit constituent output relative to binary period encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(q_M(t)=1\) when \(M\mid t\) and \(q_M(t)=0\) otherwise, for \(t\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\). This degree-zero quasipolynomial has exact period \(M\) and compact generating function \(Q_M(z)=1/(1-z^M)\). An explicit residue-class presentation must distinguish all \(M\) classes and therefore has size \(\Omega(M)\), which is exponential in the binary input length \(\Theta(\log M)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary-encoded period can be exponentially smaller than the explicit list of a quasipolynomial's residue-class constituents.
knowledge_statements.title: Large-Period Quasipolynomials

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The example has exact period M and compact generating function, so it is relevant to Large-Period Quasipolynomials. However, the Omega(M) conclusion holds for a presentation that explicitly lists one constituent or slot for every residue class; it does not hold for every possible explicit symbolic presentation, since the divisibility condition itself is compact. A source must specify the output representation model and support the lower-bound interpretation.

assumptions_latex: Projected lattice points are required as an explicit duplicate-free list.
Dimension \(n\) is part of the input.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projection can yield \(2^n\) distinct lattice points from an \(O(n)\)-size inequality description, forcing exponential explicit-output time.

notation.meaning: compact polytope in twice the dimension

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concerns explicit projected lattice-point output, not merely membership or counting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_n=\{(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\in\mathbb R^{2n}:0\leq x_i\leq1,\ y_i=x_i\text{ for }1\leq i\leq n\}\), described by \(O(n)\) inequalities and equations. Projection onto the \(\mathbf x\)-coordinates gives \(\pi_x(P_n\cap\mathbb Z^{2n})=\{0,1\}^n\), containing \(2^n\) points. Consequently, any algorithm required to materialize this projection as a duplicate-free explicit list takes \(\Omega(2^n)\) output operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linearly described lattice set can project to exponentially many distinct points, making explicit projected output exponentially large.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Complexity Explosion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The construction correctly has an O(n)-size description and projects its integer points onto the 2^n binary vectors, making the explicit-output lower bound plausible. The example shows exponentially large projected output but not an increase caused uniquely by projection, since the unprojected lattice set already has the same cardinality. A source and precise scope are required to establish that this is the intended Projection Complexity Explosion phenomenon.

assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}\)
\(P_m=[0,2^m]\subset\mathbb{R}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_m(z)\) has a rational representation of size \(O(m)\), whereas its expanded monomial representation has \(2^m+1\) terms.

notation.meaning: Lattice-point generating function of the interval

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary geometric-series family exhibiting exponential explicit output
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A one-dimensional family separating short rational representations from expanded output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}\), the binary encoding of \(P_m=[0,2^m]\) has length \(O(m)\), and its lattice-point generating function satisfies \[f_m(z)=1+z+\cdots+z^{2^m}=\frac{1-z^{2^m+1}}{1-z}.\] The rational expression uses exponents with \(O(m)\) bits, but explicit monomial output contains \(2^m+1\) distinct terms. Consequently, any algorithm required to list every monomial needs \(\Omega(2^m)\) output operations, even though a short rational representation is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interval with an m-bit endpoint has a short rational generating function but exponentially many monomials, so explicit expansion cannot run in polynomial time.
knowledge_statements.title: Explicit-Output Explosion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The elementary geometric-series example and failure-boundary classification are correct, but no inspectable source with a specific locator is supplied.
