children.title: Witness-Bound Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Elementary evidence objects used as components of broader integer optimality and infeasibility certificates.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{Z}^{r\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{Z}^r\)
\(x\in\mathbb{Z}^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Checking \(Ax\le b\) certifies that \(\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^n:Az\le b\}\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A direct witness for feasibility of a rationally encoded pure integer linear system.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 10. Sizes and the theoretical complexity of linear inequalities and linear programming p. 120
source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the integer linear system \(X=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^n:Az\le b\}\), an integer vector \(x\) is a feasibility certificate precisely when \(Ax\le b\). Given the binary encodings of \(A\), \(b\), and \(x\), integrality and every inequality can be verified using a number of bit operations polynomial in \(\langle A,b\rangle+\langle x\rangle\). Thus a polynomial-length feasible vector is an NP witness for nonemptiness of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An encoded integer vector satisfying every inequality is a directly checkable certificate that the integer linear system is feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Integer Feasibility Witnesses

knowledge_statements.title: LP Dual-Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality certificates inherited from the continuous LP relaxation of a minimization ILP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) over integer vectors satisfying \(Ax\ge b\). Any rational vector \(y\ge0\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}y=c\) is an LP dual-bound certificate for \(\beta=b^{\mathsf T}y\): every feasible integer vector \(x\) satisfies \(c^{\mathsf T}x\ge\beta\). The equalities, signs, and value of \(\beta\) are verifiable by rational arithmetic in time polynomial in the combined binary encoding length. This certificate establishes a lower bound but does not certify integer feasibility or attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible dual solution of the LP relaxation certifies a lower bound on every integer feasible objective value by weak duality.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{Q}^{r\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{Q}^r\), \(c\in\mathbb{Q}^n\)
\(y\in\mathbb{Q}_{\ge0}^r\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}y=c\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(x\in\mathbb{Z}^n\) satisfying \(Ax\ge b\) obeys \(c^{\mathsf T}x\ge b^{\mathsf T}y\).

\(x^0,r\in\mathbb{Z}^n\)
\(Ax^0\le b\), \(Ar\le0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}r>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^0+kr\) is feasible for every \(k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}(x^0+kr)\to+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A base point plus an integral improving recession direction for a maximization ILP.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the problem of maximizing \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax\le b\) and \(x\in\mathbb{Z}^n\), a pair \((x^0,r)\in\mathbb{Z}^n\times\mathbb{Z}^n\) is an unboundedness witness when \(Ax^0\le b\), \(Ar\le0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}r>0\). For every \(k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\), \(x^0+kr\) is then integral and feasible, while \(c^{\mathsf T}(x^0+kr)=c^{\mathsf T}x^0+k c^{\mathsf T}r\) diverges to \(+\infty\).

children.title: Small-Solution Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence based on bounded-magnitude feasible or optimal integer solutions.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{Z}^{r\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{Z}^r\)
\(X=\{x\in\mathbb{Z}^n:Ax\le b\}\neq\varnothing\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(x^*\in X\) with \(\langle x^*\rangle\le p(\langle A,b\rangle)\) for a universal polynomial \(p\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial binary size, rather than polynomial numerical magnitude, is the relevant smallness notion.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 10. Sizes and the theoretical complexity of linear inequalities and linear programming p. 120
source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There is a polynomial \(p\) such that, for every binary-encoded integral system \(Ax\le b\), nonemptiness of \(X=\{x\in\mathbb{Z}^n:Ax\le b\}\) implies the existence of \(x^*\in X\) satisfying \(\langle x^*\rangle\le p(\langle A,b\rangle)\). Hence feasibility has a certificate whose coordinates may be numerically large but whose total binary representation is polynomial in the instance length. Substitution of \(x^*\) into the inequalities verifies the certificate in polynomial bit time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every feasible rationally encoded integer linear system has some feasible integer point whose binary description is polynomial in the input length.
knowledge_statements.title: Small-Solution Certificates

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 10. Sizes and the theoretical complexity of linear inequalities and linear programming p. 120

children.title: Encoding-Length Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence that relevant objects admit bounded binary representations.

assumptions_latex: \(I=(A,b)\) is a binary-encoded integer linear system
\(x\in\mathbb{Z}^n\) and \(Ax\le b\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\langle x\rangle\le p(\langle I\rangle)\), then \(x\) is a polynomial-length, polynomial-time verifiable feasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate length measured under standard binary encoding of signed integers and rational input data.

source_refs.locator: 1.3.1 Problems, Instances, Encoding Size p. 17

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L=\langle I\rangle\) be the binary length of an integer linear feasibility instance \(I=(A,b)\). A feasible vector \(x\in\mathbb{Z}^n\) is an encoding-length certificate when \(\langle x\rangle\le p(L)\) for a fixed polynomial \(p\). Its sign bits and binary digits form the certificate string. Integer arithmetic verifies \(Ax\le b\) in time polynomial in \(L+\langle x\rangle\); therefore the polynomial length condition makes both reading and checking the witness polynomial in the instance size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible vector is a polynomial certificate when its binary encoding, including signs and all coordinates, has polynomial length in the input size.
knowledge_statements.title: Encoding-Length Certificates

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3.1 Problems, Instances, Encoding Size p. 17

children.title: Size–Encoding Relationship
children.top_down_role: Connection between numerical magnitude and certificate bit length.

assumptions_latex: \(z=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)\in\mathbb{Z}^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle z\rangle=\Theta\!\left(n+\sum_{i=1}^n\log_2(|z_i|+1)\right)\).

notation.meaning: Signed binary length of an integer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard signed binary encoding, up to fixed separators and dimension metadata.

source_refs.locator: 1.3.1 Problems, Instances, Encoding Size p. 17

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under signed binary encoding, define \(\ell(t)=1+\lceil\log_2(|t|+1)\rceil\) for \(t\in\mathbb{Z}\), and encode \(z=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)\) using its coordinate encodings and separators. Then \[\langle z\rangle=\Theta\!\left(n+\sum_{i=1}^n\log_2(|z_i|+1)\right).\] Consequently, a bound \(|z_i|\le2^{p(L)}\) for all coordinates and polynomially bounded \(n\) yields polynomial encoding length, while polynomial numerical magnitude is sufficient but not necessary for polynomial-length representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary length grows logarithmically with coordinate magnitude, so exponentially large coordinates can still have polynomial-size encodings.
knowledge_statements.title: Size–Encoding Relationship

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3.1 Problems, Instances, Encoding Size p. 17

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial-size integral feasible witness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of a polynomial-bit-length integer feasibility certificate for a rational linear inequality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{Q}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{Q}^m\), and let \(L\) be the maximum encoding size of the coefficients of \((A,b)\). If \(Ax\le b\) has an integral solution, then it has an integral solution \(\bar{x}\) whose encoding size is bounded by a polynomial in \(n\) and \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a rational linear inequality system has an integer solution, then it has one whose encoding size is polynomially bounded in the number of variables and the maximum coefficient encoding size.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb{Q}^{m\times n},\quad b\in\mathbb{Q}^m

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the deterministic bit model, an explicit certificate containing an integer \(z\) cannot be read in time polynomial in input length \(L\) unless \(\ell(z)=L^{O(1)}\). Values satisfying \(|z|\le2^{L^{O(1)}}\) remain compatible with polynomial certificate length. By contrast, if \(|z|\ge2^{2^{\Omega(L)}}\), then \(\ell(z)=2^{\Omega(L)}\), so merely reading the explicit binary representation requires exponential time. Thus numerical magnitude and bit complexity must not be conflated.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Doignon’s integer infeasibility theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-dependent small-subsystem certificate for infeasibility over the integer lattice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_i\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\beta_i\in\mathbb{R}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). If \(\{x\in\mathbb{Z}^n:a_i^\top x\leq\beta_i\text{ for all }i=1,\ldots,m\}=\varnothing\), then there exists \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) with \(|I|\leq 2^n\) such that \(\{x\in\mathbb{Z}^n:a_i^\top x\leq\beta_i\text{ for all }i\in I\}=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a finite system of linear inequalities in n variables has no integer solution, at most 2^n of its inequalities already form a subsystem with no integer solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Subsystem Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-family Doignon theorem for convex sets tested against the full integer lattice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\) and \(m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}\), and let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) be convex subsets of \(\mathbb{R}^n\). If \[\left(\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i\right)\cap\mathbb{Z}^n=\varnothing,\] then there exists an index set \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) with \(|I|\le2^n\) such that \[\left(\bigcap_{i\in I}C_i\right)\cap\mathbb{Z}^n=\varnothing.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If finitely many convex sets in n-dimensional space have no common integer point, at most 2^n of them already have no common integer point.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\) and \(m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}\)
\(C_1,\ldots,C_m\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) are convex
\(\left(\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i\right)\cap\mathbb{Z}^n=\varnothing\)

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Helly Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed-integer Helly theorem with continuous dimension \(d\) and integer dimension \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d,k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\), \(m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}\), and \(S=\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{Z}^k\). Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) be convex subsets of \(\mathbb{R}^{d+k}\). If \[\left(\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i\right)\cap S=\varnothing,\] then there exists an index set \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) with \(|I|\le(d+1)2^k\) such that \[\left(\bigcap_{i\in I}C_i\right)\cap S=\varnothing.\] This specializes to ordinary Helly's theorem when \(k=0\) and Doignon's lattice theorem when \(d=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If finitely many convex sets have no common point in the mixed-integer set R^d times Z^k, at most (d+1)2^k of them already have no such common point.

children.title: Lattice Obstructions
children.top_down_role: Infeasibility evidence arising from incompatibility with an integer lattice.

knowledge_statements.title: Lattice Obstructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite-group separator for nonmembership in an integer matrix's column lattice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the integer equation \(Bx=b\) with \(B\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{Z}^m\), and \(x\in\mathbb{Z}^n\), and let \(L=B\mathbb{Z}^n\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^m\). A lattice-obstruction certificate consists of a finite abelian group \(G\) and a homomorphism \(\phi:\mathbb{Z}^m\to G\) satisfying \(\phi(Bz)=0_G\) for every \(z\in\mathbb{Z}^n\) and \(\phi(b)\ne0_G\). These conditions certify \(b\notin L\), and hence certify that \(Bx=b\) has no integer solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-group homomorphism that annihilates the matrix's column lattice but not the right-hand side certifies that the integer equation has no solution.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}\)
\(B\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{Z}^m\)
\(L=B\mathbb{Z}^n\)
\(G\) is a finite abelian group
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A homomorphism \(\phi:\mathbb{Z}^m\to G\) with \(\phi(L)=\{0_G\}\) and \(\phi(b)\ne0_G\) certifies \(b\notin L\).

notation.meaning: Column lattice generated by the matrix

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary separating homomorphism for column-lattice nonmembership

children.title: Congruence Obstructions
children.top_down_role: Infeasibility evidence arising from incompatible modular residue conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Congruence Obstructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A modular separator for infeasibility of an integer equality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the integer equality system \(Ax=b\), a congruence-obstruction certificate consists of \(u\in\mathbb{Z}^m\) and \(q\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge2}\) satisfying \[u^{\mathsf T}A\equiv0\pmod q\qquad\text{and}\qquad u^{\mathsf T}b\not\equiv0\pmod q.\] These conditions certify that \(Ax=b\) has no solution in \(\mathbb{Z}^n\). They are checkable by modular matrix-vector arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A row combination divisible by q on every matrix column but not on the right-hand side certifies that the integer equality system has no solution.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}\)
\(A\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{Z}^m\)
\(u\in\mathbb{Z}^m\), \(q\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge2}\)
\(u^{\mathsf T}A\equiv0\pmod q\) and \(u^{\mathsf T}b\not\equiv0\pmod q\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The system \(Ax=b\) has no solution \(x\in\mathbb{Z}^n\).

children.title: Obstruction Composition
children.top_down_role: Combination of lattice and residue evidence into composite certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Obstruction Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition of integral equations into a modular inconsistency certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb Z^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb Z^m\), and \(m_0\ge 2\). An obstruction-composition certificate is a vector \(y\in\mathbb Z^m\) satisfying \(y^{\mathsf T}A\equiv 0\pmod {m_0}\) and \(y^{\mathsf T}b\not\equiv 0\pmod {m_0}\). Every integer solution of \(Ax=b\) would imply \(y^{\mathsf T}Ax=y^{\mathsf T}b\); the left side is divisible by \(m_0\), whereas the right side is not. Thus the certificate, verifiable by integer arithmetic, proves that \(\{x\in\mathbb Z^n:Ax=b\}=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integer combination of equations proves infeasibility when all combined variable coefficients vanish modulo a modulus but the combined right-hand side does not.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb Z^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb Z^m\)
\(m_0\in\mathbb Z,\ m_0\ge 2\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in\mathbb Z^n:Ax=b\}=\varnothing\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The modular obstruction is mathematically sound and the certificate kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied. The statement also contains a proof-style derivation, which should be removed when a sourced replacement is prepared.

children.title: Completeness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Instances where arithmetic obstructions alone do not certify infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Completeness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of certificates based only on affine-lattice and congruence inconsistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Congruence-composition certificates are complete for detecting inconsistency of an integer linear system only when some modulus and integer row combination expose the inconsistency; they are not complete for general integer inequalities. For example, \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R:0<x<1\}\) satisfies \(P\cap\mathbb Z=\varnothing\), but its infeasibility is caused by order inequalities rather than an inconsistent affine equation or a prescribed congruence. Consequently, a certificate language restricted to composed equalities and congruences requires additional lattice-free, cutting-plane, or exhaustive-enumeration mechanisms for general integer infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine and congruence obstructions cannot certify every infeasible integer inequality system; order or convexity may be the sole source of infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is described by integer equalities, congruences, or inequalities
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\cap\mathbb Z^n=\varnothing\) need not admit an equality-congruence obstruction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the asserted completeness boundary has no source. The example uses strict inequalities, whereas standard rational integer-programming systems are generally presented with non-strict inequalities, so a source-backed formulation is needed before fixing the exact boundary claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Lattice-Free Convexity Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex containment certificate for absence of integer feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the continuous feasible region. A lattice-free convexity certificate consists of a convex set \(L\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) such that \(\operatorname{int}(L)\cap\mathbb Z^n=\varnothing\) and \(P\subseteq\operatorname{int}(L)\). These two verifiable claims imply \(P\cap\mathbb Z^n=\varnothing\). Containment merely in \(L\) is insufficient, because integer points may lie on \(\partial L\); alternatively, a certificate may use a strongly lattice-free set satisfying \(L\cap\mathbb Z^n=\varnothing\) together with \(P\subseteq L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Containing the feasible region in the interior of a lattice-free convex set certifies integer infeasibility; boundary containment alone is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: \(P,L\subseteq\mathbb R^n\)
\(L\) is convex
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\cap\mathbb Z^n=\varnothing\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The set-theoretic implication is correct and the certificate kind fits the topic, but no source is supplied and the representation under which convex containment and lattice-freeness are verifiable is not specified. A source-backed certificate regime is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Cutting-Plane Refutations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite valid-cut derivation ending in an empty relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=P_0\cap\mathbb Z^n\), where \(P_0\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a rational polyhedron. A cutting-plane refutation is a finite sequence \(P_t=P_{t-1}\cap\{x:a_t^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta_t\}\) for \(t=1,\ldots,T\), where every cut is valid for \(P_{t-1}\cap\mathbb Z^n\), together with a rational infeasibility certificate for \(P_T=\varnothing\). Validity preserves all integer feasible points, so emptiness of the terminal relaxation certifies \(S=\varnothing\). Verification additionally requires a checkable derivation of each cut's validity in the selected cutting-plane system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite sequence of integer-valid cuts refutes feasibility when its final rational relaxation is empty and every cut has a checkable derivation.
assumptions_latex: \(P_0\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a rational polyhedron
\(a_t\in\mathbb Q^n,\ \beta_t\in\mathbb Q\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_0\cap\mathbb Z^n=\varnothing\)

children.title: Branching Refutations

knowledge_statements.title: Branching Refutations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exhaustive disjunction tree with infeasible leaves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=P\cap\mathbb Z^n\). A branching refutation is a finite rooted tree whose root region is \(P\). At each internal node with region \(Q\), its children have regions \(Q\cap D_1,\ldots,Q\cap D_k\), where \(Q\cap\mathbb Z^n\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^k D_i\). Every leaf carries a verifiable certificate that its region contains no integer point, commonly an LP infeasibility certificate. Exhaustiveness of every branch disjunction and infeasibility of every leaf together certify \(S=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exhaustive finite branching tree proves integer infeasibility when every leaf is independently certified infeasible.

\(D_1,\ldots,D_k\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) cover all integer points at their node

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb Q^m\), \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\), and \(S=P\cap\mathbb Z^n\). An enumeration refutation consists of a finite set \(E\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\), a verifiable covering claim \(S\subseteq E\), and, for every \(z\in E\), an index \(i(z)\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) satisfying \(a_{i(z)}^{\mathsf T}z>b_{i(z)}\), where \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\) is row \(i\) of \(A\). These data certify \(S=\varnothing\). A finite list without a certified covering claim is not an enumeration refutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumeration certifies infeasibility when a finite list covers every integer candidate and a specified violated constraint excludes every listed point.

children.title: Tree-Size Measures
children.top_down_role: Size, depth, and branching-width measures for refutation trees.

knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Size Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Syntactic size parameters for branching-refutation certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite rooted refutation tree \(T\), its node size is \(|V(T)|\), its leaf size is \(|\mathcal L(T)|\), and its depth is \(\max_{v\in\mathcal L(T)}\operatorname{dist}(r,v)\), where \(r\) is the root. Its encoded certificate size is the total bit length of the tree topology, branch descriptions, node regions, and leaf witnesses. For binary full trees, \(|V(T)|=2|\mathcal L(T)|-1\); depth alone does not control total size, since a binary tree of depth \(d\) may have \(2^d\) leaves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refutation trees are measured by nodes, leaves, depth, or total encoding length; depth can be exponentially smaller than leaf count.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a finite rooted tree
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|V(T)|,\ |\mathcal L(T)|,\ \operatorname{depth}(T)\), and encoded bit length are distinct size measures

children.title: Incumbent Certificates
children.top_down_role: Feasibility and objective-value evidence for a claimed incumbent solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal feasible-point certificate for a minimization integer program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(z^*=\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in S\}\), where \(S=\{x\in\mathbb Z^n:Ax\le b\}\). An incumbent certificate is a vector \(\bar x\in\mathbb Z^n\) for which direct arithmetic verifies \(A\bar x\le b\). Its certified value is \(U=c^{\mathsf T}\bar x\), and feasibility implies \(z^*\le U\). The incumbent alone does not certify optimality unless it is paired with a valid global lower bound that closes the optimality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible integer point certifies an attainable objective value and hence an upper bound for minimization, but not optimality by itself.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb Q^m,\ c\in\mathbb Q^n\)
\(S\ne\varnothing\) and the minimum is finite
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^*\le U=c^{\mathsf T}\bar x\)

children.title: Global-Bound Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence supporting a valid global bound on the objective.

assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) is nonempty
\(z^*=\min_{x\in S}c^{\mathsf T}x\) is finite
\(J\) is a finite nonempty index set when node bounds are used

source_refs.locator: 1.1 Integer Programming p. 1

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) be nonempty and let \(z^*=\min_{x\in S}c^{\mathsf T}x\) be finite. A global-bound certificate establishes a scalar \(L\in\mathbb R\) such that \(c^{\mathsf T}x\ge L\) for every \(x\in S\). One form is a checkable lower-bound certificate satisfying \(L\le\inf_{x\in R}c^{\mathsf T}x\) for a relaxation \(R\supseteq S\). Another uses a finite nonempty index set \(J\), an exhaustive cover \(S\subseteq\bigcup_{j\in J}S_j\), and checkable local bounds \(c^{\mathsf T}x\ge L_j\) for every \(x\in S_j\), with \(L=\min_{j\in J}L_j\). Either form certifies \(L\le z^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global lower-bound certificate proves that every feasible solution costs at least the stated value, either through a certified relaxation bound or through bounds on a finite exhaustive cover.

children.title: Gap-Closure Interface
children.top_down_role: Combination of incumbent values with global bounds to establish optimality.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap-Closure Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface joining primal incumbency and global dual bounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem with optimal value \(z^*\), suppose an incumbent certificate gives \(z^*\le U\) and a global-bound certificate gives \(L\le z^*\). Exact gap closure is the condition \(U-L=0\), which yields \(L=z^*=U\) and certifies the incumbent as optimal. For an absolute tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), the condition \(U-L\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(c^{\mathsf T}\bar x-z^*\le\varepsilon\). Any relative-gap convention additionally requires its denominator and zero-value convention to be stated explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching valid primal and global bounds certifies exact optimality; a gap within a stated tolerance certifies approximate optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(L\le z^*\le U\)
\(\varepsilon\ge0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U=L\Rightarrow z^*=U\), and \(U-L\le\varepsilon\Rightarrow U-z^*\le\varepsilon\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which relaxation or node bounds become globally valid.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Disjunctive Programming and Its Relation to Integer Programming p. 1

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization over a nonempty set \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), a scalar \(L\in\mathbb R\) is globally valid exactly when \(c^{\mathsf T}x\ge L\) for every \(x\in S\). If \(R\supseteq S\), a relaxation certificate yields a globally valid bound when it verifies \(L\le\inf_{x\in R}c^{\mathsf T}x\). Let \(J\) be finite and nonempty. If each \(L_j\) satisfies \(c^{\mathsf T}x\ge L_j\) for every \(x\in S_j\), then \(\min_{j\in J}L_j\) is globally valid whenever \(S\subseteq\bigcup_{j\in J}S_j\). A bound from a nonexhaustive branch, a relaxation that excludes feasible points, or an unverified local model is not thereby a global bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation lower bound is global only when the relaxation contains the feasible set and the bound is certified for that relaxation; local bounds combine through the minimum over a finite exhaustive cover.

knowledge_statements.title: Test-Set Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality certificate for a linear integer program over a fixed fiber using a certified directed test set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}^n:Ax=b\}\) and consider \(\min\{c^\top x:x\in F\}\). A finite set \(G\subseteq\ker_{\mathbb Z}(A)\) is a directed test set if every nonoptimal \(x\in F\) admits \(g\in G\) satisfying \(x-g\in F\) and \(c^\top g>0\). Given a certified test set \(G\), a feasible point \(x^*\) has a test-set optimality certificate when no \(g\in G\) satisfies \(x^*-g\ge 0\) and \(c^\top g>0\). The defining test-set property then certifies that \(x^*\) is globally optimal.

\(G\) is independently certified to be a directed test set for \((A,c)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Based Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite certificate combining a feasible incumbent, validity derivations for cuts, and an LP objective bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X=\{x\in\mathbb Z^p\times\mathbb R^{n-p}:Ax\ge b\}\), consider \(z^*=\min\{c^\top x:x\in X\}\). A cut-based certificate for an incumbent \(\bar x\in X\) consists of inequalities \(D x\ge d\), each accompanied by a checkable derivation proving validity for \(X\), and a rational LP certificate establishing \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax\ge b,\ Dx\ge d\}\ge c^\top\bar x\). Since every point of \(X\) satisfies all certified cuts, the relaxation bound and incumbent value coincide, certifying \(c^\top\bar x=z^*\).

Every row of \(Dx\ge d\) has a sound, checkable validity derivation.
The strengthened LP lower bound is certified exactly.

knowledge_statements.title: Enumeration-Tree Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-bound-style certificate whose leaves exhaust the integer feasible region and cannot improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X=\{x\in\mathbb Z^p\times\mathbb R^{n-p}:Ax\ge b\}\), an enumeration-tree certificate for a feasible incumbent \(\bar x\) is a finite rooted tree. Each branch covers its parent’s mixed-integer points.
Every leaf certificate is valid and exactly checkable.

knowledge_statements.title: Chvátal–Gomory Proofs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pure-integer cutting-plane derivations using nonnegative aggregation followed by integral rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\) with rational data and integer variables. A Chvátal–Gomory derivation is a finite sequence of rational inequalities in which each line is either an initial inequality or is obtained from earlier valid inequalities \(a_i^\top x\le\beta_i\) by choosing \(\lambda_i\ge0\) such that \(\sum_i\lambda_i a_i\in\mathbb Z^n\), then writing \((\sum_i\lambda_i a_i)^\top x\le\lfloor\sum_i\lambda_i\beta_i\rfloor\). A derivation ending in a target inequality certifies its validity for \(P\cap\mathbb Z^n\); one ending in \(0\le-1\) certifies integer infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each proof line aggregates earlier inequalities and rounds the right side; the final line certifies validity or integer infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb Q^m\), and all variables are integer.
Every multiplier and arithmetic operation is represented exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\cap\mathbb Z^n\subseteq\{x:\alpha^\top x\le\delta\}\), or \(P\cap\mathbb Z^n=\varnothing\) when the last line is \(0\le-1\).

notation.meaning: rational polyhedron defined by the initial inequalities

knowledge_statements.title: Gomory Mixed-Integer Proofs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed-integer cut certificate derived from a tableau row whose basic variable is required to be integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the tableau row \(x_B+\sum_{j\in N}a_jx_j=b\), where \(x_B\) and variables indexed by \(N_I\) are integer, variables indexed by \(N_C\) are continuous, and \(x_j\ge0\). Put \(f_0=b-\lfloor b\rfloor\) and \(f_j=a_j-\lfloor a_j\rfloor\). If \(0<f_0<1\), the Gomory mixed-integer inequality is
\[\sum_{\substack{j\in N_I\\ f_j\le f_0}}f_jx_j+\frac{f_0}{1-f_0}\sum_{\substack{j\in N_I\\ f_j>f_0}}(1-f_j)x_j+\sum_{\substack{j\in N_C\\ a_j\ge0}}a_jx_j-\frac{f_0}{1-f_0}\sum_{\substack{j\in N_C\\ a_j<0}}a_jx_j\ge f_0.\]
The row, variable types, and exact arithmetic certify this inequality for every feasible mixed-integer solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fractional tableau row for an integer basic variable yields an exactly checkable Gomory mixed-integer inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(x_B\in\mathbb Z\), \(x_j\in\mathbb Z\) for \(j\in N_I\), and \(x_j\in\mathbb R\) for \(j\in N_C\).
\(x_j\ge0\) for every \(j\in N\), and \(0<f_0<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_B+\sum_{j\in N}a_jx_j=b\ \Longrightarrow\) the displayed Gomory mixed-integer inequality holds.

notation.meaning: fractional part of the tableau right-hand side
fractional part of an integer-variable tableau coefficient

children.title: Split Proofs
children.top_down_role: Cutting-plane proofs organized around split disjunctions.

knowledge_statements.title: Split Proofs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential cutting-plane proof using two-term split disjunctions on integer linear forms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be rational and let the first \(p\) variables be integer. A split disjunction is \(D(\pi,\pi_0)=\{x:\pi^\top x\le\pi_0\}\cup\{x:\pi^\top x\ge\pi_0+1\}\), where \(\pi\in\mathbb Z^p\times\{0\}^{n-p}\) and \(\pi_0\in\mathbb Z\). A split-proof line is an inequality valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(Q\cap D(\pi,\pi_0))\), where \(Q\) is the relaxation defined by earlier lines. A finite sequence ending in \(\alpha^\top x\le\beta\) certifies that inequality for every mixed-integer point of \(P\), provided each line’s validity is checkable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A split proof repeatedly derives inequalities from two-term integer splits and ends with the claimed valid inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a rational relaxation of points with \(x_1,\ldots,x_p\in\mathbb Z\).
Each proof line includes a checkable certificate of validity for its stated split hull.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\cap(\mathbb Z^p\times\mathbb R^{n-p})\subseteq\{x:\alpha^\top x\le\beta\}.\)

notation.meaning: current relaxation defined by prior proof lines

knowledge_statements.title: General Disjunctive Proofs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cutting-plane derivations based on finite disjunctions covering all mixed-integer feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be rational with integer index set \(I\). At a relaxation \(Q\supseteq P\cap\{x:x_I\in\mathbb Z^I\}\), choose a finite disjunction \(D=\bigcup_{t=1}^kD_t\) that contains every point satisfying the integrality restrictions. A disjunctive-proof line is an inequality valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(Q\cap D)=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{t=1}^k(Q\cap D_t))\). A finite sequence of such checkable lines ending in \(\alpha^\top x\le\beta\) certifies that the terminal inequality is valid for every mixed-integer feasible point of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general disjunctive proof derives each line from a finite disjunction covering all mixed-integer points.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) and every disjunct \(D_t\) have rational descriptions.
Each selected disjunction covers all points satisfying the designated integrality restrictions.
Validity of every derived line for its disjunctive hull is checkable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\cap\{x:x_I\in\mathbb Z^I\}\subseteq\{x:\alpha^\top x\le\beta\}.\)

children.title: Split–Disjunction Relationship

knowledge_statements.title: Split–Disjunction Relationship
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Embedding of split inference into finite disjunctive inference for mixed-integer sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For integer indices \(I\), every split \(\pi^\top x\le\pi_0\) or \(\pi^\top x\ge\pi_0+1\), with \(\pi\in\mathbb Z^I\) and \(\pi_0\in\mathbb Z\), is a two-term disjunction covering every point with \(x_I\in\mathbb Z^I\). Consequently, for every relaxation \(Q\), the split hull \(\operatorname{conv}(Q\cap D(\pi,\pi_0))\) is a special case of a finite disjunctive hull. Every split-proof inference is therefore a general disjunctive-proof inference, and any split proof can be copied line for line into the general disjunctive system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every split is a two-term valid disjunction, so every split proof is also a general disjunctive proof.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi\) is integral and supported only on integer-constrained variables.
\(\pi_0\in\mathbb Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{split}}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{disj}}\), with preservation of proof lines and rank.

children.title: Disjunction-Width Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunction-Width Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Width classification of disjunctive proofs by the largest number of terms used in any inference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a disjunctive proof \(\Pi\), if inference \(r\) uses \(D_r=\bigcup_{t=1}^{k_r}D_{r,t}\), define its disjunction width by \(w(\Pi)=\max_r k_r\). The width-\(k\) regime contains proofs with \(w(\Pi)\le k\); the bounded-width regime fixes \(k\) independently of instance size; and the unbounded-width regime permits \(k\) to grow with the instance. Under term-count width, every split proof has width at most \(2\), while a general finite-disjunctive proof need not have a uniform width bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disjunction width is the maximum number of terms in any proof inference; split proofs have width two.
assumptions_latex: \(\Pi\) is a finite proof and every inference uses a finite disjunction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w(\Pi)=\max_r k_r\), and \(\Pi\) split implies \(w(\Pi)\le2\).

knowledge_statements.title: Proof Length
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Line-count measure for finite cutting-plane derivations, distinct from total binary encoding size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Pi=(L_1,\ldots,L_s)\) be a finite cutting-plane derivation whose initial inequalities are axioms and whose remaining inequalities are derived lines. Its line-count proof length is \(\ell(\Pi)=|\{i:L_i\text{ is derived}\}|\). If all initial lines are included in the convention, the total line length is \(s\); the convention must be fixed when comparing systems. Line-count length does not bound coefficient magnitude, so the binary certificate size is separately \(\operatorname{size}(\Pi)=\sum_{i=1}^s\operatorname{bits}(L_i)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Proof Rank
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inference-depth measure for cutting-plane proofs represented as directed acyclic derivation graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent a cutting-plane proof as a directed acyclic graph whose vertices are inequalities and whose arcs point from premises to conclusions. Assign every initial inequality rank \(0\). If a derived line \(L\) has cited premises \(P(L)\), define \(r(L)=1+\max\{r(H):H\in P(L)\}\), with \(r(L)=1\) for a premise-free derived line. The proof rank is \(r(\Pi)=\max\{r(L):L\text{ is a terminal claimed line}\}\); for a single-conclusion proof, it is the rank of that conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proof rank is the greatest number of dependent inference rounds on a path from an axiom to the conclusion.
assumptions_latex: The proof dependency relation is finite and acyclic.
Every derived line explicitly identifies its premises.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r(L)=1+\max_{H\in P(L)}r(H)\) and \(r(\Pi)=\max_{L\text{ terminal}}r(L)\).

children.title: Length–Rank Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Relationships and separations between derivation size and rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Length–Rank Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitional tradeoff for sequential cutting-plane derivations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=(I_1,\ldots,I_L)\) be a cutting-plane refutation, and assign rank zero to every initial inequality. Assign each derived inequality rank one plus the maximum rank of its antecedents, and let \(r(P)\) be the maximum assigned rank. If every derivation step has at least one antecedent appearing earlier in the sequence, then \[0\le r(P)\le L-1.\] Consequently, every refutation of rank at least \(R\) has length at least \(R+1\). The converse need not follow from these measures: a proof may contain many independent or same-rank derivations and therefore have large length while retaining small rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank never exceeds length minus one, so rank lower bounds imply length lower bounds; large length alone need not imply large rank.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a finite sequential cutting-plane refutation.
Every derived line cites at least one earlier antecedent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r(P)\le L-1\), and hence \(r(P)\ge R\Rightarrow L\ge R+1\).

notation.meaning: maximum derivation rank of the proof

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: follows directly from the sequential definitions of proof length and derivation rank

children.title: Family-Specific Separations

knowledge_statements.title: Family-Specific Separations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic separation between proof length and rank on an instance family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For infeasible integer-programming instances \(\mathcal F=(F_n)_{n\ge1}\) and a fixed cutting-plane proof system, define \(L_n\) and \(R_n\) as the minimum refutation length and minimum refutation rank of \(F_n\), respectively. The family exhibits a length-versus-rank separation when there are functions \(f\) and \(g\) such that \(R_n\le f(n)\), \(L_n\ge g(n)\), and \(g(n)/f(n)\to\infty\). A polynomial–exponential separation is the special case \(f(n)=n^{O(1)}\) and \(g(n)=2^{\Omega(n)}\). Both minima must use the same proof rules and coefficient restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family separates rank from length when its minimum rank grows asymptotically much more slowly than its minimum proof length under one fixed proof system.
assumptions_latex: \(F_n\) is infeasible for every \(n\).
Proof rules and coefficient restrictions are fixed across the family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_n\le f(n)\), \(L_n\ge g(n)\), and \(g(n)/f(n)\to\infty\).

notation.meaning: minimum refutation length of instance F_n
minimum refutation rank of instance F_n

children.title: Coefficient Growth
children.top_down_role: Magnitude growth of coefficients appearing in proof objects.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum reduced numerator or denominator magnitude across a rational cutting-plane proof.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i)_{i=1}^L\) be a rational cutting-plane proof in variables \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), where \(a_i\in\mathbb Q^n\) and \(b_i\in\mathbb Q\). Write every coordinate and right-hand side in lowest terms with positive denominator. Define \[M(P)=\max\!\left(\{1\}\cup\{|\operatorname{num}(a_{ij})|,\operatorname{den}(a_{ij}):1\le i\le L,\ 1\le j\le n\}\cup\{|\operatorname{num}(b_i)|,\operatorname{den}(b_i):1\le i\le L\}\right).\] For a family \((P_m)_{m\ge1}\), polynomial coefficient growth means \(M(P_m)\le m^{O(1)}\), while exponential coefficient growth means \(M(P_m)=2^{\Omega(m)}\). Denominators are included because rational coefficients of small absolute value may still require long encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficient growth measures the largest reduced numerator or denominator appearing in a proof, rather than only the largest absolute rational value.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) has \(L\) inequalities in \(n\) variables with rational coefficients.
Every rational coefficient is represented in lowest terms with positive denominator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(P)\) is the maximum reduced numerator or denominator magnitude occurring in \(P\).

notation.meaning: maximum reduced numerator or denominator magnitude in proof P

children.title: Encoding-Length Growth

knowledge_statements.title: Encoding-Length Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary size of all inequalities in a cutting-plane proof.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer \(z\), set \(\ell(z)=1+\lceil\log_2(|z|+1)\rceil\). For a reduced rational \(p/q\) with \(q>0\), set \(\ell(p/q)=\ell(p)+\ell(q)\). If \(P=(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i)_{i=1}^L\) has \(n\) variables, define its dense binary encoding length by \[E(P)=\sum_{i=1}^L\left(\ell(b_i)+\sum_{j=1}^n\ell(a_{ij})\right).\] Sparse encodings additionally record nonzero indices. A proof family has polynomial encoding growth when \(E(P_n)\) is polynomial in the binary size of its input instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encoding-length growth counts the binary bits needed for every reduced coefficient and right-hand side, together with indices under sparse storage.
assumptions_latex: Coefficients use reduced binary rational encodings.
The dense or sparse storage convention is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E(P)\) equals the total coefficient encoding length under the selected convention.

children.title: Coefficient–Encoding Relationship

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient–Encoding Relationship
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative relation between maximum coefficient magnitude and total bit length.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) contain \(N\) explicitly encoded reduced rational coefficient slots, including right-hand sides, and let \(M(P)\) be the maximum magnitude of any numerator or denominator. Under the signed binary convention, \[\left\lceil\log_2(M(P)+1)\right\rceil\le E(P)\le 2N\left(1+\left\lceil\log_2(M(P)+1)\right\rceil\right).\] The factor two allows one numerator and one denominator per rational slot. Thus polynomially many slots and polynomially bounded coefficient bit length imply polynomial total encoding length. A magnitude bound alone does not control \(E(P)\) when the number of encoded slots is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total encoding length is bounded by the number of rational slots times their maximum bit length; coefficient magnitude alone cannot bound proof size.
assumptions_latex: All rational coefficients are reduced and binary encoded.
\(N\) counts every explicitly stored coefficient and right-hand side.

children.title: Arithmetic-Complexity Consequences

knowledge_statements.title: Arithmetic-Complexity Consequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-complexity consequence of coefficient and encoding growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each cutting-plane inference can be checked using at most \(q(n)\) arithmetic operations on integers whose bit length is at most \(B\), where \(n\) is the number of variables. Using standard deterministic integer arithmetic, one inference is checkable in \(q(n)\operatorname{poly}(B)\) bit operations, and an \(L\)-line proof is checkable in \(Lq(n)\operatorname{poly}(B)\) bit operations. Hence polynomial \(L\), polynomial \(q(n)\), and polynomial coefficient bit length yield polynomial-time verification. A polynomial bound on proof length or rank without a coefficient-bit bound does not establish polynomial Turing complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomially many proof lines are polynomial-time checkable only when inference work and coefficient bit lengths are also polynomially bounded.
assumptions_latex: Each inference uses at most \(q(n)\) exact integer-arithmetic operations.
Every operated integer has bit length at most \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{check}}(P)\le Lq(n)\operatorname{poly}(B)\).

children.title: Proof Space
children.top_down_role: Memory required to retain intermediate or active proof objects.

knowledge_statements.title: Proof Space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Line-space measure induced by verification schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_P\) be the directed acyclic dependency graph of a cutting-plane proof \(P\), with one vertex per proof line and arcs from antecedents to their derived line. A verification schedule may load or derive a line, retain it, delete it, and, if permitted, reload or rederive it; a derivation may be checked only while all cited antecedents are present. The line space \(S(P)\) is the minimum, over valid schedules ending with the contradiction line present, of the maximum number of simultaneously retained proof lines. Bit space instead maximizes the total binary encoding length of retained lines.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proof space is the least peak number of simultaneously retained lines needed by a valid dependency-respecting verification schedule.
assumptions_latex: The proof dependency graph is acyclic.
The schedule's reload and rederivation permissions are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S(P)=\min_{\sigma}\max_t |M_{\sigma,t}|\), where \(M_{\sigma,t}\) is the set of lines retained at time \(t\).

notation.meaning: lines retained by schedule sigma at time t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: proof line space is the blackboard or pebbling-space measure of the dependency DAG
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition depends materially on whether derived lines may be loaded, reread, or rederived and on what persistent input is available. Merely saying those permissions are fixed does not identify one proof-space measure; a cutting-plane or pebbling-space source is needed to select the intended model.

children.title: Checking Complexity
children.top_down_role: Resources required to validate an encoded cutting-plane proof.

knowledge_statements.title: Checking Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic verification cost for an explicitly annotated proof.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be an explicitly annotated \(L\)-line cutting-plane proof with total encoding length \(E(P)\). Suppose every annotation identifies earlier antecedents and a rule whose side conditions are decidable in time polynomial in the combined binary length of the cited and derived lines. A deterministic checker reads each line, verifies its annotation and arithmetic, and accepts exactly when every inference is valid and the final line is a contradiction. Its running time is \(\operatorname{poly}(E(P))\) and its working bit space is at most \(E(P)+O(\log L)\) when all previously read lines may be retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Locally checkable annotations make verification polynomial in the certificate's total binary length, with linear storage available by retaining the proof.
assumptions_latex: Every line explicitly cites earlier antecedents and its inference rule.
Each rule's side conditions are polynomial-time decidable in the cited bit length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{check}}(P)=\operatorname{poly}(E(P))\) and \(S_{\mathrm{bit}}(P)\le E(P)+O(\log L)\).

notation.meaning: total binary encoding length of the annotated proof

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: deterministic verification is obtained by sequentially checking polynomial-time local inference predicates
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional verification claim is plausible, but no cutting-plane rule system or source establishes the assumed polynomial-time local predicates. Source support is needed before treating this as a checking-complexity bound for cutting-plane certificates.

children.title: Space–Verification Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Relationships between retained proof state and checking effort.

knowledge_statements.title: Space–Verification Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto tradeoff between verifier working space and checking time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed encoded proof \(P\), let \(T_P(s)\) be the minimum checking time among valid verification schedules using at most \(s\) bits of working storage, and set \(T_P(s)=\infty\) when no such schedule exists. Then \[s_1\le s_2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad T_P(s_2)\le T_P(s_1).\] Let \(s_{\mathrm{full}}\) denote the space needed to retain the encoded proof together with the checker's auxiliary state. If every local inference predicate is decidable in polynomial time, then \[T_P(s_{\mathrm{full}})\le \operatorname{poly}(E(P)).\] Smaller space may require rereading or rederiving deleted antecedents when the verification model permits those operations. Any resulting time increase depends on the dependency graph and the specified access model, not on proof length alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal checking time cannot increase when more working memory is available, and retaining the full proof supplies a polynomial-time upper bound when local inferences are polynomial-time checkable.
assumptions_latex: Reloading and rederivation permissions and their costs are fixed by the verification model.
Every local inference predicate is decidable in time polynomial in the encoding length of its inputs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_1\le s_2\Rightarrow T_P(s_2)\le T_P(s_1)\), and \(T_P(s_{\mathrm{full}})\le\operatorname{poly}(E(P))\).

notation.meaning: minimum checking time with bit-space budget s
total encoded length of proof P
space sufficient to retain the encoded proof and checker state

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: feasible schedules under a smaller space budget remain feasible under a larger budget

children.title: Streaming Verification Regimes
children.top_down_role: Checking models that process proof records with restricted retained state.

knowledge_statements.title: Streaming Verification Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-pass verification under a supplied retention schedule and bounded retained state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an instance description, an annotated proof stream \(I_1,\ldots,I_L\) in topological order, a memory budget \(s\), and a retention schedule specifying which stored lines to delete after each item. The instance axioms remain available read-only, but discarded streamed proof lines cannot be accessed again. Initialize an empty store \(M\). Upon reading \(I_i\), reject unless every cited non-axiom antecedent is currently in \(M\) and the local inference predicate succeeds. Otherwise insert \(I_i\), perform the scheduled deletions, and reject if the binary encoding of \(M\) exceeds \(s\) bits. Accept after the final item exactly when every item passed and \(I_L\) is a contradiction. The verifier is sound. It accepts a valid proof whenever the supplied schedule retains every non-axiom antecedent through its last use and respects the budget \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-pass checker follows a supplied retention schedule, stores selected prior proof lines, and verifies each arriving inference using stored antecedents and read-only instance axioms.
assumptions_latex: Proof lines \(I_1,\ldots,I_L\) arrive once in dependency-respecting order.
The original instance axioms remain available read-only.
Annotations identify antecedents and locally decidable inference predicates.
Discarded streamed proof lines cannot be accessed again.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The verifier is sound and accepts \(P\) whenever the supplied last-use retention schedule uses at most \(s\) bits.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the algorithm directly performs one-pass local checking under an explicit retention schedule

children.title: Rank Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Hardness results based on required proof rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic lower-bound predicate for cutting-plane rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a cutting-plane proof system \(\mathcal C\), a family of infeasible instances \((F_n)_{n\ge1}\), and a function \(r:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N_0\). The function \(r\) is a rank lower bound for this family if, for every \(n\ge1\) and every legal \(\mathcal C\)-refutation \(P\) of \(F_n\), \[\operatorname{rank}_{\mathcal C}(P)\ge r(n).\] The quantification includes every coefficient and derivation choice permitted by \(\mathcal C\). Imposing bounded coefficients or other restrictions defines a different lower-bound statement and must be declared explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank lower bound says that every legal refutation of every indexed family member requires at least the stated rank in one fixed proof system.
assumptions_latex: \(F_n\) is infeasible for every \(n\ge1\).
\(\mathcal C\) and all coefficient restrictions are fixed across the family.
\(r:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall n\ge1,\ \min\{\operatorname{rank}_{\mathcal C}(P):P\text{ is a legal }\mathcal C\text{-refutation of }F_n\}\ge r(n)\).

notation.meaning: claimed rank lower-bound value for the n-th instance

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a proof-measure lower bound universally quantifies over legal refutations in a fixed system

children.title: Length Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Hardness results based on required proof size.

knowledge_statements.title: Length Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic lower-bound predicate for cutting-plane proof length.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a cutting-plane proof system \(\mathcal C\), a family of infeasible instances \((F_n)_{n\ge1}\), a line-counting convention, and a function \(\ell:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\). The function \(\ell\) is a length lower bound if, for every \(n\ge1\) and every legal \(\mathcal C\)-refutation \(P\) of \(F_n\), \[\operatorname{len}_{\mathcal C}(P)\ge \ell(n).\] The lower bound is superpolynomial when, for every constant \(k>0\), there exists \(n_0\) such that \(\ell(n)>n^k\) for every \(n\ge n_0\). It is exponential when there are constants \(c>0\) and \(n_0\) such that \(\ell(n)\ge2^{cn}\) for every \(n\ge n_0\). A line-count lower bound alone does not determine binary certificate size unless the coefficient-encoding convention is also fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A length lower bound requires every legal refutation of every indexed family member to contain at least the stated number of lines under one fixed counting convention.
assumptions_latex: \(F_n\) is infeasible for every \(n\ge1\).
\(\mathcal C\) and the line-counting convention are fixed across the family.
\(\ell:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall n\ge1,\ \min\{\operatorname{len}_{\mathcal C}(P):P\text{ is a legal }\mathcal C\text{-refutation of }F_n\}\ge \ell(n)\).

notation.meaning: claimed length lower-bound value for the n-th instance

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a proof-length lower bound universally quantifies over legal refutations under a fixed counting convention

children.title: Rank–Length Separations
children.top_down_role: Instance families separating rank complexity from length complexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank–Length Separations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines asymptotic separation between rank and proof length for a fixed cutting-plane proof system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a cutting-plane proof system \(\mathcal P\) and infeasible instances \((I_n)_{n\ge1}\). Let \(r_{\mathcal P}(I)\) be minimum proof rank and \(L_{\mathcal P}(I)\) minimum proof length. The family exhibits a rank–length separation if there are functions \(f,g:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R_+\) such that \(r_{\mathcal P}(I_n)\le f(n)\), \(L_{\mathcal P}(I_n)\ge g(n)\), and \(g(n)\) is superpolynomial in \(f(n)+n\); the reverse separation interchanges rank and length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family separates rank from length when one proof measure stays small while the other grows superpolynomially relative to it and the instance parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) has well-defined rank and line-count measures.
Each \(I_n\) is infeasible and has a \(\mathcal P\)-refutation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((I_n)_{n\ge1}\) satisfies the stated asymptotic rank–length separation predicate.

notation.meaning: minimum rank of a refutation of instance I
minimum number of lines in a refutation of instance I

review_flags: Exact separation convention depends on the selected cutting-plane proof system.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The system-dependent asymptotic convention has no citation. Moreover, under usual line-count and rank measures rank is bounded by proof length, so the claimed reverse separation cannot simply be obtained by interchanging the measures.

children.title: Hard-Instance Families
children.top_down_role: Structured integer programs used to expose proof-complexity lower bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Hard-Instance Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines hardness relative to a fixed cutting-plane proof system and resource measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a cutting-plane proof system, let \(s(I)\) denote binary encoding length, and let \(M_{\mathcal P}(I)\) be minimum refutation rank, length, or coefficient size. An infinite family \((I_n)_{n\ge1}\) of infeasible integer programs is \(h\)-hard for \((\mathcal P,M)\) if \(s(I_n)\le n^{O(1)}\) and every \(\mathcal P\)-refutation of \(I_n\) has \(M_{\mathcal P}(I_n)\ge h(n)\). It is superpolynomially hard when \(h\) dominates every polynomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hard family has polynomially encoded members but forces every refutation in the chosen system to consume a prescribed large resource.
assumptions_latex: Every \(I_n\) is infeasible over its declared integer domain.
The proof system \(\mathcal P\) is sound and complete for the family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((I_n)_{n\ge1}\) is \(h\)-hard under the selected proof resource \(M\).

notation.meaning: binary encoding length of an instance

review_flags: Abstract proof-complexity definition requires a system-specific source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is plausible, but the parameterization, encoding-size condition, and selected proof-resource convention require a proof-system-specific source. The wording also conflates the minimum resource M_P(I) with the resource used by an individual refutation.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Size Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measures the unavoidable binary magnitude of rational coefficients in cutting-plane refutations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rational inequality \(a^\top x\le b\), define its coefficient size as the binary encoding length of the primitive integer vector obtained by clearing denominators and dividing all entries of \((a,b)\) by their greatest common divisor. A family \((I_n)\) has coefficient-size lower bound \(h(n)\) in proof system \(\mathcal P\) if every \(\mathcal P\)-refutation of \(I_n\) contains an inequality whose coefficient size is at least \(h(n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lower bound says every refutation must contain at least one inequality whose normalized coefficients require many bits.
assumptions_latex: All proof inequalities have rational coefficients.
Coefficient vectors are canonically normalized after clearing denominators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(\mathcal P\)-refutation of \(I_n\) contains a line of coefficient size at least \(h(n)\).

children.title: Branching Limits
children.top_down_role: Limitations arising from the size or structure of branching trees.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States a leaf lower bound obtained from bounded progress of each branching path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_n\) be the feasible integer set and let a branch-and-bound certificate partition \(S_n\) into leaf regions \(R_1,\ldots,R_L\). Suppose a nonnegative hardness measure \(\mu\) satisfies \(\mu(S_n)\ge H_n\), every permitted branching disjunction partitions any region into at most \(q\) children, and each root-to-leaf branch can reduce \(\mu\) by at most \(d_n\). If every certified leaf must have measure zero, then the tree depth is at least \(\lceil H_n/d_n\rceil\) and \(L\ge q^{\lceil H_n/d_n\rceil}\) for a full \(q\)-ary tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If each branch removes only bounded hardness, reaching certifiable leaves requires large depth and, for full branching, exponentially many leaves.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu\) is monotone under restriction.
Each permitted branch reduces \(\mu\) by at most \(d_n>0\).
Every certified leaf has \(\mu=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{depth}\ge\lceil H_n/d_n\rceil\), with the stated leaf bound for full \(q\)-ary trees.

notation.meaning: maximum hardness decrease per branch level

review_flags: The leaf bound requires the explicit full-tree hypothesis and is not valid for arbitrary unbalanced trees.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The depth argument requires a precise per-edge decrease bound. The exponential leaf conclusion additionally requires every leaf to have depth at least the threshold and every internal node above that threshold to have exactly q children; merely having a full q-ary tree and large maximum depth is insufficient. A sourced branching lower-bound formulation is needed.

children.title: Cut-Derivation Limits
children.top_down_role: Limitations arising from the strength or complexity of admissible cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Derivation Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes bounded local strength as a barrier to short cut-only or branch-cut certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a cut family \(\mathcal C\) and closure operator \(T_{\mathcal C}\). If a relaxation \(P_n\) and target inequality \(\alpha_n^\top x\le\beta_n\) satisfy \(\alpha_n^\top x\le\beta_n\notin T_{\mathcal C}^{k-1}(P_n)\) but \(\alpha_n^\top x\le\beta_n\in T_{\mathcal C}^{k}(P_n)\), then no derivation using one \(\mathcal C\)-closure layer per round can establish the target in fewer than \(k\) rounds. The same obstruction applies at every branch-cut node whose local relaxation retains rank \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut whose closure rank is k cannot be derived in fewer than k rounds, including at branch nodes where the same obstruction remains.
assumptions_latex: One proof round applies at most one \(\mathcal C\)-closure layer.
The target inequality is valid for the integer hull.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every permitted derivation of the target requires at least \(k\) cut rounds.

notation.meaning: closure induced by the allowed cut family

review_flags: System-specific closure and round conventions require sourcing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An inequality is valid for a closure rather than an element of the closure polyhedron, so the membership notation is not well typed. The round convention and its transfer to local branch-and-cut relaxations are system-specific and need a source.

children.title: Tree–Cut Interaction
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs between branching structure and cut strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Tree–Cut Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expresses branch-and-cut validity as exact local cut preservation propagated through a disjunctive tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a branch-and-cut tree have pre-cut node regions \(R_v\). At each node \(v\), cuts produce a strengthened region \(R'_v\subseteq R_v\) satisfying \(R'_v\cap\mathbb Z^p=R_v\cap\mathbb Z^p\). For every internal node, suppose its children cover the post-cut integer set: \(R'_v\cap\mathbb Z^p\subseteq\bigcup_{w\in\operatorname{ch}(v)}(R_w\cap\mathbb Z^p)\). If every leaf \(\ell\) has an exact certificate that \(R'_\ell\cap\mathbb Z^p=\varnothing\), then \(R_{\mathrm{root}}\cap\mathbb Z^p=\varnothing\). Thus branching combines integer cases disjunctively, while valid cuts strengthen node relaxations without deleting integer-feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cuts strengthen each node while preserving its integer points, and branches cover all remaining integer cases; exact infeasibility of every leaf therefore certifies root infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: Every post-cut region satisfies \(R'_v\subseteq R_v\) and \(R'_v\cap\mathbb Z^p=R_v\cap\mathbb Z^p\).
Every branching disjunction covers the post-cut integer points of its parent.
Every leaf has an exact infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{root}}\cap\mathbb Z^p=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: pre-cut relaxation region at tree node v
region at node v after certified cuts

children.title: Lower-Bound Transfer
children.top_down_role: Transfer of lower bounds among branching, cutting-plane, and hybrid proof systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Bound Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfers proof lower bounds through a resource-controlled simulation between certificate systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let proof system \(\mathcal A\) simulate proof system \(\mathcal B\) with resource overhead \(p\): every \(\mathcal B\)-certificate of size \(s\) converts into an \(\mathcal A\)-certificate of size at most \(p(s,n)\) for instances of parameter \(n\). If every \(\mathcal A\)-certificate for \(I_n\) has size at least \(L(n)\), then every \(\mathcal B\)-certificate has size at least \(\inf\{s:p(s,n)\ge L(n)\}\). For increasing invertible \(p(\cdot,n)\), this is \(p^{-1}(L(n),n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower bound transfers backward through a simulation, weakened by the simulation’s resource overhead.
assumptions_latex: The simulation preserves certificate validity.
\(p(s,n)\) is nondecreasing in \(s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{size}_{\mathcal B}(I_n)\ge\inf\{s:p(s,n)\ge L(n)\}\).

notation.meaning: lower bound in the simulating system

review_flags: Standard simulation principle, but no supplied locator addresses proof-complexity transfer.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The backward-transfer principle is plausible, but the certificate-size domain and generalized inverse convention must be fixed. A proof-complexity simulation source is required before relying on the displayed lower bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact LP Subproblem Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives rational primal-dual certificates for exact LP bounds and Farkas certificates for infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the rational minimization LP \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax\ge b\}\), rational vectors \(x\) and \(y\) certify optimality when \(Ax\ge b\), \(y\ge0\), \(A^\top y=c\), and \(c^\top x=b^\top y\). The common value is the exact optimum by weak duality. Alternatively, a rational vector \(y\ge0\) satisfying \(A^\top y=0\) and \(b^\top y>0\) certifies infeasibility, because multiplying \(Ax\ge b\) by \(y\) would imply \(0\ge b^\top y>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact rational primal-dual equality certifies an LP optimum; a rational Farkas multiplier certifies infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(A,b,c\) and all certificate entries are rational.
The LP is represented with inequalities \(Ax\ge b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The supplied rational data certify either the exact optimum or infeasibility.

children.title: Safe Bound Certificates
children.top_down_role: Exact evidence supporting globally valid objective bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Safe Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certifies a rigorous lower bound for a rational minimization LP or its MIP restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\ge b\}\) with rational data and objective \(\min c^\top x\). A rational vector \(y\ge0\) with \(A^\top y=c\) certifies the lower bound \(c^\top x\ge b^\top y\) for every \(x\in P\). Consequently the same bound holds for any mixed-integer feasible set \(X\subseteq P\). Verification consists solely of exact rational sign tests, matrix multiplication, and comparison with the claimed bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exactly dual-feasible rational multiplier certifies a lower objective bound for the LP relaxation and every contained MIP feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(A,b,c,y\) are represented exactly as rationals.
The mixed-integer feasible set satisfies \(X\subseteq P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c^\top x\ge b^\top y\) for every \(x\in X\).

children.title: Safe Cut Certificates
children.top_down_role: Exact evidence supporting the validity of generated inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Safe Cut Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certifies a linear cut by exact aggregation and, when applicable, integer rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Ax\le b\) describe a rational relaxation and let \(X\) impose integrality on all variables appearing in \(u^\top Ax\), where \(u\ge0\) is rational. Exact aggregation gives the valid inequality \(u^\top Ax\le u^\top b\). If \(u^\top A\) is integral on \(X\), then \(u^\top Ax\le\lfloor u^\top b\rfloor\) is also valid. The multiplier \(u\), exact products, integrality check, and rounded right-hand side form a verifiable safe-cut certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative exact aggregation is valid, and its right side may be rounded down when the aggregated left side is integer-valued.
assumptions_latex: \(A,b,u\) are exact rational data and \(u\ge0\).
\(u^\top A x\) is integer-valued for every \(x\in X\) when rounding is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u^\top Ax\le\lfloor u^\top b\rfloor\) is valid for \(X\).

children.title: Bound–Cut Composition
children.top_down_role: Combination of certified cuts with certified bounds in rational MIP verification.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound–Cut Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that exact bound and cut certificates compose by induction over a certificate sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_0\) be a rational relaxation containing the mixed-integer feasible set \(X\). For \(i=1,\ldots,k\), let \(P_i=P_{i-1}\cap\{x:a_i^\top x\le\beta_i\}\), where an exact safe-cut certificate proves \(X\cap P_{i-1}\subseteq\{x:a_i^\top x\le\beta_i\}\). Then \(X\subseteq P_k\). Hence any exact safe-bound certificate proving \(c^\top x\ge L\) on \(P_k\) also proves \(c^\top x\ge L\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequentially certified cuts preserve every MIP feasible point, so a bound certified on the final relaxation is valid for the original MIP.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq P_0\).
Each added cut has an exact validity certificate relative to its parent relaxation.
The terminal bound certificate is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c^\top x\ge L\) for every \(x\in X\).
