children.title: Numerical-Safety Failure Modes
children.top_down_role: Rounding, reconstruction, and encoding conditions that can invalidate claimed certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical-Safety Failure Modes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Demonstrates that tolerance-based rounding can delete an exactly feasible integer point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{x\in\mathbb Z:0\le x\le1\}\). The exact inequality \(x\ge0\) is valid and admits \(x=0\). If a floating-point routine perturbs its right-hand side to \(\varepsilon>0\) and then incorrectly treats \(x\ge\varepsilon\) as an exact antecedent for integer rounding, it emits \(x\ge1\). That cut deletes the feasible point \(x=0\). Thus rounding is safe only after exact validity and integer-valuedness of the unrounded inequality have been established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive floating-point perturbation followed by unjustified integer rounding can turn a valid bound into a cut that removes a feasible integer point.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\varepsilon<1\).
The perturbed inequality is accepted without an exact validity check.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The emitted cut \(x\ge1\) is invalid for \(X\) because \(0\in X\).
review_flags: Concrete counterexample is directly checkable; external source remains desirable.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

knowledge_statements.title: Rational Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unique bounded reconstruction of a rational number from one modular residue.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given integers \(M>0\), \(r\), and bounds \(P,Q>0\) satisfying \(M>2PQ\), run the extended Euclidean algorithm on \((M,r)\). Inspect its remainder–coefficient pairs \((u,v)\), where \(u\equiv rv\pmod M\), until \(|u|\le P\) and \(0<v\le Q\). Accept and output \(u/v\) only after verifying \(\gcd(u,v)=1\), \(\gcd(v,M)=1\), and \(u\equiv rv\pmod M\); otherwise report reconstruction failure. If a reduced fraction \(p/q\) satisfies \(|p|\le P\), \(0<q\le Q\), and \(r\equiv pq^{-1}\pmod M\), then it is unique and the accepted output equals \(p/q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extended Euclidean reconstruction uniquely recovers a bounded reduced fraction from its modular residue when the modulus exceeds twice the product of the numerator and denominator bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(|p|\le P\) and \(0<q\le Q\)
\(\gcd(p,q)=\gcd(q,M)=1\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u/v=p/q\) whenever reconstruction is accepted under the stated bounds.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and bounded-uniqueness claim fit the container, but no inspectable citation supports the stated modulus condition or the precise extended-Euclidean stopping and recovery procedure.

children.title: Iterative Refinement for Certificate Recovery
children.top_down_role: Covers refinement regimes used to improve approximate certificate data before exact validation.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterative Refinement for Certificate Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact residual refinement followed by rational reconstruction and verification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonsingular \(A\in\mathbb{Q}^{n\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{Q}^n\), initialize a numerical approximation \(x_0\). At iteration \(k\), compute the residual \(r_k=b-Ax_k\) exactly or with a certified enclosure, approximately solve \(A d_k=r_k\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\). Apply componentwise rational reconstruction to \(x_{k+1}\) using prescribed denominator bounds. Stop with \(\widehat{x}\in\mathbb{Q}^n\) only when exact arithmetic verifies \(A\widehat{x}=b\) and every required certificate inequality; stop with failure when the iteration or precision budget is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method repeatedly corrects an approximate solution, reconstructs a rational candidate, and returns it only after exact certificate checks succeed.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{Q}^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular.
A correction solver and finite reconstruction bounds are supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(\widehat{x}\) satisfies \(A\widehat{x}=b\) and all declared certificate predicates exactly.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact-verification safeguard is sound and the algorithm fits the leaf, but no source supports this particular refinement–reconstruction procedure or states conditions under which it recovers a certificate rather than merely returning failure.

children.title: Directed Rounding for Safe Certificates
children.top_down_role: Covers outward rounding choices that preserve the validity of certificate bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Directed Rounding for Safe Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outward-rounded interval evaluation of certificate inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent every computed scalar by an interval \([\underline z,\overline z]\) containing its exact value. Initialize exact input data by enclosing each datum between representable endpoints, and evaluate every arithmetic operation using downward rounding for lower endpoints and upward rounding for upper endpoints. For a required inequality \(g\le0\), accept the numerical certificate only when the resulting enclosure satisfies \(\overline g\le0\); for \(g\ge0\), require \(\underline g\ge0\); and for \(g=0\), require a separate exact check. Under correct outward rounding, every accepted inequality is valid for the exact quantity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outward rounding encloses every exact value, so a one-sided inequality is certified only when the entire computed interval lies on its valid side.
assumptions_latex: Every interval operation is inclusion isotonic and outward rounded.
No division interval contains \(0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\overline g\le0\Rightarrow g\le0\) and \(\underline g\ge0\Rightarrow g\ge0\).

notation.meaning: certified enclosure of an exact scalar

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The outward-rounding acceptance conditions are mathematically standard and fit safe certificate checking, but the record supplies no authoritative source or locator for interval inclusion and directed-rounding guarantees.

children.title: Refinement–Rounding Coordination
children.top_down_role: Covers how correction accuracy, rounding direction, and certificate acceptance interact.

knowledge_statements.title: Refinement–Rounding Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinates error reduction, outward rounding, reconstruction, and exact acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given certificate predicates \(g_j(z)\le0\), initialize a numerical candidate \(z_0\), precision \(p_0\), and tolerance budget. At stage \(k\), refine \(z_k\), evaluate each predicate with outward rounding to obtain \([\underline g_{j,k},\overline g_{j,k}]\), and increase precision whenever an interval intersects \(0\). When every \(\overline g_{j,k}\le0\), rationally reconstruct a candidate \(\widehat z\) and verify all predicates exactly. Return \(\widehat z\) only after exact verification; otherwise continue refinement until the declared iteration, denominator, or precision limit is reached, then return failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refinement continues while rounded predicate intervals cross zero; reconstruction occurs after separation, and only exact verification permits acceptance.
assumptions_latex: The predicates \(g_j\) admit certified interval evaluation.
Finite refinement, precision, and reconstruction budgets are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A returned \(\widehat z\) satisfies \(g_j(\widehat z)\le0\) for every \(j\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coordinated refinement, interval evaluation, reconstruction, and exact acceptance workflow fits the algorithmic leaf, but it is an uncited synthesized procedure and its triggering and stopping rules lack source support.

children.title: Precision Exhaustion Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Covers regimes where available precision cannot support a safely rounded exact certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Precision Exhaustion Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite precision cannot resolve predicates separated by less than a rounding cell.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix binary round-to-nearest arithmetic with \(p\) fractional bits near \(1\). Let \(t_-=1-2^{-p-2}\) and \(t_+=1+2^{-p-2}\). Both values round to the same floating-point number \(1\), although the predicate \(t\le1\) is true for \(t_-\) and false for \(t_+\). Consequently, any recovery procedure whose remaining precision is at most \(p\) and whose decision uses only that rounded value cannot safely decide this predicate. It must increase precision, obtain an exact representation, or report precision exhaustion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two rationals on opposite sides of a certificate threshold can share one finite-precision representation, forcing more precision, exact arithmetic, or failure.
assumptions_latex: Binary round-to-nearest arithmetic retains \(p\) fractional bits near \(1\).
The decision procedure observes only the rounded scalar.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{fl}_p(t_-)=\operatorname{fl}_p(t_+)=1\), but \(t_-\le1<t_+\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The indistinguishability example fits a failure-boundary container, but the spacing convention encoded by “p fractional bits near 1” and the asserted rounding identities require a precise floating-point model and an inspectable citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Symbolic–Numeric Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical discovery combined with exact symbolic certificate verification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a rational MIP instance, use numerical optimization to propose a finite certificate object \(C^{\mathrm{num}}\), such as primal points, dual multipliers, cuts, or branching data. Convert its scalar fields to rational candidates \(C^{\mathbb Q}\) by exact parsing, rational reconstruction, or bounded rounding. A symbolic verifier then recomputes every premise and side condition over \(\mathbb Q\), rejecting any failed or undefined operation. Output \(C^{\mathbb Q}\) only if every derivation and terminal claim passes; otherwise request refinement or return failure. Numerical tolerances never constitute acceptance conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerics discover a candidate certificate, while exact rational reconstruction and symbolic checking alone determine acceptance.
assumptions_latex: The MIP data are rational.
Every accepted inference has an exact rational verification rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance implies that every claim encoded by \(C^{\mathbb Q}\) holds under the exact verifier rules.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hybrid algorithm matches the local topic and correctly makes exact verification the acceptance criterion, but no cited proof-system or exact-MIP-certification source supports the proposed certificate objects and verifier guarantees.

children.top_down_role: Proof-log representations, independently checkable transformations, and verifier architecture.

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Derivation Logs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linearized proof objects whose inferences reference only earlier records.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequential derivation log is a finite sequence \(L=(R_1,\ldots,R_m)\). Each record \(R_i\) contains a rule identifier, exact rational payload, indices of premises drawn only from the instance axioms or \(R_1,\ldots,R_{i-1}\), and the resulting claim \(C_i\). A verifier processes records in order, checks the designated rule and all side conditions exactly, and stores \(C_i\) only after success. The log is accepted precisely when every record verifies and the final claim \(C_m\) is the required optimality, infeasibility, or bound statement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequential log orders exact inference records so every premise precedes its use and the final verified record states the requested result.
assumptions_latex: The rule set has deterministic, exact verification predicates.
All premise references are backward references.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\text{ is accepted}\iff\bigl(\forall i,\ R_i\text{ verifies}\bigr)\land C_m\text{ is the required terminal claim}.

notation.meaning: claim produced by the i-th record

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is the correct kind for a sequential log, and the backward-reference semantics are coherent, but the claimed record format and acceptance semantics have no proof-system source with a specific locator.

children.title: Branching Decision Records
children.top_down_role: Covers recorded variable disjunctions, node identifiers, and child-node provenance.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching Decision Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable records that establish exhaustive child disjunctions at search nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a parent node region \(R\), a branching decision record specifies predicates \(D_1,\ldots,D_s\) and child regions \(R_i=R\cap D_i\). It is valid when exact checking establishes \(R\cap(\mathbb{R}^{n_c}\times\mathbb{Z}^{n_i})\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^s R_i\). For ordinary integer-variable branching on \(x_j\) at integer \(k\), the two predicates are \(x_j\le k\) and \(x_j\ge k+1\); these cover every integer value of \(x_j\). Thus pruning all recorded children is sufficient to account for every feasible integer point of the parent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branching record is valid when its child predicates exhaustively cover all integer-feasible points of the parent region.
assumptions_latex: \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_c}\times\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\).
The branched coordinate \(x_j\) is integer-constrained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R\cap(\mathbb{R}^{n_c}\times\mathbb{Z}^{n_i})\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^s R_i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind and exhaustive-disjunction condition fit branching decision records. The ordinary integer split is correct, but no inspectable source supports the proposed log semantics and sufficiency claim.

children.title: Node Bound Records
children.top_down_role: Covers logged local bounds used to justify pruning or continued exploration.

knowledge_statements.title: Node Bound Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact dual certificates for lower bounds at minimization search nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(v\), let its rational LP relaxation be \(P_v=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:A_vx\ge b_v\}\) with minimization objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x\). A node-bound record contains \(y_v\in\mathbb{Q}^{m_v}\) and \(L_v=b_v^{\mathsf T}y_v\). The verifier checks exactly that \(y_v\ge0\) and \(A_v^{\mathsf T}y_v=c\). These equalities certify \(c^{\mathsf T}x\ge L_v\) for every \(x\in P_v\), hence also for every integer-feasible point represented by the node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rational dual-feasible vector certifies an exact lower bound for every LP-relaxation point and therefore every integer-feasible point at the node.
assumptions_latex: \(A_v,b_v,c\) are rational.
The node problem is a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in P_v\}\ge L_v=b_v^{\mathsf T}y_v\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dual-feasibility equations correctly yield a lower bound for the stated minimization relaxation and the certificate kind fits the leaf, but no source with a theorem or section locator is supplied.

children.title: Search-Tree Linkage
children.top_down_role: Covers the navigable correspondence among branch records, node bounds, and tree ancestry.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Tree Linkage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural certificate connecting branch records, children, and terminal closures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A search-tree linkage certificate specifies a finite node set \(V\), root \(r\), parent map \(\pi:V\setminus\{r\}\to V\), and ordered children for every internal node. Exact verification requires that repeated application of \(\pi\) reaches \(r\), every nonroot node occurs once as a child, and each internal node’s children coincide with a valid branching record whose regions cover the parent’s integer-feasible region. Every leaf must carry accepted closure evidence. These conditions make the linked records an exhaustive rooted search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linkage records form an acyclic rooted tree, connect each child to its certified branch, and require closure evidence at every leaf.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite.
Each internal node has a valid branching decision record.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigcup_{\ell\in\operatorname{Leaves}(V)}R_\ell\) covers every integer-feasible point represented by \(R_r\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The structural certificate fits search-tree linkage and its rooted-tree and coverage conditions are coherent, but the complete linkage semantics and global coverage conclusion lack an inspectable branch-and-bound proof-log source.

children.title: Node Closure Evidence
children.top_down_role: Covers infeasibility, integrality, dominance, or objective-based closure represented in the log.

knowledge_statements.title: Node Closure Evidence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact evidence justifying termination of a branch-and-bound node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization node with region \(P_v=\{x:A_vx\ge b_v\}\) and incumbent value \(U\), valid closure evidence is one of: an infeasibility vector \(y\ge0\) with \(A_v^{\mathsf T}y=0\) and \(b_v^{\mathsf T}y>0\); a certified lower bound \(L_v\ge U\); or a feasible integer point \(\bar x\) together with exact evidence that every feasible point in the node has objective at least \(c^{\mathsf T}\bar x\). Exact verification of any case proves that the node contains no improving integer solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node closes through exact infeasibility, domination by the incumbent bound, or a feasible point accompanied by matching node-optimality evidence.
assumptions_latex: The node and incumbent data are rational.
The objective is minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists x\in P_v\cap(\mathbb{R}^{n_c}\times\mathbb{Z}^{n_i})\text{ with }c^{\mathsf T}x<U\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The listed infeasibility and bound-dominance cases are suitable node-closure certificates, but the closure rule set and its exact-verification interpretation are uncited. A specific branch-and-bound certificate source is required.

children.title: Presolve Transformation Records
children.top_down_role: Covers logged reductions, eliminations, substitutions, and reformulations introduced before or during search.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Transformation Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact equivalence records linking original and presolved optimization models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original and presolved minimization models have feasible sets \(X\) and \(X'\) and objectives \(f\) and \(f'\). A presolve transformation record supplies exact maps \(\phi:X\to X'\) and \(\psi:X'\to X\), together with a rational offset \(\delta\). The verifier checks that both maps preserve all declared integrality restrictions, that \(f'(\phi(x))=f(x)-\delta\) for every \(x\in X\), and that \(f(\psi(x'))=f'(x')+\delta\) for every \(x'\in X'\). Consequently, feasibility, infeasibility, and optimal solutions transfer between the two models.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A presolve record certifies model equivalence using exact forward and lifting maps that preserve feasibility, integrality, and objective values up to a fixed offset.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(X'\) are rational mixed-integer feasible sets.
The transformation maps and offset are exactly representable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in X}f(x)=\delta+\inf_{x'\in X'}f'(x')\), with optimizers transferable by \(\phi\) and \(\psi\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits transformation records, and the two exact maps provide strong sufficient conditions for equivalence. No presolve-certification source supports this bidirectional map formulation, integrality requirements, or optimizer-transfer conclusion.

children.title: Propagation Deduction Records
children.top_down_role: Covers logged domain tightenings and implied restrictions derived during solver reasoning.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Deduction Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A locally checkable record for one domain tightening during MIP propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the current relaxation be \(F=\{x\in D:Ax\le b\}\), where \(D=\prod_{j=1}^n D_j\). A propagation deduction record is a tuple \(r=(i,B,D,D')\), where \(B\) identifies constraints used as reasons and \(D'=D_1'\times\cdots\times D_n'\subseteq D\) differs from \(D\) only by tightening \(D_i\). The record is valid precisely when \[\{x\in D:A_Bx\le b_B\}\subseteq\{x:x_i\in D_i'\}.\] A verifier checks the displayed implication using the recorded arithmetic rule and accepts the update only after that check succeeds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A propagation record certifies that specified constraints imply one recorded domain tightening under the pre-update domains.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(b\) have exactly represented rational entries.
Each integer-variable domain records integral bounds or an explicit finite set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq D'\), so replacing \(D\) by \(D'\) preserves every feasible solution.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct implication checking is the defining validity requirement for a propagation certificate
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The implication is mathematically sufficient for safe tightening and the certificate content kind fits, but no inspectable source supports this specific record format or its recorded arithmetic-rule semantics.

children.title: Transformation Provenance
children.top_down_role: Covers dependencies linking each recorded reduction or deduction to prior certified information.

knowledge_statements.title: Transformation Provenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provenance data connecting each presolve model to its predecessor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For models \(P_0,P_1,\ldots,P_k\), transformation provenance is a sequence \(\Pi=(\tau_t,w_t,R_t)_{t=1}^k\). Here \(\tau_t\) identifies the transformation from \(P_{t-1}\) to \(P_t\), \(w_t\) is locally checkable witness data, and \(R_t\) is a recovery map. Valid provenance certifies that every feasible \(y\) of \(P_t\) yields feasible \(R_t(y)\) for \(P_{t-1}\), with the same objective value, and that any claimed infeasibility or bound transfer is justified by the rule encoded in \(\tau_t\) and \(w_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transformation provenance records each presolve rule, its witness, and a checked recovery map to the preceding model.
assumptions_latex: All models use a common optimization sense.
Every rule identifier has a fixed solver-independent verification semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_1\circ\cdots\circ R_k\) reconstructs an original-model solution from any terminal feasible solution.

notation.meaning: Recovery map to the preceding model

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reversible transformation logs require rule witnesses and predecessor recovery maps
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the provenance container, but the requirements of objective equality, recovery maps, infeasibility transfer, and bound transfer need a direct source defining the supported presolve transformations.

children.title: Original-Model Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Covers certificate interpretation after reduced-model reasoning must be related back to the original instance.

knowledge_statements.title: Original-Model Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse replay of verified presolve transformations to recover an original solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a verified provenance sequence \(\Pi=(\tau_t,w_t,R_t)_{t=1}^k\) and a feasible terminal solution \(x^k\) of \(P_k\). Initialize \(t=k\). While \(t\ge1\), compute \(x^{t-1}=R_t(x^t)\), verify all values restored or modified by \(\tau_t\), and verify feasibility of the constraints whose status changes at that reversal; then decrement \(t\). Output \(x^0\) only if every reversal succeeds and direct evaluation confirms that \(x^0\) satisfies the original variable domains, constraints, and claimed objective value. Otherwise reject the reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reverse the verified presolve log, checking each restored value, then validate the reconstructed solution directly in the original model.
assumptions_latex: Each accepted transformation supplies a deterministic recovery map.
The terminal solution \(x^k\) is exactly represented.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On acceptance, \(x^0\) is feasible for \(P_0\) and has the objective value certified by \(\Pi\).

notation.meaning: Reverse recovery map for transformation t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reverse replay followed by direct feasibility checking certifies reconstruction
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and reverse-map ordering are coherent, but no source establishes that the stated local reversal checks are sufficient for the intended presolve proof system.

children.title: Symmetry Reduction Records
children.top_down_role: Covers logged orbit restrictions, representative choices, and symmetry-based search reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry Reduction Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A certificate that canonical-representative restrictions preserve an optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(G\) act on the feasible set \(F\), and let the objective \(c\) satisfy \(c(gx)=c(x)\) for every \(g\in G\) and \(x\in F\). A symmetry reduction record specifies generators for \(G\), checks preservation of \(F\) and \(c\), and supplies a canonical predicate \(K\) satisfying \[\forall x\in F\;\exists g\in G:\ K(gx).\] The restriction to \(F_K=\{x\in F:K(x)\}\) is then valid: every feasible orbit retains a representative, and the optimal value over \(F_K\) equals that over \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid symmetry record proves invariance and retains at least one canonical representative from every feasible orbit.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and its recorded generators define an exact action.
Feasibility and the objective are invariant under every generator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in F_K}c(x)=\min_{x\in F}c(x)\) whenever either minimum is attained.

source_refs.locator: Symmetry in mathematical programming p. 263

source_witnesses.locator: Symmetry in mathematical programming p. 263

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The group-invariance argument is mathematically sound and the certificate kind fits, but the cited page is not yet inspectable and does not presently support the proposed machine-checkable generators-and-canonical-predicate record format.

children.title: Dominance Elimination Records
children.top_down_role: Covers logged comparisons used to discard states, solutions, or subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Elimination Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A checkable witness that a discarded region cannot improve the retained region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem with feasible set \(F\) and objective \(c\), let \(E\subseteq F\) be marked for elimination and let \(R=F\setminus E\). A dominance elimination record supplies a verifier-computable map \(\phi:E\to R\) and witnesses the predicates \[\phi(x)\in F\quad\text{and}\quad c(\phi(x))\le c(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in E.\] The verifier accepts elimination only if these predicates follow from the recorded constraints and arithmetic. Consequently, any eliminated feasible solution has a retained feasible solution with no worse objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dominance record maps every eliminated feasible solution to a retained feasible solution having no worse objective value.
assumptions_latex: The optimization sense is minimization.
The map \(\phi\) is total on the eliminated feasible region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in R}c(x)=\inf_{x\in F}c(x)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a feasible no-worse replacement map is a sufficient dominance certificate
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A total feasible no-worse replacement map is sufficient to preserve the infimum, but no inspectable source supports this as the intended dominance-elimination certificate format.

children.title: Symmetry-Aware Dominance
children.top_down_role: Covers dominance claims whose validity depends on equivalence classes induced by symmetry.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Aware Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance certified after allowing a symmetry transformation of the replacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) preserve the feasible set \(F\) and objective \(c\), and let \(E\subseteq F\) and \(R=F\setminus E\). Symmetry-aware dominance holds when there exist verifier-computable maps \(\phi:E\to F\) and \(\gamma:E\to G\) such that \[\gamma(x)\phi(x)\in R\quad\text{and}\quad c(\gamma(x)\phi(x))\le c(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in E.\] Thus a replacement may first be constructed outside the retained canonical region and then transported into it by a recorded symmetry without degrading its objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An eliminated solution is dominated when a no-worse replacement can be moved into the retained region by a valid symmetry.
assumptions_latex: Every element of \(G\) preserves feasibility and objective value.
The maps \(\phi\) and \(\gamma\) are total on \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in R}c(x)=\inf_{x\in F}c(x)\).

notation.meaning: Recorded symmetry used for solution x

children.title: Reduction Validity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Covers cases where incomplete mappings, invalid representatives, or context-sensitive comparisons obstruct verification.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduction Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective invariance and no-worse replacement are necessary boundaries for safe reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Feasibility symmetry alone does not justify symmetry reduction for optimization. Consider \(F=\{(1,0),(0,1)\}\), minimization objective \(c(x)=x_1\), and the coordinate swap \(g(x_1,x_2)=(x_2,x_1)\). Although \(gF=F\), the restriction \(x_1\ge x_2\) retains only \((1,0)\), whose value is \(1\), while the removed point \((0,1)\) has value \(0\). Hence objective invariance, or an independently verified no-worse replacement condition, cannot be omitted from a valid symmetry or dominance reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasibility-preserving permutation can delete the optimum when it does not also preserve the objective.
assumptions_latex: The problem is interpreted as minimization over the displayed finite set.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the explicit finite counterexample is directly checkable
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Independent Verifiers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic certificate replay using only a published proof-format semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an exactly encoded MIP instance \(P\), a certificate stream \(C=(r_1,\ldots,r_m)\), and a public rule specification \(\mathcal R\). Initialize state \(S_0\) from \(P\). For \(t=1,\ldots,m\), parse \(r_t\), reject if its references are unavailable, check its side conditions by exact arithmetic under \(\mathcal R\), and set \(S_t=U(S_{t-1},r_t)\) only after acceptance. Accept only if the final state contains the claimed conclusion and every transformation needed to interpret that conclusion in the original model has been verified. The procedure uses no private solver state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver-independent verifier exactly replays a public certificate format and accepts only a derived original-model conclusion.
assumptions_latex: The instance, certificate, and rule semantics have unambiguous canonical encodings.
Arithmetic operations required by \(\mathcal R\) are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance implies that the claimed conclusion is derivable from \(P\) under \(\mathcal R\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: deterministic replay under public semantics defines solver independence
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the solver-independent verifier topic, but its public rule semantics, state transitions, and original-model interpretation requirements need an inspectable proof-format or verifier specification.

children.title: Certificate Compression Formats
children.top_down_role: Covers compact encodings for repeated derivations, references, coefficients, and proof structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Compression Formats
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lossless encodings of logical certificate records with explicit decoding semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=(r_1,\ldots,r_m)\) be a logical certificate over record alphabet \(\Sigma\). A lossless certificate compression format consists of an encoder \(E\), decoder \(D\), framing rule, and canonical dictionary semantics such that \[D(E(C))=C\qquad\text{for every valid finite }C\in\Sigma^*.\] References, repeated coefficients, and rule templates may be replaced by dictionary indices or deltas only when decoding uniquely restores their exact values and order. Verification is semantically sound when it is performed on \(D(z)\), or directly on \(z\) by a procedure proven equivalent to verification of \(D(z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compression format is lossless when decoding uniquely restores every certificate record, value, reference, and ordering.
assumptions_latex: Record values and dictionary entries have canonical exact encodings.
Malformed or ambiguous compressed strings are rejected.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact round-trip decoding is the basic lossless-format condition
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Streaming Certificate Transport
children.top_down_role: Covers incremental certificate delivery when full proof material is not retained in memory.

knowledge_statements.title: Streaming Certificate Transport
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered transport and verification without materializing the entire certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a framed compressed stream \(z=z_1\cdots z_q\), an initial decoder state \(d_0\), and verifier state \(S_0\). For each chunk \(z_j\) in sequence, validate its frame, update the decoder, and emit every complete logical record in order. For each emitted record \(r_t\), check it against the current verifier state and update \(S_t=U(S_{t-1},r_t)\); retain any incomplete suffix in the decoder state. After the final chunk, accept only if decoding ends at a record boundary, no frame or record was rejected, and the terminal verifier state contains the claimed conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Chunks are decoded in order, and complete records are verified immediately while incomplete suffixes remain buffered.
assumptions_latex: Chunk ordering and framing are unambiguous.
The streaming decoder emits exactly the records produced by whole-stream decoding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance equals verification of the fully decoded stream \(D(z)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: stateful in-order decoding gives the canonical streaming realization of a framed lossless format
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is coherent, but its equivalence to whole-stream decoding depends on framing and decoder semantics for which no inspectable source or formal specification is supplied.

children.title: Incremental Verification State
children.top_down_role: Covers verifier state retained across certificate segments and reference boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Verification State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal persistent state sufficient to check the next streamed deduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a deterministic verifier with update function \(U\), an incremental verification state after prefix \(C_t=(r_1,\ldots,r_t)\) is a finite object \(S_t\) satisfying \[S_0=I(P),\qquad S_t=U(S_{t-1},r_t).\] It contains the active model, established facts, live identifiers, provenance needed for future references, decoder residue, and rejection status. It is sufficient when any two accepted prefixes producing the same \(S_t\) have identical acceptance behavior for every common continuation \(Q\): appending \(Q\) to either prefix yields the same final verdict and claimed conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incremental state summarizes an accepted prefix sufficiently to determine verification of every future continuation.
assumptions_latex: Verification and state updates are deterministic.
All future record references resolve through information retained in the state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_t\) is a sufficient summary of \(C_t\) for continued verification.

notation.meaning: State after the first t records

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: continuation equivalence formalizes sufficiency of incremental verifier state
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Continuation equivalence is a precise sufficiency condition and the definition kind fits, but the proposed contents and finiteness of verifier state require a source tied to the intended streaming certificate calculus.

children.title: Compression–Verification Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Covers effects of compact representations on decoding cost, random access, auditability, and verifier memory.

knowledge_statements.title: Compression–Verification Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates transport size, decoding work, verification work, and live memory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let compressed data \(z\) decode to records \(C=(r_1,\ldots,r_m)\). Suppose streaming decoding costs \(T_D(z)\), checking record \(r_t\) costs \(T_V(r_t)\), and the maximum decoder-plus-verifier state occupies \(M(z)\) words. A single-pass implementation has total time \[O\!\left(T_D(z)+\sum_{t=1}^m T_V(r_t)\right)\] and working memory \(O(M(z))\), excluding the immutable input model and output. Compression reduces transport from \(|C|\) to \(|z|\), but it improves verification time only when reduced parsing or a directly verifiable compressed rule compensates for decoding overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Streaming verification adds decoding and record-checking costs while using only peak live state; smaller transport alone need not mean faster verification.
assumptions_latex: Each decoded record is emitted and checked once.
State operations are charged in the same word-RAM cost model.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the bound follows from additive single-pass accounting of decoding and checking operations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive single-pass accounting is plausible, but the complexity-bound container requires a source specifying the decoder, verifier operations, word-RAM model, and exclusions used by the bound.

children.title: Truncation Recovery Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Covers incomplete streams, damaged references, and restart limitations affecting certificate verification.

knowledge_statements.title: Truncation Recovery Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recovery boundary for prefix-truncated, compressed MIP certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\) be a certificate class, let \(E:\mathcal C\to\Sigma^*\) encode certificates, and let \(D:\mathcal C\to\mathcal S\) denote their verifier-relevant semantics. A truncation to \(k\) symbols is exactly recoverable when a map \(R_k:\Sigma^k\to\mathcal C\) satisfies \(D(R_k(\operatorname{pref}_k(E(C))))=D(C)\) for every \(C\in\mathcal C\). If certificates \(C_0,C_1\) satisfy \(\operatorname{pref}_k(E(C_0))=\operatorname{pref}_k(E(C_1))\) but \(D(C_0)\ne D(C_1)\), no such recovery map exists. Any sound verifier must then obtain additional data, reject the truncated stream, or restrict the admissible certificate class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated certificate is exactly recoverable only if its retained prefix uniquely determines all verifier-relevant semantics; colliding prefixes with different semantics make recovery impossible.
assumptions_latex: \(E:\mathcal C\to\Sigma^*\) is the fixed certificate encoding.
\(D(C)\) contains every fact used by verification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists C_0,C_1:\operatorname{pref}_k(E(C_0))=\operatorname{pref}_k(E(C_1))\land D(C_0)\ne D(C_1)\implies \nexists R_k\text{ giving exact recovery}.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The information-theoretic collision argument fits the failure-boundary leaf, but no source is cited. The formulation also must specify that every encoded certificate has length at least k, or define pref_k for shorter encodings, before the recovery map on Sigma^k is well-defined.

children.title: Certification Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Soundness, coverage, and proof-size boundaries for exact and machine-checkable certification.

knowledge_statements.title: Floating-Point Unsoundness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete mismatch between floating-point acceptance and exact rational feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a binary floating-point set containing \(1\), and let \(a<1\) be the greatest element of \(F\) below \(1\). Choose rational \(\varepsilon\) with \(0<\varepsilon<(1-a)/2\). Under round-to-nearest arithmetic, \(\operatorname{fl}(1-\varepsilon)=1\). The exact rational system \(x\ge 1\), \(x\le 1-\varepsilon\) is infeasible, but after independently rounding its upper bound, the floating-point system becomes \(x\ge1\), \(x\le1\), and accepts \(x=1\). Thus floating-point satisfaction alone is not a sound certificate of exact rational feasibility or infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rounding can turn an exactly infeasible pair of rational bounds into a feasible floating-point system, so floating-point checking alone is unsound.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) uses round-to-nearest and contains adjacent values \(a<1\).
\(0<\varepsilon<(1-a)/2\) is rational.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:x\ge1,\ x\le1-\varepsilon\}=\varnothing\), while \(x=1\) satisfies both rounded inequalities.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly shows that rounded floating-point satisfaction is not a sound certificate of exact rational feasibility, and the knowledge kind fits the leaf. It does not establish the separate claim about certifying infeasibility, and no source supports the certificate-verification interpretation.

children.title: Uncertified Model Transformations
children.top_down_role: Covers solver-side reformulations whose equivalence or provenance is absent from the certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertified Model Transformations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certification boundary when preprocessing transformations lack checked equivalence maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an original model \(P\) and transformed model \(T(P)\), a certificate for \(T(P)\) certifies the corresponding claim about \(P\) only when the checker verifies a claim-preserving transformation record, including any required lifting map. Without that record, validity need not transfer. For example, let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb Z:x\le0\}\), and let an erroneous transformation drop the inequality, producing \(T(P)=\mathbb Z\). The point \(x=1\) is a valid feasibility certificate for \(T(P)\) but is not feasible for \(P\). Therefore verification confined to the transformed model cannot establish original-model feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transformed-model certificate does not certify the original model unless the transformation and any solution-lifting map are themselves checked.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is the authoritative original model.
The verifier receives no checked equivalence or implication record for \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in T(P)\nRightarrow x\in P\); hence transformed-model validity alone does not certify original-model validity.

notation.meaning: Model produced from P by preprocessing or reformulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The example correctly demonstrates failure to transfer feasibility from an erroneously transformed model to the original model, and failure_boundary fits the container. An inspectable source on proof-producing presolve or checked transformation reconstruction is required.

children.title: Uncertified Callback Reasoning
children.top_down_role: Covers user-supplied cuts, lazy constraints, heuristics, or pruning decisions lacking checkable justification.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertified Callback Reasoning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by accepting callback-generated restrictions without validity checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider maximizing \(x\) over \(P=\{x\in\mathbb Z:0\le x\le1\}\), whose optimum is \(1\). Suppose an untrusted callback inserts the unsupported cut \(x\le0\). The resulting restricted problem has optimum \(0\), and a complete branch-and-bound certificate for that restricted problem may be internally valid. Nevertheless it does not certify the optimum of \(P\), because the callback cut excludes the feasible point \(x=1\). Consequently every callback assertion that can remove solutions or nodes must be independently checked for validity or represented by a supported derivation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unchecked callback cut can remove the true optimum, making an otherwise valid downstream search certificate irrelevant to the original MIP.
assumptions_latex: The callback may add constraints used for pruning.
The verifier does not validate the callback constraint against \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{x:x\in P\}=1\ne0=\max\{x:x\in P,\ x\le0\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unsupported-cut example is mathematically correct and counterexample is an appropriate knowledge kind. No citation is supplied for the broader requirement imposed on solution-removing callback assertions.

children.title: Transformation–Callback Interactions
children.top_down_role: Covers certification gaps caused when callback reasoning operates on transformed rather than original model state.

knowledge_statements.title: Transformation–Callback Interactions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-mapping failure between preprocessing and callback-generated constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let preprocessing substitute \(x=1-y\) with \(x,y\in\{0,1\}\). A callback constraint written in original coordinates must be transported by substitution before it is used in the transformed search. In particular, the constraint \(x\le0\) is equivalent to \(y\ge1\). If an interface instead applies the syntactically similar constraint \(y\le0\), it retains \(x=1\) and excludes \(x=0\), reversing the intended restriction. Thus separate correctness of a transformation and a callback is insufficient: the checker must also validate the coordinate map and the stage at which each callback assertion is interpreted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid callback constraint can become invalid when interpreted in transformed coordinates without a checked mapping and stage convention.
assumptions_latex: \(x,y\in\{0,1\}\) and preprocessing records \(x=1-y\).
The callback expression \(x\le0\) is intended in original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\le0\iff y\ge1\), whereas \(y\le0\iff x\ge1\); confusing the two reverses the restriction.

notation.meaning: Preprocessing substitution between original and transformed variables.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary substitution example correctly distinguishes the transported constraint y>=1 from the inequivalent constraint y<=0, and it fits the interaction leaf as a counterexample. A source specifying transformation-callback coordinate and stage semantics is absent.

children.title: Certificate Reconstruction Gaps
children.top_down_role: Covers missing provenance needed to relate solver-produced evidence back to the submitted instance.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Reconstruction Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-theoretic boundary for reconstructing omitted certificate events.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) range over full certificates, let \(S(C)\) be the retained event stream, and let \(V(C)\in\{0,1\}\) be exact verification. A deterministic reconstruction procedure \(R\) can preserve verification for every certificate only if \(V\) is constant on every fiber of \(S\). Indeed, if \(S(C_0)=S(C_1)\) while \(V(C_0)\ne V(C_1)\), then \(R\) receives identical input for both certificates and produces one reconstructed object, so it cannot reproduce both verification outcomes. Any omitted transformation, bound justification, or callback derivation creating such a collision is therefore a certificate reconstruction gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstruction is impossible when the retained stream is identical for two full certificates having different exact verification outcomes.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is the complete retained stream available to reconstruction.
\(R\) is deterministic and receives no external evidence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S(C_0)=S(C_1)\land V(C_0)\ne V(C_1)\implies \nexists R\text{ preserving }V\text{ on all certificates}.\)

notation.meaning: Retained stream derived from full certificate C.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fiber-collision argument fits the reconstruction-gap boundary, but no authoritative source is cited. A sourced formulation should also state the domain and codomain of S and R explicitly and express preservation as V(R(S(C)))=V(C).

children.title: Trusted-Code Boundary Expansion
children.top_down_role: Covers increases in the trusted computing base caused by unverifiable transformations or callback behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Trusted-Code Boundary Expansion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization of trust added by semantic operations delegated outside the checker.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a certificate checker and let \(U_1,\ldots,U_m\) be external components whose returned predicates \(Q_i(P,C)\) influence acceptance. If \(K\) neither recomputes \(Q_i\) nor checks a certificate implying \(Q_i\), soundness of the composite verifier requires assuming that \(U_i\) always reports \(Q_i\) correctly. Hence the trusted computing base is not merely \(K\): it includes every such \(U_i\), together with model transformations, callback handlers, numerical routines, or reconstruction procedures delegated to them. Moving an inference outside checked certificate semantics therefore expands, rather than eliminates, the trust boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every external component whose unchecked result affects acceptance becomes part of the trusted computing base.
assumptions_latex: Acceptance by \(K\) depends on at least one externally supplied predicate \(Q_i(P,C)\).
No checked derivation of that predicate is supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_i\text{ affects acceptance and is unchecked}\implies U_i\text{ belongs to the trusted computing base}.\)

notation.meaning: External component consulted by the checker.
Semantic predicate reported by component i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The trusted-computing-base characterization is appropriate as a property of this leaf, but it has no source. The domains and quantification of P and C, and the precise acceptance dependence on each Q_i, also require specification in a sourced version.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Size Explosion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary defined by superpolynomial minimum certificate length.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a proof system \(\Pi\) and a binary encoding of MIP instances. For an instance \(I\), define \(s_\Pi(I)\) as the minimum bit length of any \(\Pi\)-certificate accepted for the claimed conclusion. If a family \((I_n)\) has input length \(|I_n|\le n^c\) and satisfies \(s_\Pi(I_n)\ge2^{\alpha n}\) for constants \(c,\alpha>0\), then every complete certificate generator and every lossless certificate transport for \(\Pi\) must emit or communicate at least \(2^{\alpha n}\) bits on that family. Polynomial-time verification per certificate symbol does not remove this output-size lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the shortest certificates for a polynomial-size instance family are exponential, every complete generator or lossless transport must incur exponential output size.
assumptions_latex: \(\Pi\) and the instance encoding are fixed.
\(|I_n|\le n^c\) and \(s_\Pi(I_n)\ge2^{\alpha n}\) for fixed \(c,\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{output}_\Pi(I_n)\ge s_\Pi(I_n)\ge2^{\alpha n}\) bits.

notation.meaning: Shortest accepted certificate length for instance I in proof system Pi.
Binary input length of instance I.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The output-length implication is correct conditional on the stated certificate lower bound, and complexity_bound fits the leaf. However, it supplies no source or explicit MIP family satisfying that lower bound, so it does not substantiate the asserted certificate-size-explosion phenomenon beyond a conditional consequence.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsupported Solver Reasoning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between solver inferences and the checker’s formal proof language.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\) be a certificate language with checker \(V_L\), and let a solver prune a search state using an assertion \(q\). If no accepted \(L\)-derivation establishes \(q\), and the remaining certificate omits the pruned state, then acceptance of that remaining transcript cannot by itself certify completeness of the original search. Sound certification requires either encoding a derivation of \(q\), replacing the step by supported inferences, or independently checking the omitted state. Merely recording that the solver executed an unsupported heuristic, propagator, symmetry rule, or numerical test records provenance but supplies no machine-checkable justification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pruning step outside the checker’s proof language leaves search completeness uncertified unless its claim or the omitted state is independently checked.
assumptions_latex: \(V_L\) recognizes only derivations expressible in \(L\).
The assertion \(q\) is used to omit a search state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q\text{ has no accepted }L\text{-derivation}\implies\text{the pruning step is not certified by }V_L.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement accurately identifies the boundary between a solver inference and the checker's supported proof language, and failure_boundary is the correct role. No inspectable source on formal proof logging and completeness-preserving pruning is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Certificate Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of convex linearization certificates for a nonconvex constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a differentiable convex function \(g\), the tangent inequality \(g(z)+\nabla g(z)^{\mathsf T}(x-z)\le0\) is a valid relaxation of \(g(x)\le0\). This rule fails without convexity. Take \(g(x)=1-x^2\), whose feasible set is \(\{x:|x|\ge1\}\). At \(z=0\), the tangent inequality is \(1\le0\), which is inconsistent and would falsely certify infeasibility although \(x=1\) and \(x=-1\) are feasible. Thus certificate systems based on convex supporting inequalities cannot soundly cover general nonlinear constraints unless curvature assumptions or alternative globally valid derivations are checked.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tangent cut can falsely prove infeasibility for a nonconvex constraint, so convex linearization certificates require checked curvature assumptions.
assumptions_latex: The certificate rule treats a tangent inequality as globally valid.
No convexity certificate for \(g\) is checked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(x)=1-x^2\le0\) is feasible, but its tangent inequality at \(0\) is the contradiction \(1\le0\).

source_refs.locator: 1.1 Classification of Nonlinear Integer Programming Formulations p. 2

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 Classification of Nonlinear Integer Programming Formulations p. 2

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convex tangent-relaxation statement and the nonconvex counterexample are mathematically correct, and counterexample fits this boundary leaf. The cited classification section does not specifically support the tangent rule, its convexity hypothesis, or the stated counterexample; a precise section, theorem, or page is required.
